How this works. This file is the map, not a second copy of anything (Leanness Law: one home per fact, pointers over copies). Every link below goes to the file that actually holds that canon. If two things ever disagree, the newest dated entry wins and the older one gets fixed.

Where canon lives. The Series Bible is the spine. Character profiles hold per-character detail. This wiki is how you find either without reading a thousand lines.

Browsable version: "The Danim Codex". The Rules

Full set in the workspace CLAUDE.mdrepo. The ones that bite most often:

  • No em dashes. Anywhere, ever, workspace-wide.
  • The Kegare layer is NEVER explained in-series. Creator's Easter egg only.
  • Never write a lucky escape for Kevin missing the water. He was not born. That is enough.
  • Every Kūga joke is a live will-test. He is never only joking.
  • Staging is never invented in the Reading Edition. It goes into the script first and propagates down.
  • Never describe voodoo with Aura's vocabulary. Cold, void, silence.
  • New lore gets drafted in the Book's voice, as a page, because the Book is to exist in real life.

Hood Ninjaz is an action-packed adult comedy anime series set in Danim City, a fictional UK city inspired by London.

Contents
  1. Core Pillars
  2. THE EXTREMITY CALIBRATION (locked 2026-08-10, Bupe)
  3. Target Audience

Hood Ninjaz is an action-packed adult comedy anime series set in Danim City, a fictional UK city inspired by London. The series fuses British urban grime and drill culture with a hidden ninja underground, following a new generation of young warriors discovering their powers in a world that doesn't know they exist.

The show blends real-life social commentary with supernatural ninja combat, accents ranging from the Queen's tongue to roadman dialect, and a soundtrack driven by drill, grime, and trap music. It is Naruto meets Top Boy meets The Boondocks, with the unflinching consequences of Invincible.

Core Pillars

1. It's British. Red buses, underground trains, Caribbean and African heritage families, council estates, corner shops, chicken shops, cockney police, road slang. The Queen's English sits next to "what you saying fam." That contrast IS the comedy and the culture.

2. It Doesn't Hold Back. People you love can die. When someone gets cut, they bleed. Relationships involve sex and it's shown honestly. Characters swear like real people. The police are corrupt and prejudiced. The system is broken. This is 15-18 rated. Invincible-level intensity, not gore for gore's sake.

3. Comedy Is Essential. Sleeze interrupting Face's speech to ask about getting paid. Ninjas debating Skepta vs Wiley in the back of a lorry. Face's mum bursting in screaming about his room. The comedy isn't filler. It's what makes the dark moments hit harder. When you're laughing one minute and someone dies the next, that's when the audience says "this show doesn't hold back."

4. Music Is a Character. Every character has theme music. Face's theme is bass-heavy and vicious. Fights are choreographed to music. Drill beats during action, trap during tension, something softer during emotional moments. The soundtrack drives the energy of every scene.

5. Fights Are the Main Event. This is a show about ninjas. Fights are intelligent, strategic, and escalating. Not just punching. Reading opponents, setting traps, using the environment. Early fights are grounded and tactical. By the finale, full anime-level with visible auras clashing.

6. Shock Value Through Reality. The shock comes from things that feel REAL. A father not knowing his son exists. A detective unknowingly helping build weapons that will destroy the people she's investigating. A kid eating an ancient evil thinking it's a sweet. The shock comes from "I can't believe that just happened," not "I can't believe they showed that."

7. Cultural Representation. Jamaican grandad, African mum, mixed heritage families, British-Japanese ninja lore, the Caribbean and African diaspora in the UK. The racial and cultural mix isn't tokenism. It's the world these characters actually live in.

THE EXTREMITY CALIBRATION (locked 2026-08-10, Bupe)

Taking extremity right to the edge is a Hood Ninjaz signature, not a risk to be managed. This is the house setting and it applies to every episode, not just the scenes people flinch at.

  • Sex: toward softcore, never hardcore, never explicit. The edge is where it lives.
  • Violence: you feel every violent act. Not a bloody gore mess. Explicitly not Chainsaw Man. It sits between Attack on Titan and Mortal Kombat: weight, consequence and impact, not spectacle-splatter.

How this reads against the Seven Pillars. The pillar bans gore and sex for shock value alone, which is a different thing from banning intensity. Intensity with purpose is the brand. The test is never "is this too much", it is "is this doing work". A scene that earns its extremity keeps it.

Worked example: Sera's ritual (Characters/Sera/Sera.md). It is the conception of a main character and the moment a person becomes a monster, so it does work and it stays intense. Play it at full weight.

Target Audience

Ages 15-18+. The demographic that drives the highest engagement globally. They want shocking, real, uncensored storytelling that doesn't talk down to them. Every episode should leave the audience saying: "This show doesn't hold back and it's very real."

Danim City is a fictional UK city inspired by London but with its own unique geography and landmarks.

Contents
  1. Key Landmarks
  2. City Districts
  3. The Ninja Code
  4. Political Backdrop: Dexit
  5. In-World Popular Culture
  6. JENNY (the street drug). Named by Bupe 2026-08-27.

Danim City is a fictional UK city inspired by London but with its own unique geography and landmarks. Like Gotham to New York or Wakanda to the real world, Danim City exists fictionally within the real United Kingdom. It has a striking resemblance to London (red double-decker buses, an underground train system, iconic landmarks) but it is its own place with its own identity.

People who live there just call it "Danim." Calling it "Danim City" is formal, tourist-talk.

Key Landmarks

  • Danim Bridge: iconic bridge mirroring London Bridge, a recognisable symbol of the city
  • The Pendulum: famous clock tower in Central Danim
  • Danim View: scenic viewpoint overlooking the city
  • The Underground: train system using triangular logos and "Clam cards" (like Oyster cards)

City Districts

Central Danim. The heart of the city. Danim Bridge, The Pendulum, main high streets, the underground hub, government buildings, news studios. Most public area with the most cameras. Ninja fights here are rare and always make the news. The Episode 1 fight between Jaden and Spike causes destruction here, kicking off the entire plot.

South Danim. The hood. Council estates, chicken shops, barbershops. Face's crew operates across South Danim. Sleeze and his boys are from here. This is where most ninja activity happens because it's less policed and people mind their business. Top Boy energy.

Jon's Barbershop (Border of Central/South). Uncle Jon's Barbershop sits on quiet back streets right on the border where Central Danim meets South Danim. Technically South but only just past Central. Not deep in Face's territory. One bus ride from North Danim. Kevin's mum has been bringing him here since he was young.

North Danim. Kevin's home. Wood Green, Edmonton, Tottenham energy. Multicultural, Caribbean and African families, busy high streets, market stalls. Not soft but not a warzone. Kevin's mum and grandad live here. Kevin's school is here. This is his safe world before he crosses into the ninja world every time he visits Jon.

East Danim. Industrial, forgotten, rough. Abandoned warehouses, old factories, the river. Donte's foster home was here. Donte and Uno's warehouse hideout is here. The underground tunnels run deepest beneath East Danim, where ancient secrets are buried.

West Danim. The gentrified bubble. Trendy cafes, yoga studios, artisan bakeries, young professionals completely oblivious to what's happening in the rest of the city. Provides comedy and tonal contrast. Characters from other areas react to West Danim like "what planet are these people on."

Belvedire (Outskirts). Wealthy, gated, separate from Danim City proper. Paul Mitchell's estate is here. Connected to Danim by motorway but feels like a different world, like Milton Keynes to London. Hella grew up here. Tammy still lives here.

The Underground. Beneath everything. The public train system that everyone uses, but also ancient tunnels, plague pits, and forgotten chambers older than the city itself. The deeper you go, the older the secrets. This is where ninja history is buried, literally.

The Ninja Code

When a ninja's powers awaken, they instinctually know the number one rule: the general public must never find out ninjas exist. Good or bad, every ninja follows this code because exposure means everyone is at risk. The public sees "gang violence" or "unexplained incidents." Police file it as criminal activity because they have no other explanation. Some reckless ninjas go off track, and these incidents create the rumours and urban legends that characters like Sharon investigate.

Political Backdrop: Dexit

Dexit is a political event mirroring Brexit. A divisive national decision that creates instability, economic uncertainty, and a power vacuum. Face sees Dexit as the perfect "blind spot" to execute his plans while the government and public are distracted.

In-World Popular Culture

Danim has its own comics, its own boxing, its own everything, and the audience meets that world the way a thirteen-year-old does.

Perfect. The superhero Kevin grew up on, and his favourite. Load-bearing rather than decorative: Perfect is the answer to Grandad's question about why anyone would protect a stranger. "Why would Perfect save you if he doesn't even know you?" "Because... he's a hero." That exchange is the seed of Kevin's entire moral position, planted years before he has any power to act on it. (Locked 2026-08-13, Bupe's call. The final tier of TANC was renamed Apex to clear the name; nothing else in the world may reuse "Perfect" as a proper noun.)

Andy Jaxson. In-world boxer, the one Grandad argues about. Grandad rates him over "that wild swinging Tyson". Kevin shortens him to AJ.

JENNY (the street drug). Named by Bupe 2026-08-27.

What the street calls it: Jenny. "Got a fresh batch of Jenny." Where the name actually comes from: Gen, as in Bio Genetix, and nobody on the street knows that. It arrived in Danim roughly nine to thirteen years before the present day, which places it in Sharon's party years and near the Loyalty Elixir era.

The whole device is the gap between what the users think they are taking and what it is. Dealers, users and half the police treat Jenny as one more street drug with a girl's name. The audience is given the name early, casually, in a smoking area, and only much later has any reason to hear "Gen" in it.

Sharon took it once and it did nothing to her. She was disappointed, never tried it again, and never wondered why it did not work. Open question flagged to Bupe: her profile carries "possibly water-exposed as a child but never trained", so whether Jenny failing on her is a plant or a coincidence is undecided.

The Energy Source

All ninja power in Hood Ninjaz is fuelled by Aura, an internal energy that exists within every person but remains dormant in most. Aura is invisible at lower levels but becomes increasingly visible as a ninja's power grows, eventually manifesting as coloured energy that can be seen and felt.

The Three Pillars

The ancient ninja teachings (contained in the Book) state that Aura is mastered through three interconnected pillars:

1. Mind. Mental discipline and focus. Unlocks psychic abilities such as telekinesis, memory alteration, illusion casting. Face's blade telekinesis and Manic's memory manipulation come from Mind mastery.

2. Body. Physical training that enhances the body beyond normal human capabilities. Super strength, speed, reflexes, endurance. Jon's blade precision and fighting discipline come from Body mastery.

3. Spirit. Mastering inner energy allows control over elemental forces or pure energy projection. Eve's shadow snakes and Donte's fire manipulation come from Spirit.

A ninja must find balance between these pillars, or risk their powers turning against them. Overreliance on one pillar at the expense of others leads to instability.

The Five Tiers

Tier 1: Dormant. Everyone has Aura but most never awaken it. Regular civilians. Kevin starts here. No visibility, no sensing, just untapped potential.

Tier 2: Awakened. Aura unlocked through training, trauma, or bloodline activation. Faster, stronger, sharper than any normal human. Heightened senses. Most of Face's rank-and-file crew sits here. Fights look like elite martial arts with superhuman speed. No visible aura yet, but trained ninjas can sense each other's presence.

Tier 3: Channelled. Aura can be actively pushed into the body or weapons. Enhanced strikes that crack walls, blade control, wall clinging, short bursts of invisibility. Subtle visual manifestation begins (heat distortion, faint shimmer). Hella and Eve operate at this tier. Unique Aura abilities manifest here.

Tier 4: Radiant. Aura becomes fully visible. Coloured auras manifest: Face's black smoke, Jon's blue calm, Jaden's gold warmth. Can project Aura outward: pressure that freezes weaker ninjas, shockwaves from strikes, object control at range. The Mandem in their prime all operated at Tier 4.

Tier 5: Transcendent. Near god-tier. The Mandem's combined ultimate technique lives here. Aura becomes a force of nature: the sky darkens, the ground cracks, the environment reacts. Only reached through extreme emotional connection or by those who carry the Hakai Sphere itself. The Apex TANCs are designed to match this level.

The Growth Ladder (added 2026-08-10)

Aura growth is not one curve. Where a ninja sits on the ladder is the real measure of them, and it is the language the series uses to make scale legible without ever printing a power level.

  • Ordinary ninjas grow by addition. Train, add a bit.
  • The elite grow by multiplication. Each gain compounds the last.
  • The Mandem grow exponentially. They had the water and the Book, and the Book is what turns multiplication into an exponent.
  • Kūga is a different operation entirely: tetration. See section 4.

Nobody in-world says these words. It is the shape the writing holds to.

Kevin's Unique Power: The Power of Will (added 2026-08-10)

Every other ninja in the series is judged on roughly the same scale: how much Aura, which pillar, which tier. Kevin is the one exception, and his exception is not a bigger number. It is a different kind of power.

Kevin's power is the Power of Will. What he genuinely wants, happens. Not because his will is stronger than anyone else's, but because his is the only will in the world wired to an amplifier. Full mechanics, the asymmetry that governs it, and the rules of engagement between Kevin and Kūga are in section 4.

The One Power Outside The System: Voodoo (locked 2026-08-10)

Every power in the series descends from Kega or Kūga. Aura is Kūga's leak. The Book is Kega's prison. Trace is the Second Seal's provision. TANCs are Bio Genetix failing to copy Aura. Uno is Springvale plus a doctor's blood.

Voodoo is the single exception, and there is a reason rather than a hand-wave.

Every voodoo ability is death-side: resurrection, phantoms, spirit manipulation, soul binding, soul capture, life drain. Not one touches a living system. And the gods only ever legislated for the living: Kega set the order of life, Kūga amplifies the living, Aura is life energy in living bodies, the Book is the law of the living.

So voodoo is the door the gods never legislated, because they never legislated for the dead.

SENSORY RULE. Aura is heat, light and crackle in a living body. Voodoo is the exact inverse: cold instead of hot, void instead of light, heavy silence instead of energy. Where Aura fills a room, voodoo empties it. Never describe voodoo with Aura's vocabulary.

Its source is mundane on purpose. Sera found the degraded remains of something real, in books, in Danim, while looking for a love spell (Characters/Sera/Sera.md). Nothing divine gave it to her. Anyone could have found it. The mythology is 6,000 years old and the thing that eventually cracks it is a nineteen-year-old girl who was ignored.

What being outside the order buys the only two beings who are: Tribal and Kūga. Trace has no authority over Tribal because the Second Seal is a covenant among the living. Kega has no jurisdiction over him either, which is why a god of judgment stops to ask a human a calm question instead of purging him: Tribal is the first being in 6,000 years he has no verdict for. Full detail in Characters/Tribal/Tribal.md.

Consequences of Overuse

  • Body Deterioration: physical powers take a toll, causing accelerated aging or pain
  • Mental Breakdown: psychic abilities risk the user's sanity if pushed too far
  • Loss of Control: unbalanced spirit leads to unintended destruction or powers turning against the user

Aura Visibility Progression

Aura starts completely invisible in the early series. As power levels increase across seasons, Aura becomes more visible: from subtle shimmer, to coloured wisps, to full anime-level energy displays by the finale. The audience grows with the power system.

Everything in this subsection is what history believes.

Everything in this subsection is what history believes. Most of it is wrong. It is what the characters know and what the audience is told first.

In ancient Japan, a force of pure destruction existed: Hakai. Not a demon, not a god. Destruction itself given consciousness. Hakai could destroy on a planetary scale. It was intelligent, patient, and cruel. It enjoyed watching civilisations build themselves up just to tear them down.

When it became clear Hakai couldn't be killed, ten warriors came together: the 5 highest Shinobi and 5 secret Ninja from rival clans who had been sworn enemies for generations. Together they created the Sphere and sealed Hakai inside it at the cost of all ten of their lives. Their life force became the prison walls. The warriors who buried the Sphere then took their own lives so the location would die with them.

Three things the record gets wrong, and the reason it gets each one wrong.

Three things the record gets wrong, and the reason it gets each one wrong.

1. It was never Japan. The events predate Japan by thousands of years. Japan is where the story was eventually recorded and where the Sphere was eventually buried, so that is where history thinks it happened. Japan inherited the myth, it did not originate it. This is also why the route from there to Danim City is a deliberate grey area: none of it was ever Japan-exclusive.

2. They were not warriors. They were gods. Kega was the head of a pantheon, ten gods answering to him, each with their own village (a couple of them sharing one). The record calls them "the 5 highest Shinobi and 5 secret Ninja" because the people who eventually wrote it down were shinobi, and they retro-fitted their own vocabulary onto beings who predated the word by millennia. The clans later claimed them as ancestors. Both halves of that record are wrong and both are believed absolutely.

3. "Sworn enemies for generations" is true, but it is the consequence, not the starting condition. The ten were united once. Their feud came later, and it passed down into their villages, which became the clans. The clans inherited a hatred that began as a disagreement between gods about what a law meant.

Total span from the Severing to present day: 6,000 years.

Total span from the Severing to present day: 6,000 years.

EventYears before present
THE SEVERING. Kega amputates. Weak for months. Kūga wakes naked in the bushes. The village, the kindness, the raid, the slave chain.6,000
THE FIRST SEAL. The ten seal Kega into the Book. Done in arrogance. Relief for months, then the collapse.5,500
THE SECOND SEAL. The ten seal Kūga into the Sphere. Done in humility. Sacrifice seal: all ten die. The age of gods ends here.4,000
The Sphere buried, the buriers take their own lives, the location dies with them. Millennia pass; fragments survive in scattered texts. Bio Genetix tracks it, the keeper steals it, the chain moves it west.4,000 to 22
The Sphere reaches Danim City. Springvale contamination begins.22

The ratios that matter:

  • Kūga was free for 2,000 years and sealed for 4,000. Twice as long in the seal as in the world, which is why the will of ten gods remains the dominant thing he has ever absorbed.
  • Kega has been in the Book for 5,500 years. And has been right for 5,500 years.
  • Kūga's 2,000 free years cover the entire rise of human civilisation. He did not watch history. He was passed through it.

Free consequence: the Book is older than writing. Human script begins roughly 5,200 years ago. The Book is 5,500 years old, so it is not written in any human language. This is why Tribal is the only person alive who can read the deep chapter: the Book is not encrypted, it is simply older than the concept of reading.

THE SEVERING: Why and How (locked 2026-08-10)

ID
Bible s4.4

4. THE HAKAI SPHERE, KŪGA, AND THE POWER OF WILL
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Why. For a long time Kega set law and knew exactly why each law existed.

Why. For a long time Kega set law and knew exactly why each law existed. Then experience accumulated, and the accumulation clouded him. The laws began contradicting each other and going against the orders of life. He traced the fault to its source: the half of himself that takes in the world.

The name is the tragedy. He amputated himself to stop being defiled, and he is named 穢我, the defiled self. Kegare is not moral sin; it is accumulated heaviness, contamination that builds whether or not anyone did wrong. That is a precise description of what happened to his judgement. He cut away his ability to change in order to escape defilement, and the cutting is what defiled him permanently. Never explained in-series (see section 9).

How, and why it took years. His only tool is the verdict, and a verdict requires the whole self: judgment to pass sentence, and the thing sentenced ruled broken. For years he tried every way around it and failed.

What finally worked was the one thing he had never been able to do: rule himself the defect. The day he genuinely believed he was the broken thing was the day it became possible. Self-condemnation. It cost enormous power and left him weak for months.

So the last honest verdict he ever passed was against himself. Every judgement since has come from something with no way to check its own work.

Purging is not killing, it is removal from the order. The severed half was not destroyed, it was cast out. Which is why it survived with nothing: no nature, no judgment, no place. And it is why Kūga sits outside the order entirely, which is why the sacred balance has no grip on him and why he could sit in a water tank and contaminate a generation.

Visually: no cut, no wound, no blood. He passes the verdict and part of him simply stops being included. It falls out of him the way a name falls off a list.

WHAT IS LEFT BEHIND (locked 2026-08-10). Abstract. A presence, not a body.

Kega finishes the ritual and leaves. The camera stays. In the empty air where it happened, something begins to gather. Not a figure, not a shape, just a presence starting to come together.

We never see it materialise. The scene ends before it becomes anything. He has no form yet because he has no nature yet, and form is something he only acquires from exposure. By the time the villager finds him in the bushes he has taken shape, and the audience is left to understand that the gap between those two moments is where a body came from.

Do not explain the gap. Do not show the transition. The cut is the point.

In order, and this is the entire explanation of what he became:

In order, and this is the entire explanation of what he became:

  1. A village man finds a naked frail man lying in the bushes and, for no reason at all, helps him up, bathes him, clothes him and takes him in.
  2. The village is attacked. People are taken as slaves. Frail, weak Kūga is one of them.

He has no nature. He becomes what he is exposed to. The kindness lasted days. The violence lasted centuries. That is why he became "destruction," and it is a life rather than a rule.

THE LOAD-BEARING CONSEQUENCE. The first thing that ever happened to Kūga was a stranger being good to him for nothing. It is the oldest thing in him, buried under two thousand years of the other and four thousand years of the seal. So when a barbershop, a mother, a grandad and three kids from North Danim get amplified in Season 3, that is not a new input. It is the first one. He met it once, and it was too brief to take.

Growth curve: flat then vertical. Tetration is almost flat for a very long time. He spends centuries as a nobody passed from hand to hand, unremarkable, absorbing, and the horror is that nothing appears to be happening. The last hundred years before the Second Seal are the vertical climb.

Kega did not even finish the job.

Kega did not even finish the job. Destruction would have been mercy. What Kūga got was being discarded while still conscious, into a world of men, with nothing. Cast out like a wild dog. Scraped off like something on the tip of a boot. The injury is not that Kega tried to kill him. It is that Kega could not be bothered to.

The accusation, and he is entitled to it: "You made me this. Not the world. You put me in the world."

He feels the connection, and it helps nothing. It explains nothing and comforts nothing. It sits there being true, like being related to someone you despise. He would rather it were not there and it will not go. It angers and frustrates him rather than answering anything.

PERFORMANCE NOTE: calculatedly irritated, never emotional. He gets more precise when he is angry, not louder. The register never rises. Anger shows as exactness. This sits on the bored refined English in the voice section and means the scene most performers would play big gets played cold.

Why the two-seal irony is his line. The gods who threw Kega away then had to die to contain the thing Kega threw away. Kūga took revenge on Kega's behalf and his own, by accident, without ever intending it, and every one of them knew what they were paying at the end. It is the one thing that genuinely amuses him.

"The first seal was done by beings who thought they knew better. The second by the same beings, once they had learned they did not." A short laugh. "The irony is absolute poetry."

The Name, and Why It Is Wrong (added 2026-08-10)

ID

4. THE HAKAI SPHERE, KŪGA, AND THE POWER OF WILL
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

破壊 (hakai) is ordinary modern Japanese for destruction or demolition.

破壊 (hakai) is ordinary modern Japanese for destruction or demolition. 破 = break, tear, rupture. 壊 = destroy, collapse, ruin. Everyday word, not mystical: 破壊力 (destructive power), 環境破壊 (environmental destruction). Pronounced ha-ka-i, three even beats.

The homophone worth knowing: 破戒 is also read hakai and means the breaking of a religious vow, specifically the Buddhist monastic precepts. Ten warriors from rival clans broke generations of sworn enmity to seal it, and then took their own lives. The second reading sits on top of the story for free. Never explained in-series.

CANON: "Hakai" is a misnomer. The name was bestowed at the sealing. It is what ten frightened men called the thing based on the only behaviour they had ever seen from it. They were describing a symptom and mistaking it for a species. The name is wrong, it stays in every script, and the audience does not learn it is wrong until the true name surfaces (Season 1 ending, see below).

What It Actually Is: Kūga (added 2026-08-10)

Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

空我 KŪGA. "The empty self." 空 is Buddhist emptiness (śūnyatā), the doctrine that nothing has inherent self-nature and everything takes its form from conditions.

空我 KŪGA. "The empty self." 空 is Buddhist emptiness (śūnyatā), the doctrine that nothing has inherent self-nature and everything takes its form from conditions. 我 is self, I, ego.

Its power is not destruction. Its power is amplification. Kūga has no nature and no power of its own. It is not a value, it is an operator. It takes whatever it is exposed to and raises it. This is why it appeared to be destruction for a thousand years: destruction was what it was fed.

Scale: tetration. Addition, multiplication, exponentiation, then tetration, each the repetition of the one before. Tetration is iterated exponentiation and it produces numbers that cannot be written down. 3↑↑4 has roughly 3.6 trillion digits. There is not enough matter to print it on.

How the series conveys this: never state the number. The number genuinely cannot be expressed, and that is the point. Show someone try and fail. Bio Genetix has instruments and a scale; when they finally get a reading off Kevin the problem is not that the meter maxes out, it is that their notation cannot hold it. "It is not a big number. Our system has no way to write what it is."

The audience's ruler is already on screen. Everything they have loved for three seasons, Face's black smoke, Jon's blue, Jaden's gold, three men at Tier 4 and their combined ultimate technique, was made by diluted runoff. One line of dialogue recontextualises the whole series.

The Five Stages of Kūga's Power (added 2026-08-10)

ID
Bible s4.9
Details
Part of
4. THE HAKAI SPHERE, KŪGA, AND THE POWER OF WILL
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Stage 0. The split. Severed from Kega (section 9) with no nature and no power.

Stage 0. The split. Severed from Kega (section 9) with no nature and no power. An operator with nothing plugged in. Silent, and worth nothing.

Stage 1. The world. Exposed to ancient Japan: war, slaughter, corruption. It amplified what it saw. The output was annihilation, so humans named the output. This is where 破壊 comes from.

Stage 2. The seal. Ten of the strongest people alive died to contain it. Not to beat it. To contain it. That is the series' fixed measuring point.

Stage 3. The millennium. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. The prison walls are made of ten warriors' life force. So for over a thousand years the only input Kūga had was the will of ten people who chose to die rather than let it out. It amplified that. Every day. For a thousand years.

Consequences, all of them structural:

  • Kūga is about will because will is all it has eaten for a millennium. The Power of Will comes from the seal itself.
  • The ten warriors did not only fail to kill it. They fed it, and what they fed it was the finest thing humans have.
  • The exponent became tetration during those thousand years of iterating on the purest possible input.
  • It learned will. It never learned love. Ten people willing themselves to die is conviction, not connection. The Final Twist below is not a character trait, it is a dietary fact: Kevin beats it by feeding it the one human thing that was never in the cell.

Stage 4. The leak. A trace, diluted, into a school water tank for two years. That runoff made every ninja in Danim City.

Stage 5. Now. All of it, undiluted, in the gut of a thirteen-year-old.

The Power of Will: The Rules (added 2026-08-10)

ID
Bible s4.10
Details
Part of
4. THE HAKAI SPHERE, KŪGA, AND THE POWER OF WILL
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

The teachable rule: Kūga does not answer requests.

The teachable rule: Kūga does not answer requests. It answers declarations.

"Help me" contains doubt, so it dies in the air. "I will not let this happen" contains none, so it detonates. Kūga will not intervene for pain, fear or pleading, no matter how bad it gets. It intervenes only when Kevin ultimately, definitely and without a shred of doubt wants a thing to be otherwise, and genuinely believes it.

The asymmetry that drives Kevin's whole arc: harm is cheap, good is expensive.

Violence is Kūga's native register after stage 1, so a destructive thought is already in a language it speaks perfectly and needs almost no signal. Constructive will is a foreign language it only ever met as ten men holding a door shut, so Kevin has to be deafening, and any tremor of doubt and nothing happens at all.

Evil is a whisper. Good is a scream.

The intrusive-thought mechanic. Kūga can grow his nails and mime a throat-cut on someone only Kevin can see him touching. If Kevin so much as pictures it, the throat opens in reality. Kūga smiles: the will was too weak to refuse the thought. This is the elephant-in-a-bathroom problem weaponised, and it is genuinely unfair, which is the point.

Kūga's test pattern. He says "I could just [mischief]" to the ceiling, bored, unserious, never looking at Kevin. Then the corner-of-the-eye check. Then, in a voice with the temperature dropped out of it: "Oh. Interesting." Two words that mean I caught you.

WRITING RULE: every one of Kūga's jokes is a live test. He is never only joking. This is why the comedy and the horror run off one engine instead of fighting each other, and why the audience learns to tense at his jokes before Kevin does.

Kūga's thesis, never stated this plainly in dialogue: if you have the thought, and the heart to believe it, you will achieve it. He does not care about Kevin and only becomes interested at flashes of real will.

Kevin's training is subtractive, not additive. Most shonen training adds. Kevin's first year is damage control: he has to learn to think less before he can learn to think one thing completely. Clearing the mind is not zen decoration, it is survival.

Kevin grows without power creep. Kevin never gets stronger. Kūga never gets stronger. Neither number moves. The only variable is how much of it Kevin can hold without being rewritten. Season 1 he can hold a flicker and it nearly kills him. By Season 3 he can hold a decision. The ceiling was always infinite; the story is the boy widening.

Not a skill he learns. A property of what he carries.

Not a skill he learns. A property of what he carries.

An amplifier at rest emits nothing. Dormant, Kūga has no nature and therefore no signature. There is genuinely nothing to detect. What can be sensed is never Kūga existing, it is Kūga doing something.

  • Kevin is not hiding. There is nothing to find until he uses it.
  • His power is his beacon. Every time he reaches for it to save someone, he announces his position.
  • The strongest thing on earth stays safe only by staying weak, which is a perfect thirteen-year-old's dilemma.

The exception, and how Kega first senses him (Season 4): Kega flares. That flare passes through the city and Kūga answers involuntarily, two halves of one self resonating. Kevin did nothing and could not have stopped it. He gets the headache and the psychic distress at the exact instant Kega's arm is up mid-strike. His face is not "I need to hide." It is "who is that, and why did something in me just reach for them."

How It Reached Danim City

ID
Bible s4.12
Details
Part of
4. THE HAKAI SPHERE, KŪGA, AND THE POWER OF WILL
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Centuries later, fragments of the story survived in scattered texts.

Centuries later, fragments of the story survived in scattered texts. Bio Genetix, researching the science behind ninja abilities, discovered these fragments and began tracking the Sphere's last known location. A lone keeper, connected to the original guardians, stole it before Bio Genetix could reach it. He passed it through a network of people, each sacrificing themselves to keep it moving. The final person smuggled it to the UK, went undercover as a janitor at a school in Danim City, and hid the Book (the training manual) in the school library.

THE ROUTE IS A DELIBERATE GREY AREA (locked 2026-08-10). Where the Sphere travelled between ancient Japan and Danim City is never specified and must never be specified. Every place it rested near water long enough, it leaked. Danim City is not the first stop. It is the last one. This is the seed for a future US link-up: other cities, other contaminations, other hood ninjaz.

How the seed is planted, and it is planted silently. Bio Genetix have been tracking the Sphere for years, so they have a map. A wall or a screen with pins on it. Danim City is one pin. It is not the only pin. The camera holds one beat too long, then moves on. No dialogue, nobody comments, never mentioned again. If Hood Ninjaz runs long enough to need it, that map was always there. If it never gets used, nothing was ever claimed. Backup option only if an audible version is ever wanted, in Archer's voice: "It did not travel in a straight line. They never do."

The names (locked 2026-08-10). Two registers, as with everything in this world.

The names (locked 2026-08-10). Two registers, as with everything in this world.

  • SPRINGVALE. The brand. The water was bottled and sold into schools, so it had a label: a cheap, forgettable British bottled water that folded twenty years ago. This is what Danim calls it. "He's a Springvale kid." "You drank Springvale?" It doubles as an age marker, because if you are Springvale you are 27 to 37 and everybody knows it.
  • 濁り NIGORI. What the Book calls it. Cloudiness, turbidity, the impurity suspended in a liquid (a real word, used for unfiltered sake). The Book says the Nigori, Danim says Springvale, and nobody ever connects the two.

Why water, and only water. The seal is made of ten warriors' life force, and water is what life is mostly made of. It did not leak into the air, the soil or the stone. It leaked into the one substance in the building that resembled its own prison walls. (The purification rite for defilement by water is misogi. The medium of contamination and the medium of cleansing are the same substance. Nobody in the show ever says this.)

The timeline (locked 2026-08-10, tightened from the old "approximately 20-25 years"). The contamination ran 22 to 20 years before present day. Two years exactly.

Why it stopped, and why the keeper vanished. He hid the Sphere in the school water tank because it was the safest place he could think of: constantly moving, sealed, nobody looks in a school water tank. He did not know it would leak. Two years in he started noticing the children changing, understood what he had done, pulled the Sphere out and ran. That is why the contamination ended and why he "disappeared." The man who saved the world is also the man who accidentally created every ninja in Danim City.

Who it took, and the two different reasons for the two bounds. Thousands of children aged 5 to 15 were exposed. Dormant potential unlocked; without training, powers stayed inactive. Those who trained became ninjas, good or bad. Those who never trained stayed dormant.

  • The lower bound (5) is purely logistical. It was school water. The youngest children in a UK school are four or five. Nothing mystical about it.
  • The upper bound (15-16) is the real law: Kūga can only enter what is not finished yet. An adult has a settled self, fixed shape, hardened pathways, a person who already knows who they are. There is nothing there for a formless thing to take root in. A child is still forming, so the pathway is still open because the person is still open.

Nobody in-world knows these are two different reasons. They just say "kids."

This is the same law as the whole mythology, which is why it is not arbitrary biology. Kūga is the half that changes, so it can only enter what can still change. Kega amputated its own ability to change. Adults simply lose theirs by growing up.

And it makes the Ultimatum mechanical rather than poetic. "Master it by manhood or be consumed" is a real deadline: Kevin's window is closing because Kevin is finishing. When he is fully formed the shape sets, and either he set it or Kūga did.

A consequence of the locked timeline that shapes the entire cast.

A consequence of the locked timeline that shapes the entire cast.

Every ninja made by the water is now between 27 and 37 years old. One cohort, a single band, nobody older and nobody younger. Danim City's entire ninja population is one year group that drank the same water.

So the second generation can only get in through blood. Every kid ninja is the child of a water-generation ninja. Donte (Face and Hella). Kevin (the Young line; Jaden is Tier 4 gold). Uno is artificial (see Uno's profile). Tribal is outside the Aura system entirely.

Scale to hold to: a few dozen second-generation kids in Danim with the potential, of whom only a handful have actually woken up, because activation still needs the trigger (training, trauma, or bloodline activation). Enough for rival crews, a school thread and recruitment arcs. Never enough to break the Ninja Code.

Rejected alternatives, and why. A My Hero Academia model (powers common, society reorganised around them) is structurally incompatible: the moment there are enough kids for a school, the Ninja Code is dead and a locked pillar goes with it. A Miles Morales model (two or three peers, everyone else an adult) makes Danim feel small and leaves nowhere to grow.

What Lineage buys that neither does: every young character arrives with an adult attached. A parent, a secret, or an absence. "Whose kid are you?" becomes the most loaded question in the series, which is already Donte's entire arc.

The free ticking clock. One cohort had their children at roughly the same time, so the second generation is hitting the activation window simultaneously. Right now. A wave is cresting in Danim City, which is why the story happens this year and not any other, and why Bio Genetix, Face and Sharon are all about to notice the same thing from three different directions.

Correction of an earlier formulation.

Correction of an earlier formulation. "A prison, not a manual" was written for punch and it was wrong: the Book demonstrably teaches. It is both, and it is both for one reason.

The arts are Kega's. He taught them, he set the law around them, and the Book is that teaching written down: his complete works. You cannot imprison a god in a random object. You imprison him in the thing that is most completely him. The ten did not put Kega in a book, they put him in his own life's work, which is the only container that was ever going to hold him.

So "his own laws are the bars" is literal. The teaching is the material the walls are made of.

1. FORWARD: the teaching. The Book translates itself into the reader's own language.

1. FORWARD: the teaching. The Book translates itself into the reader's own language. Generous, complete, and it wants to teach you. The Three Pillars, the arts, the discipline. This is what the Mandem learned.

2. BACKWARD: the prohibition. Flip the Book over and read the other way and it stops translating. Raw god-language. This is the forbidden layer, the Loyalty Elixir and the rest.

Why it stops, and this is the key: the translation IS the permission. The Book renders what you are permitted to have and refuses to render what you are not. The language barrier is not a lock, it is a refusal. The Book is telling you to stop, in the only way a book can.

Why the forbidden things are in there at all: a complete law must name what it forbids. You cannot outlaw a technique without describing it. Every law book contains the crimes.

3. THE PAGE. Not a location, an event. It appears only when the forbidden ritual is performed, under the conditions of law, at the right moment in time. It is in the language of the gods and must be performed within a window. Performing it frees Kega from the seal.

The right moment is a STATE, not a date.

The right moment is a STATE, not a date. The moment is right when the seal has thinned enough, and what thins it is the violation list: the water, the Elixir, the TANCs, the necromancy, Kevin swallowing the Sphere.

So the whole cast set the clock. Sharon feeding intel she did not understand. Bio Genetix. Jaden. A thirteen-year-old eating a sweet. Tribal did not choose the hour. The world chose it, and he happened to be standing there holding the right chapter when it arrived.

The conditions of law, and the irony. Kega is procedure. The seal can only be undone by someone following his own legal formalities exactly, so the god of law can only be freed by someone obeying the rules perfectly in order to commit the most forbidden act there is. Tribal did everything correctly. That is why it worked.

The page is the receipt. The window is the mercy. The ritual plus conditions plus moment is the lock turning; the page appearing is the door already swinging. Which gives the beat: Tribal had a window in which he could have stopped, and did not, because the page arrived and he read it as the prize finally being handed to him. It was the last step of a release protocol and he thought it was a reward.

And the seal is maintained by correct practice. Every hour the arts are used as intended, the walls thicken. Every misuse thins them. Which means the Mandem, training the Three Pillars properly for years, were unknowingly the strongest part of the prison in four thousand years. Then Jaden read the same book and brewed the Elixir. He did not only betray his brothers. He was the seal, and he tore it from the inside, and he still does not know that is what he did.

The Book set no trap. It taught Tribal for years, generously and completely, and he reasonably expected more of the same when he turned it over. It taught him to trust it, and then he flipped it. That is not malice. That is what a complete law looks like from underneath.

Three names (locked 2026-08-10), in the usual pattern.

  • THE ORIGINAL BOOK OF NINJA. The formal name. What it is called by anyone who knows what it is.
  • THE BOOK OF KEGA. What it actually is, learned very late: the prison. It is also the manual, and that is precisely why it can be the prison (above).
  • "the Book." What everyone in Danim says. No change to existing usage anywhere.

JADEN FOUND IT (locked 2026-08-10). All three of the Mandem read it, but Jaden's hand touched it first during that detention. This is compatible with the existing "the Mandem found it" and strictly better, because Jaden is the one who later pulls the Loyalty Elixir out of it and uses it on his brothers. The finder becomes the betrayer.

It is 5,500 years old and older than writing (see the Timeline above), so it is not set down in any human language. It is not encrypted. It is simply older than the concept of reading, which is why almost nobody can read the deep chapters and why Tribal being able to read one of them is so significant.

Condition-revealed pages are already canon and now apply throughout. The Loyalty Elixir sits on a page that only reveals itself after three riddles (Trust, Sacrifice, Memory) and a spoken phrase. The chapter Tribal reads works the same way: it appears only once the terms are met and the time is right. Same mechanic, no reconciliation needed.

PRODUCTION NOTE (Bupe, 2026-08-10): the Book is to exist in the real world as a limited physical run. Consequence for how we write from today: every new piece of lore discovered across Hood Ninjaz gets drafted in the Book's voice, as a page, rather than as bible prose. Do that as we go and the physical edition assembles itself instead of needing a translation pass over four seasons of notes. It also keeps the in-world writing consistent, because it will all have been written by the same hand. Actual production is a much later Bupe gate (money and publishing); the material just gets built correctly in the meantime.

He did not miss the contamination by luck.

He did not miss the contamination by luck. He missed it by seven years, and he was not alive for any of it. The contamination ended 20 years before present day. Kevin is 13. He was born seven years after the last contaminated bottle was drunk, and Endsworth's water has been clean since long before he started there.

WRITING RULE: never write a lucky escape for this. A coincidence you have to engineer is a weakness. A chronology that simply works is a strength. The story never has to explain it. If anyone asks, he wasn't born.

Why that is what protects him. Everyone who drank the water carries a trace of Kūga, a signature, and Kūga resonates with its own signature. In a small way every water-generation ninja is already partly Kūga. Had Kevin drunk it, the Sphere would have arrived to find a door already open in its own handwriting and poured straight through: consumed from the first second.

Kevin has no trace. No signature, no door, no foothold. He is the first host in history who is not already partly the thing inside him. This is the mechanism behind The Rule below, "a living human will resists in ways stone doesn't."

The irony, for a much later reveal. Jon, Face and Jaden are the strongest ninjas alive precisely because they drank it, and every one of them would have been consumed instantly. The only person on earth who could survive carrying it is the one person who had no power at all.

The Hakai Sphere didn't just contain energy.

The Hakai Sphere didn't just contain energy. It contained a consciousness. Hakai is pure evil given awareness. Now sealed inside a living human for the first time in history, Hakai takes the form of whatever the host would find familiar. Kevin sees and hears a version of himself, but older, darker, colder. His own voice with something wrong underneath it.

Visual identity: Void black eyes. No iris, no white, just complete emptiness. This is the only visual marker. In dark environments they may appear as white outlines due to lighting, but the canonical colour is black. Hakai often wears a slight, knowing grin.

Shapeshifting: Can take any form, but the void black eyes are always present if you look.

Projections: Can create fully real visions that only Kevin experiences (e.g., the decapitated mum vision in Episode 1).

Presence: Kevin sees him walking about in the world, and only Kevin can see him. He can appear to have a hand round someone's throat and that person feels nothing.

Refined, cold, precise English.

Refined, cold, precise English. The evil-genius register: cunning, exact, intelligent. Against a Danim City backdrop the register collision does a lot of work by itself.

CRAFT FLAG, must be solved on purpose: Archer is already a refined English voice ("the refined voice arrives already amused", S1E02 opening). Two of them will blur badly in audio. Separate them mechanically so a director can execute it:

  • Archer performs. He has an audience, he is amused, he enjoys himself, and he uses long sentences. "Do try to keep up."
  • Kūga endures. He has one listener he despises, he is bored rather than amused, and he speaks in short flat sentences. He never explains anything twice.

Amused versus bored. Long versus short. Same accent, no confusion.

The comedy dynamic. Kevin teaches him slang. He deploys it correctly but in a horrifying context, so the joke is register collision rather than error. He finds pure hood talk tedious and would rather Kevin just killed the person than kept talking like that. It genuinely frustrates him that a god is reduced to this mediocrity, and that his host is weak and feeble. Every one of these jokes is also a test (section above), so the laugh and the dread are the same beat.

The evolution is not a writer's convenience.

The evolution is not a writer's convenience. Kūga is the half that can change (Kega amputated exactly this, section 9), so change is the one thing he is structurally capable of and Kega is not. It is also why he asks Kevin for mischief "for old times' sake", from back when he could not control it as well as he can now.

  • Stage 1, Cold and Indifferent: Single words at random moments. "Pathetic." "Weak." "Boring." Testing Kevin, watching, not invested yet.
  • Stage 2, Antagonistic: When Kevin starts training and growing, Hakai pushes back. Mocks him. Tries to destabilise him during fights. May attempt to take over during extreme emotion.
  • Stage 3, Dark Mentor: Hakai starts to respect Kevin. Not because Kevin is powerful, but because Kevin keeps getting up. Guides him through harsh truths and cruelty. Never kind, but useful.
  • Stage 4, Mutual Understanding: Kevin proves Hakai wrong. For the first time in its eternal existence, Hakai's prediction about a host is incorrect.

Three reveals are stacked and the order matters or it reads as confusion instead of mystery:

Three reveals are stacked and the order matters or it reads as confusion instead of mystery:

  1. The name: EPISODE 6 of Season 1 (Bupe's call: four or five episodes from the end, not the finale). "Hakai" was never his name.
  2. The mechanic (Season 2). He is not destruction, he is an amplifier, and the Ultimatum lands on top of this.
  3. The origin (Season 3 into Season 4). He is the severed half of Kega, and the seal taught him will.

Why not the finale. The Jaden reveal closes Season 1 and is the season's gut-punch. Two enormous reveals in one episode make each other smaller. Episode 6 also puts the name at the midpoint, where a reveal has to turn the show rather than just add information, and it gives the audience four episodes of holding the name before the finale.

How it surfaces: as a correction, and it must be earned. Kevin says "Hakai." Kūga corrects him.

He has been called Hakai for four thousand years and has never once cared, so the correction only works if something changed. It changed because Kevin has just done something that made him interested for the first time: a flash of real will, per the Power of Will rules above. The correction is Kūga's version of respect. He gives his name to something he has decided is worth naming himself to. That ties the season's biggest reveal to the power system rather than to the calendar.

Audience-first or simultaneous? Split it.

  • The name lands simultaneously. Kevin hears "Kūga" in the same second the audience does. That moment is the relationship and holding it back from him costs more than the irony is worth.
  • What the name MEANS is audience-first. Only the audience gets the second beat: a cut, an Archer line, a pin on a map. Kevin walks away with a word. The audience walks away with a warning. That gap runs four episodes into the Jaden reveal and belongs in the Audience Knowledge Tracker.

The Loyalty Elixir is an ancient concoction found in the Book, hidden on a page that only reveals itself after solving three riddles (Trust, Sacrifice, Memory) and speaking a secret phrase.

Contents
  1. How It Works
  2. How Jaden Created It
  3. Current Effects

The Loyalty Elixir is an ancient concoction found in the Book, hidden on a page that only reveals itself after solving three riddles (Trust, Sacrifice, Memory) and speaking a secret phrase. Designed specifically for trios, it is both a bond and a safeguard.

How It Works

If the trio maintains unity, the Elixir enhances their collective power, making them nearly unstoppable. However, should they ever split, the Elixir erases key memories of their time together after 3 months of no contact. This prevents former allies from targeting each other's families or identities out of vengeance. The only way to reverse the erasure is through frequent interactions that slowly trigger recall of shared memories, habits, and bonds.

How Jaden Created It

Jaden orchestrated the Loyalty Elixir as a contingency plan, knowing the Mandem might split. He obtained Jon's and Devon's blood without their knowledge:

  • Devon's blood: Jaden staged a sparring match and secretly collected droplets that spilled during combat
  • Jon's blood: Jaden feigned illness and set up a healing technique where Jon unknowingly pricked his finger on a tool Jaden provided

Current Effects

The Elixir has been active for approximately 7 years. Devon believes his rise to power was entirely his own doing. Jon is haunted by a feeling of loss he can't name. Neither remembers the depth of their bond. Small triggers (fighting techniques, old habits, Kevin's presence) cause flashes of memory that grow stronger with repeated contact.

Kevin Young (Protagonist)

ID
Bible s6.1
Details
Part of
6. CHARACTERS
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Kevin is 13 years old, awkward but brave, and the youngest of the Young siblings.

  • Age: 13
  • Tier: 1 (Dormant), reaches 2 (Awakened) by end of Season 1
  • Aura Colour: gold and white (resolved 2026-06-03)
  • Location: North Danim
  • Family: Mum (Ivy), Grandad (Jamaican), Sister (Sharon, 32), Brother (Jaden, 28, believed dead)
  • Mentor: Jon (Blade)
  • Inner Entity: Hakai

Kevin is 13 years old, awkward but brave, and the youngest of the Young siblings. His brother Jaden left home when Kevin was 3 and was reported dead when Kevin was 6. Kevin has been going to Jon's barbershop since childhood, brought by his mum. His heightened awareness leads him to notice things others miss: the back room door, the people who enter without getting haircuts, Jon's micro-reactions when certain topics come up. He accidentally consumed the Hakai Sphere, making him the most important person in Danim City, though nobody knows it yet.

Motivation Evolution:

  • Phase 1: Curiosity. Something's not right, he wants to understand.
  • Phase 2: Protection. Protect the people he loves.
  • Phase 3: Truth. Discovers Jaden is alive, wants answers.
  • Phase 4: Identity. Fighting Hakai's prediction of who he'll become.
  • Phase 5: Purpose. Comes full circle, fights for everyone.

Face / Devon Jakes (Antagonist)

ID
Bible s6.2
Details
Part of
6. CHARACTERS
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Devon has a scar on his face from childhood that caused relentless bullying.

  • Age: 30
  • Tier: 4 (Radiant)
  • Aura Colour: Black (oozing smoke, wavy thick cloud with a fizzing sound)
  • Ninja Name: Face
  • Real Name: Devon Jakes
  • Alignment: Morally grey. The audience should never fully hate or love him.

Devon has a scar on his face from childhood that caused relentless bullying. Jaden was the only person who ever accepted him. After Jaden's "death," Devon spiralled into darkness, and the Loyalty Elixir erased his memories of the bond he shared with Jon. He became Face, a warlord building a crew and planning to reshape Danim City.

Three-Layer Motivation:

  • Layer 1, The Void: The Loyalty Elixir erased his bonds. He feels an emptiness he can't name and fills it with power. Nothing satisfies him because what he's actually missing is brotherhood.
  • Layer 2, Ideology: He genuinely believes the system is corrupt. He wants to tear it down and build a survival-based meritocracy. He sees himself as a liberator, not a villain.
  • Layer 3, Trauma: The scar, the bullying, losing Jaden. His "only the strong survive" philosophy comes from being made to feel weak as a child.

Key Facts:

  • Does NOT know he has a son (Donte). This is a major reveal.
  • His mum is African descent. He deeply respects her, she's the only person who checks him.
  • Fighting style: Jin Kazama (Tekken 3), muay thai, kickboxing, blade telekinesis.
  • His crew includes: Manic (2nd in command), Sleeze, Eve, Spike, Grynd, and others.

Arc: Season 1: Charismatic, terrifying leader executing plans. Season 2: Cracks show, memories return, crew fractures. Season 3/Finale: Forced to confront that his vision was wrong when the TANCs embody his philosophy in soulless machine form. Must choose: die alone as king of nothing, or reunite with the brothers he forgot.

Jon / Blade (Mentor)

ID
Bible s6.3
Details
Part of

Jon is a master of blades: swords, knives, shurikens.

  • Age: 29
  • Tier: 4 (Radiant), suppressed, operating at 2-3 because he's holding back
  • Aura Colour: Blue (calm, disciplined, controlled)
  • Ninja Name: Blade
  • Location: Barbershop on Central/South border

Jon is a master of blades: swords, knives, shurikens. After Jaden's death and the Mandem's split, Jon withdrew from the ninja world and opened a barbershop. The Loyalty Elixir erased his deep memories of Devon, leaving him with guilt he can't explain and a feeling of loss he can't name. He still carries Jaden's double-sided coin.

Arc: Reluctant mentor (Kevin pushes, Jon gives in) to memories slowly returning through Kevin's presence, to accepting his past, to fully stepping back into the fight. Being around Kevin is slowly healing him because Kevin moves like Jaden, talks like Jaden sometimes, triggers flashes Jon can't explain.

Jaden Young / Daps (The Ghost)

ID
Bible s6.4
Details
Part of

Source

Jaden is the genius strategist of the Mandem, always ten steps ahead.

  • Age: 28 (presumed dead, actually alive)
  • Tier: 4 (Radiant), possibly the most complete ninja of the Mandem
  • Aura Colour: Gold (warm, adaptive, the light between Jon's blue and Face's black)
  • Ninja Name: Daps (from his ability to adapt in battle, almost precognition-like)

Jaden is the genius strategist of the Mandem, always ten steps ahead. He found the Book in detention, created the Loyalty Elixir, rigged the double-sided coin so Jon would stay. He is the cloaked figure from Episode 1. He faked his death 7 years ago at age 21 to protect his family after discovering Bio Genetix was behind the government missions the Mandem were running. He left home at 18 (when Kevin was 3) and has been operating undercover, investigating Bio Genetix and protecting from the shadows.

Different people call him different names: Face calls him Dappy (personal, from childhood). Other ninjas call him Daps (respect). Blade calls him Jaden (sees the person, not the ninja).

The Mandem Aura Colours: Gold (Jaden), Blue (Jon), Black (Face). Light, calm, darkness. When the gold disappeared, blue withdrew and black consumed.

Season 1 Reveal: Jaden reveals himself alive at the end of Season 1.

Details

Sharon is the eldest Young sibling.

  • Age: 32
  • Skills: Deadshot marksman, drunken master martial arts style
  • Notes: Recovering alcoholic, emotionally complex

Sharon is the eldest Young sibling. After Jaden's "death" she spiralled: substance abuse, partying, lost purpose. She eventually channelled her grief into joining the police force and becoming a detective. She is assigned the ninja case and becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth.

Arc:

  • Season 1, Investigator: Compiles files, tracks ninja incidents, captures and loses a low-level ninja. A senior officer assigns her to a special task force, but he's secretly feeding her intel to Bio Genetix through Paul Mitchell.
  • End of Season 1, Betrayal: Discovers the senior officer's connection to Bio Genetix. Witnesses a TANC in action. Discovers Jaden is alive.
  • Season 2, Reluctant Ally: Switches from hunting ninjas to helping them. Fights to undo the damage her investigation caused. Her arc is redemption.
  • Finale: Witnesses the Mandem's reunion and finally understands the depth of the ninja code.

Hella Mitchell (The Chaotic Flame)

ID
Bible s6.6
Details
Part of
6. CHARACTERS
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Hella is the rebellious daughter of billionaire Paul Mitchell.

  • Age: 28
  • Tier: 3 (Channelled), reaches Tier 4 when emotionally pushed
  • Aura Colour: No fixed colour. Shifts and flickers like fire, reflecting her instability.
  • Weapons: Twin daggers
  • Father: Paul Mitchell (billionaire, funds Bio Genetix)
  • Sister: Tammy Mitchell
  • Son: Donte (given up at birth, told he went to a good family)

Hella is the rebellious daughter of billionaire Paul Mitchell. She left her privileged life in Belvedire for the streets of Danim City, drawn to Face's danger and charisma. Their relationship is an unofficial couple: they have sex and act like a couple, but neither has ever said it out loud, and Hella privately considers Devon her boyfriend and lover. The day-to-day texture keeps what the old "sibling-like" note was reaching for: Hella plays the brat to him, the cute kind, a tiny wife bothering a huge quiet mountain of a husband (amended 2026-08-05, Bupe). She got pregnant at 15, gave birth at 15. Paul Mitchell manipulated her into giving Donte up, telling her the child would go to a good family. She doesn't know about the abuse in foster care.

Arc: Season 1: Chaotic wild card, follows Face, suppresses the pain of losing Donte. Season 2: Discovers the truth about Donte's abuse. A mother's fury directed at her own father. Steps out from Face's shadow, fights for her own purpose. Evolution: chaotic follower to independent force to mother reclaiming her son.

Donte is Kevin's dark mirror. Both are 13, both are discovering their powers, but Kevin has love and support while Donte has nothing.

  • Age: 13 (few months older than Kevin)
  • Tier: 2-3 (Awakened/Channelled), raw, untrained, emotion-driven
  • Aura Colour: black and white (Bupe's canon call, 2026-07-15; earlier dark red / crimson retired)
  • Power: Pyrokinesis, fire manipulation tied directly to his emotions
  • Parents: Face and Hella (doesn't know either)

Donte is Kevin's dark mirror. Both are 13, both are discovering their powers, but Kevin has love and support while Donte has nothing. He is the boy in the black "LIT" hoodie that Kevin sees fight four bullies from his window in Episode 1. Abused in foster care, Donte's powers awakened through rage. He lives in an abandoned warehouse in East Danim.

Arc: Anti-hero. He does bad things but the audience understands why. A lone wolf causing problems for everyone. His path crosses with Uno first (Chapter 9, their silent wordless bonding), then eventually Kevin. He will discover the truth about his parents, and that revelation forces him to choose between darkness and forging his own way. By the finale, he becomes a hero in his own right, separate from both parents.

ID

Uno is the first TANC built by Bio Genetix, but his creator Dr.

  • Appears: 13 (actually a cyborg)
  • Creator: Dr. Lucius Kane
  • Origin: Bio Genetix's first fully autonomous TANC

Uno is the first TANC built by Bio Genetix, but his creator Dr. Kane gave him something no other TANC has: a conscience. Built in the form of a young boy, Uno was designed to think, feel, and grow. When the military demanded Kane strip away Uno's autonomy, Kane refused and helped Uno escape. During the escape, a military EMP wiped most of Uno's memory and destroyed his tracker. Bio Genetix believes he's dead. Dr. Kane's fate is uncertain.

Uno washed up in East Danim with fragmented memories and childlike innocence. He retains combat abilities and advanced intelligence but doesn't understand human emotions or social cues. He found Donte's warehouse and became his silent companion (Chapter 9). His struggle is identity: is he a weapon or a person?

Kevin, Donte, and Uno are the next generation Mandem.

Kevin, Donte, and Uno are the next generation Mandem. The parallels to the originals are deliberate:

  • Kevin mirrors Jaden: the heart, the glue, family-first
  • Donte mirrors Devon/Face: rage, abandonment, fire, the dark path
  • Uno mirrors Jon/Blade: the outsider who joins, questions everything, developing moral compass

History repeats, but with higher stakes. The Mandem found a book. These three carry the actual forces that will shape the world: ancient power, inherited fire, and artificial life.

Tribal (The Voodoo Master)

ID
Bible s6.10
Details
Part of
6. CHARACTERS
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

Tribal's powers don't come from the Hakai Sphere or the water supply.

  • Age: 30s
  • Origin: Born from Sera's dark voodoo ritual, conceived through a forbidden ceremony
  • Powers: Voodoo magic, resurrection/cloning, life drain, spirit manipulation, memory manipulation, soul capture
  • Alignment: Lone operator, no fixed loyalty

Tribal's powers don't come from the Hakai Sphere or the water supply. They come from an entirely separate source: inherited voodoo from his mother Sera's dark ritual. This makes him unique in the power system. He can see things others can't, including the fractures in Face's memories from the Loyalty Elixir. He feeds Face cryptic hints about his forgotten past, slowly guiding him toward remembering Jon. His motives are always unclear.

Sera (Tribal's Mother). Raised by an abusive father, became obsessed with a priest. Performed a dark voodoo ritual to control him, which resulted in his death and her pregnancy. Imprisoned; Tribal taken at birth. She became feared in prison as a "serpent." Tribal inherited her mystical abilities but was raised by a secret society that both revered and feared him.

Tribal's Role: Season 1: Cryptic advisor to Face. Season 2: His mystical powers become essential against the TANCs. Sequel (Season 4): His ritual is the final crack that awakens the Original Ninja God.

Each member of the Mandem has a unique burn mark on their wrist, done by the group when they were teenagers.

Each member of the Mandem has a unique burn mark on their wrist, done by the group when they were teenagers. Same placement, same method, different designs for each member. The designs are not yet defined.

Spike noticed the cloaked figure's (Jaden's) burn mark during the Episode 1 fight. When he described it to Face ("some kind of burn mark, like it was done on purpose, old, healed"), Face's hand involuntarily moved to his own wrist. The Loyalty Elixir erased the context but couldn't erase the scar.

Jon has one too. Kevin may notice it during a haircut or training session later in the series.

DI Marcia Boateng. Danim City police, created 2026-08-27.

DI Marcia Boateng. Danim City police, created 2026-08-27. Late forties, British Ghanaian, twenty-three years in, fifteen of them stuck at the same rank because she refused Lucas and everyone like him. The officer who should have been SIO on the ninja case, and who objected in writing when a Detective Constable was appointed instead, over Lucas. She also wrote Sharon's accelerated-promotion recommendation years earlier, so both papers in Sharon's file carry her signature. She reads to Sharon as an obstacle and is in fact the only person protecting her. Her existence PROVES the sentence Lucas sold Sharon. He said no woman climbs the ranks here and he was describing his own handiwork: he made the same offer to Marcia two decades earlier, she refused, and she has not moved since. Marcia refused and was frozen; Sharon paid and was fast-tracked; and Sharon was going to be promoted anyway. Named once in E1, in Nelson's complaint. Survives, is eventually sought out and thanked by Sharon, and dies much later in an apparent suicide with a note that is not hers. Profile: Characters/Marcia Boateng/Marcia Boateng.md.

Superintendent Teddy Lucas. Danim City police, named 2026-08-27. The man Sharon paid for her fast-track at 28: he told her, truthfully, that her talent was off the charts, then told her no woman climbs the ranks here, and named the price. The promotion was already coming on merit and he knew it, so it was a robbery dressed as a transaction. Referenced without appearing in E1, in Nelson's "what is it the captain sees in you". Strongly indicated to be the corrupt officer on Paul Mitchell's payroll below, not yet confirmed. Profile: Characters/Teddy Lucas/Teddy Lucas.md.

Paul Mitchell. Billionaire father of Hella and Tammy. Lives in Belvedire. Funds Bio Genetix. Has a corrupt senior police officer on his payroll who feeds Sharon's intel to Bio Genetix (strongly indicated to be Teddy Lucas, above; awaiting Bupe's confirmation). Manipulated Hella into giving up Donte, then placed him in abusive foster care. Hidden puppet master connecting police, corporate world, and ninja underground.

Tammy Mitchell. Hella's intelligent younger sister. Timid but brilliant. Skilled in wrestling, fencing, archery, and hacking. During work experience at one of Paul's bank branches, she gets caught in the ninja bank robbery. This shatters her sheltered worldview and starts her journey toward discovering her father's true nature.

Audrey. The Mitchell household maid through Hella's teens (S1E02: the kitchen, the nursery brochure). Kind and powerless; genuinely believed Stonebridge House was real, which made her good heart one of Paul's instruments. When Hella left the house, Audrey took care of Tammy; what Audrey taught her, and the stories she told her about Hella, are future-episode backstory (Bupe 2026-08-05). She has since left the household and is not in the present-day picture.

Manic. Late 20s. Face's second-in-command. Illusionist with memory-altering abilities. Supreme strategist. Loyal to Face but often the voice of reason.

Sleeze Ball. Late 20s. Wild, unpredictable, covered in tattoos. Jagged blade combat, berserker fighting style. Comic relief of Face's crew. Street-smart and chaotic.

Eve. Late 20s. Snake ninja and poison specialist. Shadow snakes with white eyes, snake fangs, green blood that turns red. Cold, manipulative, seductive. Rivals with Hella over Face's attention.

Spike. Highly skilled ninja in black and gold. Name LOCKED 2026-08-13 (Bupe). He has been through three, and the record of them is worth keeping straight because two of Vision's own files had drifted apart on it.

  • "Sting" is what every drafted E1 script called him, right up to 2026-08-13.
  • "Vesor" is what this Bible called him (the entry read "Vesor (formerly Sting)"), and it is the title of the October 2024 draft Chapter 4, "Vesor's Reckoning". Bupe's account, 2026-08-13: he wrote Vesor because he did not want to use Sting. He also says it appears in the 3 Little Ninjaz scrapbook notes; that document was retired to BIN on 2026-08-05 and has not been re-read, so the scrapbook part of this is Bupe's word and not a checked citation.
  • "Spike" is the name that stands, and it supersedes both.

The pre-existing inconsistency, recorded so it is not repeated: the Bible had Vesor as current and Sting as the former name while every script still said Sting, so the two contradicted each other and nobody had caught it. Bupe's Spike call resolves it. Both earlier names are superseded and must not resurface.

The motif is a WASP (corrected 2026-08-13 after a brief mis-record as bee; the Bible had it right the first time). Black and gold are wasp colours, which is where his palette comes from, and his signature move and weapon are the sting, which is where the name Spike comes from.

The roller-skate girl's "a queen bee always gets the honey" is a joke resting on that, not a second motif. Wasps and bees wear the same colours and get mistaken for each other constantly, so she reaches for the bee version because it is the one with honey in it. Do not build a hive: there is no bee iconography in this crew, only the resemblance the line plays on.

The attacker from Episode 1 who fights Jaden in broad daylight, gets dismantled inside ten seconds in an earlier robbery, and reports the burn mark to Face without knowing what he has just handed over.

Sonya. Early 20s. Blind shinobi, mixed Japanese and Black heritage. Heightened senses make her one of the most dangerous fighters. Calm, introspective, strong sense of justice.

Trace. Age unknown. Guardian of the Book. Enigmatic entity who appears at pivotal moments. Has telepathy and weapon spawning. Connected to the janitor/keeper backstory. Can feel when the balance is shifting.

Archer (Narrator). The narrator of the series. Old-fashioned, posh voice resembling a British butler. Introduces Danim City and provides satirical commentary. The contrast between his refined tone and the street-level action adds ironic humour.

THE PUBLIC FACE (2026-08-27). To Danim, Bio Genetix is the trusted consumer AI company.

Contents
  1. Bio Genetix (Bio Gen)
  2. T.A.N.C. (Tactical Advanced Nuclear Cyborg)

Bio Genetix (Bio Gen)

THE PUBLIC FACE (2026-08-27). To Danim, Bio Genetix is the trusted consumer AI company. Gadgets, adverts, posters on bus stops, products in people's hands. Nobody in the show ever suggests it is sinister, and it is never investigated, right up until Boateng's tape names it.

THE SLOGAN, and it carries a second meaning: "Everything you are. Only better."

First hearing it is ordinary warm consumer branding and nobody thinks about it, which is the entire design. What it actually describes: "everything you are" is the harvest, every ninja encounter and every scrap the police feed them, taken down; "only better" is the product, the TANCs, built out of what was taken to replace what it was taken from. The full sentence is not a promise to the customer, it is a description of what happens to them, and it has been on the side of buses since Episode 1. Use it as the tag on every advert, shorten it later to just the first half so the audience completes it themselves, and save one deployment for somebody saying "everything you are" flat, unselling, in a room where the second meaning is standing in front of them.

Seeding is ambient and long. Full plan, with the Boateng trail that leads to the reveal: Scrapbook/Threads/boateng-trail-and-bio-genetix.md.

A corporation developing AI and cybernetic organisms, funded by Paul Mitchell. They've been tracking the Hakai Sphere for years and are using data gathered from ninja encounters to build the TANCs. They have a corrupt senior police officer feeding them Sharon's investigation intel. Their goal is to replicate and surpass ninja abilities through technology.

T.A.N.C. (Tactical Advanced Nuclear Cyborg)

Bio Genetix's artificial warriors, designed to counter and eventually replace ninjas. They evolve across the series:

Season 1, Prototypes. Crude, strong but beatable. Reliant on direct orders. Stiff movements. Vulnerable to stealth and teamwork. Bio Genetix learns from failures and begins collecting data.

Season 2, Adaptive. Smarter, faster, developing personalities (sadistic, calculating, comical). Can mimic basic ninja techniques. Self-repair systems. Specialised units emerge. Force good and bad ninjas to recognise a common threat.

Season 3 / Finale, Apex. Fully autonomous, self-aware, develop their own agenda. Can execute nearly all ninja techniques. Energy absorption, psychological warfare, near-indestructible. Break free from Bio Genetix's control. The Mandem's combined ultimate technique is one of the few things that can stop them.
