Character Ages (Present Day)

  • Face/Devon: 30
  • Jon: 29
  • Jaden: 28
  • Hella: 28
  • Sharon: 32
  • Kevin: 13
  • Donte: 13 (few months older than Kevin)
  • Uno: Appears 13

Timeline

30 years ago. Devon (Face) born.

29 years ago. Jon born. Hella born.

28 years ago. Jaden born.

~25-22 years ago. Water contamination period. Janitor/keeper hides the Sphere and Book at school. Water supply contaminated for 2-3 years. Distributed across Danim City schools. Thousands of children exposed. Janitor disappears. Devon (5-8), Jon (4-7), Jaden (3-6) all exposed as young children. Sharon (4-7) possibly exposed.

16 years ago. The Mandem meet in detention. Devon 14, Jon 13, Jaden 12. They find the Book in the school library. Training begins. Dormant powers start awakening. (Note 2026-08-05: at the S1E02 meet-cute three years later, Devon was with random mates, not Jon and Jaden; the two of them have never known about the girl or the baby.)

13 years ago. Kevin born. Jaden now has a baby brother.

14 years ago. Hella (15) gets pregnant by Devon (17). (Amended 2026-08-05 per S1E02's "sixteen in ten months"; the old 14/16 figures also failed her birth-year maths: born 29 years ago, so 15 at the time.)

13 years ago. Donte born. Face is 17, Hella is 15. Paul Mitchell manipulates Hella into giving up the child. Donte placed in foster care in East Danim. Face never told.

16-10 years ago. The Mandem's prime years (ages 14-20). Training, missions, rising to legendary status. Spy missions, assassin missions for the greater good. Government and secret service take notice. Off-the-record missions begin. Jaden starts investigating the organisations giving them missions. Discovers Bio Genetix is the funder behind everything.

10 years ago. Jaden (18) leaves home to protect his family. Kevin is 3. Old enough for hazy memories of playing with his brother, too young to remember his face clearly.

8 years ago. Jaden (20) creates the Loyalty Elixir. Tricks Jon and Devon into giving blood.

7 years ago. Jaden (21) fakes his death. The Loyalty Elixir activates. After 3 months of no contact, Jon and Devon's memories of each other begin to fade. Kevin is 6 when told his brother is dead. Sharon is 25, finishing her law degree.

7-4 years ago. Sharon spirals: party phase, substance issues, lost purpose. Eventually joins the police, rises to detective. Devon builds his crew as Face, forgets Jon. Jon opens the barbershop, withdraws from ninja world.

1 year ago. Kevin starts visiting Jon's barbershop more regularly. Jon notices something familiar about him but can't place it.

Present Day. Face (30) leading his crew, planning around Dexit. Jon (29) running the barbershop, avoiding his past. Jaden (28) alive, operating in secret as the cloaked figure. Sharon (32) detective, assigned the ninja case. Hella (28) with Face, doesn't know Donte was abused. Kevin (13) entering the ninja world, Hakai Sphere inside him. Donte (13) lone wolf, fire powers, living in warehouse with Uno.

Saved for after the main series. Throughout the main series, the sacred balance has been violated: water contamination, Elixir tampering, TANCs mimicking sacred arts, Tribal's necromancy, Kevin consuming the Sphere. Tribal's failed voodoo ritual is the final crack in an already weakening seal. The Original Ninja God awakens. Not out of revenge, but necessity. It doesn't see heroes and villains. It sees a broken order that needs to be purged.

The Name (locked 2026-08-10)

穢我 KEGA. "The defiled self." 穢 is the defilement kanji taken from kegare; 我 is self, I, ego. Pronounced KEH-gah, two beats, and identical in sound to the everyday Japanese word for injury or wound (怪我, kega, the word a kid uses for a scraped knee). Those kanji are ateji, chosen for sound: 怪 is suspicious or uncanny, the same character that opens 妖怪 (yōkai), and 我 is self. So the ordinary word for "wound" is written, by pure historical accident, as the uncanny I.

The Book writes 穢我. When anyone in Danim City says the name aloud it is indistinguishable from a word about a grazed elbow. Nobody hears the difference. Jon can read the character on a page and go quiet while a kid three feet away thinks someone got hurt.

WRITING RULE, ABSOLUTE: the Kegare layer is NEVER explained in-series. This is a creator's Easter egg. Surface reading is the wound. Anyone who researches it finds kegare (穢れ), the Shinto term for pollution and defilement, and realises the list of violations that wake him is not a list of crimes but a list of defilements. No future draft "helpfully" explains this. Ever.

Why kegare is the exact right word: it is not moral sin, it is accumulated heaviness, contamination that builds whether or not anyone did wrong. Nobody on the list is a villain. Sharon fed intel without knowing. Kevin swallowed a sweet.

Known and accepted collision: Kamen Rider Kuuga (2000) uses the kanji 空我 for Kūga. Flagged to Bupe 2026-08-10, his call, locked, not to be re-opened.

The Amputation: What Kega Cut Off (locked 2026-08-10)

Kega cut out the part of itself that could change its mind.

Kega had two functions that could not live together. It could judge: weigh what is broken, decide what gets purged. And it could be changed by what it saw: learn, adapt, take the shape of its surroundings. Those cancel each other out. A judge that can be talked round is not a law, it is an opinion, and Kega could never be absolute while it could still be persuaded.

So it kept the verdict and cut away the mind.

The cost is the whole tragedy. The part it removed was also the only part that could feel anything, understand anything new, or be wrong. Kega made itself permanently correct by making itself permanently incapable. And the discarded half went into the world with no judgment left in it at all, no way to tell good from bad, so it did the only thing it could still do: absorb whatever was nearest. For a thousand years, what was nearest was war. That half is Kūga (section 4).

What this buys, structurally:

  • Why Kega "doesn't see heroes and villains." Not a philosophy. A missing limb. It literally cannot. It removed the faculty.
  • Why Kega comes. Not to reclaim it. You do not reattach the limb you amputated on purpose. It is coming to finish the operation.
  • The yin and yang, with no good and evil in it. Kega is fixed, absolute, unchangeable. Kūga is formless, reflective, all change. Total opposition, zero morality.
  • Why Kega is the harder final boss. Not stronger. Unpersuadable. Kevin wins Season 3 by proving something wrong; Kega surgically removed the ability to be proven wrong. The whole series asks whether people can change (Face's memories, Jaden's return, Donte and his father). Kega is the thing that made itself unable to. That is the Season 4 thesis and it is load-bearing all the way back to Episode 1.
  • The quiet tragedy: the severed half is the only part that could ever have learned anything, and it ends up in a thirteen-year-old from North Danim.

Archer's version, if it is ever wanted aloud: "The god performed surgery on itself. It removed the only organ capable of mercy, on the grounds that mercy is a form of inaccuracy."

The Pantheon and the Two Seals (locked 2026-08-10)

Kega sat at the head of a pantheon. Ten gods answered to him, each with their own village, a couple of them close enough to share one. He set the law. They kept it. For a long time it worked and everybody knew why.

Then the Severing (section 4), and his law hardened with nothing left to correct it.

THE FIRST SEAL, 5,500 years ago. Done in arrogance. By this point everybody was on the same page and everybody was against him: he read as drunk on his own laws. They sealed him into the Book, and they were united, certain, and sure it was for the best.

For months it was. Then the problem nobody had thought about. Kega's laws were the foundation, and with him gone there was no authority on which law was fit for purpose and which was not. Competing readings. Things lost in translation. Contradictions nobody could settle. Too many factors at once.

Then the slide. They stopped meeting at the secret place, or somebody did not turn up. Whispers. Deceptive accusations. Not seeing eye to eye spread like a virus. The gods who had sealed him together became, over centuries, deadly enemies, and their feud passed down into their villages, which became the clans.

Kega's line as they sealed him, and it should be quiet, not shouted: "You don't know what you have done."

He was not evil. He was right, and it came true within months. Removing the foundation is what collapsed the order, and the collapse is what let Kūga rise. Sealing Kega directly caused the thing that killed all ten of them. The Season 4 antagonist is a god who was proved correct by history and has spent 5,500 years in a book being right.

THE SECOND SEAL, 4,000 years ago. Done in humility. Kūga caught wind of the order failing and rose. By the time they faced him he was a terrifying force: if they had not worked together he would have consumed and destroyed everything.

It took real persuasion to get the hottest head to agree. They tried to seal him the normal way, in open battle, and it did not work. They only realised mid-fight that it was going to be a sacrifice seal. Ten gods understanding, live, that they are already dead, and continuing anyway.

All ten died. The age of gods ended here. That is why the present day has Aura and no divine presence anywhere: there is nobody left. Kega survives only because he was already locked away when the bill came.

The pair, and this is the line Kūga gets (section 4): the first seal was done by beings who thought they knew better; the second by the same beings, once they had learned they did not.

Kūga's position, and it should be almost gentle rather than a rant: cause and effect. This is what the world made me, so I am amplifying it and giving it back. See it and experience it for what it is, multiplied.

No contradiction with the existing bible. The record already says the ten died in the seal and that a separate group buried the Sphere and then took their own lives. Those buriers are a smaller human group, almost certainly the first keepers in the chain that eventually reaches Danim City.

Kega Is Sealed Inside His Own Book (locked 2026-08-10)

He is the Original Ninja God, so the arts are his. The Book holds the Three Pillars, the forbidden techniques, the Elixir. He wrote the foundation and they bound him into it. His own laws are the bars.

THE TRIANGULAR ORDER (locked 2026-08-10, Bupe). Opening the Book is not the violation.

The Book can be opened. It can even be read. That is not what breaks anything.

The violation is a triangle, and it only becomes a problem when all three corners complete outside the law:

  1. READ
  2. UNDERSTOOD
  3. ACTED UPON

That triangle has to be monitored, has to follow law, and must not be misused. Any one corner alone is harmless. A man can hold the Book open on his lap for a decade and nothing happens. He can even read it. The binding only loosens when reading becomes understanding becomes action, taken outside the law.

This is why twenty years in a school library cost nothing, and it is why the violation list is what it is:

WhoReadUnderstoodActedVerdict
The Mandem, learning the Three Pillarsyesyesyes, within the lawNo damage. The arts used as intended.
Jaden, brewing the Loyalty Elixiryesyesyes, outside the lawTriangle completed wrongly. Real damage.
Bio Genetix, TANCs mimicking sacred artspartialpartialyes, outside the lawDamage, and they do not know it.
Tribal's chapter and ritualyesyes, and he is the only one who canyesThe final crack.

So Trace is not a guard on an object. It is the monitoring of a sequence. It does not care where the Book physically is or who is holding it. It steps in at the exact point where understanding turns into action outside the law, which is why Face can run the entire Danim underworld and never once trouble it.

And the Sphere is the second vector, separate from the triangle entirely: the water and Kevin swallowing it are the other half of Kega reaching back.

Which makes an existing fact terrifying rather than convenient: the most dangerous object in existence has been sitting in the Endsworth School library for two decades, guarded by Trace, read by three teenagers in detention sixteen years ago, in the school Kevin now attends.

Tribal Thought He Was Claiming Power (locked 2026-08-10)

Tribal is the only person alive who can read that chapter, and he does not understand what the chapter is. He sensed something enormous and reached for it. He believed he was taking the power for himself. He was turning a handle.

Better than intent as a catalyst, and it keeps his motives unreadable, which his profile says they always are.

REQUIRED THREAD, not yet built: how Tribal reaches the Book. It is in the Endsworth library and Trace guards it. Tribal against Trace is now a story that has to exist somewhere in Seasons 1 to 3. (See the Trace entry below, which may be most of the answer.)

TRACE: The Embodiment of the Second Seal (locked 2026-08-10)

While the gods lived there was no need for Trace. They were the order, and the Book was theirs.

Part of what the crystal seal meant was that the gods would be no more and the divine Book would be left to man. Trace was born out of that reality. He is not a ghost and he is not a person: he is what the Second Seal left behind to hold the line the gods could no longer hold themselves. They died knowing the Book would outlive them, and Trace is the provision they made for it.

So Trace haunting a school library is not a spooky detail. It is a 4,000-year post that has never once been relieved.

IT IS A REASON, not a being (locked 2026-08-10). Trace was not born and was not created. It is the reason the Book stays shut, given a shape, which is why it is not solid and why its appearance is closer to a conceptual outline than a body. Use "it", never "he": the writing must never quietly promote it to a person.

The illusion. Nobody sees Trace as a ghost and nobody questions its appearance, because a reason arrives already accepted. Humanity files it as just another person and moves on. The audience will notice long before any character does, and that gap is the hook, not a bug.

Tribal is the only one who sees it as it is, and it is the same rule as everything else about him. The acceptance is a property of the gods' order, and he sits outside that order (section 3, Voodoo). One rule, three consequences: Trace has no authority over him, Kega has no jurisdiction over him, and the illusion does not reach him.

Full profile: Characters/Trace/Trace.md. It holds the football, the thought-speech and the language of the gods, the two-channel device, the appearance spec, the engagement rule, and the one canonical fight (Face lost, and has never told anyone). Everything not in that file is still open.

This answers the Tribal thread (LOCKED 2026-08-10). Trace's authority derives from the Second Seal, and the Second Seal is a covenant among the living. Tribal's power is death-side and sits entirely outside the gods' order (section 3, Voodoo). He is not covered by the terms. Tribal does not beat Trace and never fights him. He walks past a guard who has no authority over him. The required "how does Tribal reach the Book" thread is closed.

Kega Arrives Unaware (locked 2026-08-10)

Kega does not know Kūga is here. He is not hunting. Tribal's ritual pulled him blind, and this is the correct shape: an arrival, not a hunt.

Hard rule, and it protects the whole series.

Hard rule, and it protects the whole series. A god who reads minds ends most scenes before they start and creates plot holes everywhere. Kega has no access to anyone's thoughts, ever.

What he does have is speed of acquisition. He learns a language in about a minute purely by listening to it spoken. He learns like a genius observing, never like a telepath. Every single thing he knows, he got by watching or hearing it, which also means he can be wrong, confused, and out of date, and he is all three when he arrives.

THE ARRIVAL SCENE (locked 2026-08-10, Bupe's blocking)

ID

Details
Part of
9. SERIES STRUCTURE
Source
Hood_Ninjaz_Series_Bible.md

The sting: Tribal is alive by accident.

Contents
  1. Establishing Kega's Scale
  2. Sharpening Kega's Shock (locked 2026-08-10)
  3. Staging the Season 4 Explanation (locked 2026-08-10)
  4. The Spine of the Entire IP (added 2026-08-10)
  1. Kega speaks, calmly, in the language of the gods. He has no reason to think he will not be understood.
  2. Tribal understands nothing. He is thinking he has heard this before somewhere, and is frantically trying to place it. He says nothing.
  3. Kega lifts a hand and charges a strike. His face is visibly frustrated. This is the first time in 6,000 years anyone has failed to answer him.
  4. Tribal says it out loud: "I don't understand you." That is the hinge of the whole scene, and it is the only reason he survives it.
  5. Kega realises it is a foreign language. The strike does not land.
  6. POV SWITCHES TO KEGA. We hear him thinking, and what is in there is not omniscience, it is disorientation. What is this language. What era is this. Why is he dressed like that. How was I brought back. Underneath his thoughts we hear Tribal still talking in the background, babbling, pleading, explaining, trying to save himself.
  7. And that is exactly what hands over the language. Tribal talks to stay alive, and the talking is the corpus. No mind-reading needed, and the irony is entirely his own doing.
  8. Kega stops thinking and decides: he needs to learn this language. The focus shifts onto Tribal and he starts analysing him.
  9. Over about thirty seconds his speech merges out of the god-language into English. No glow, no effect, nothing impressive to him. He simply starts speaking English, and that is what makes it terrifying.
  10. The same calm question again, now in English. Tribal understands it, has to answer, and cannot.
  11. The arm goes up. Mid-strike, at the corner of his eye: Kūga. This sensation. This power. This... Then it lands, and you can see it land. Not scared, not shaken. Focused, and determined.
  12. He leaves.

The sting: Tribal is alive by accident. Kega did not spare him. Kega found something more important mid-swing.

Why the POV switch matters. Those thirty seconds inside Kega's head are the only time the audience gets to be inside him, and what they find is a being who is lost rather than all-knowing. It plants "he arrives unaware" as a fact they felt rather than were told, and it is the moment the Season 4 antagonist stops being a force and starts being a character.

Simultaneously, across the city, Kevin. A headache, psychic distress, and he stops dead. He did nothing: the flare passed through him and Kūga answered without permission, two halves of one self resonating (see section 4, Kevin's Masking). The look on his face is not "I need to hide." It is "who is that, and why did something in me just reach for them."

Establishing Kega's Scale

Kega goes through elite ninjas on arrival. Nobody from the Mandem. The tier below: the ones who climbed to near-Mandem level without the Book, on raw talent alone, and are therefore arguably more gifted and permanently capped by literacy rather than ability. A good bitter fact for one of them to know about themselves. (Bupe's framing: if the Mandem are Messi and Ronaldo, these are the Maradona, Pelé, Zidane, Ronaldinho and Neymar of Danim.)

CRAFT RULE: this only works if the audience has watched those ninjas win first. Beating strangers establishes nothing. They need seeding across Seasons 1 to 3 so that by Season 4 we have seen them do something impossible, and then watch it not matter.

Sharpening Kega's Shock (locked 2026-08-10)

He knew he removed a defect. He never knew it survived as a thing. He was excising a faculty, not creating a being: in his mind it was cut out and gone, the way you burn a diseased limb.

So the beat is not a reunion, it is a discovery, and the discovery is worse. "That is mine. And it has been alive this whole time."

Staging the Season 4 Explanation (locked 2026-08-10)

The anime default is two gods monologuing at each other. Do not.

Kega explains it to Kevin, not to Kūga. He is a judge and judges address the accused, and Kevin is the one holding stolen property. Kūga listens from the side and interjects: corrects a detail, chuckles at the poetry line, and drops the "you left me to die" accusation into the middle of somebody else's testimony.

The exposition becomes a trial rather than a lecture, Kevin is inside it rather than watching it, and the two halves never quite address each other directly, which is far more uncomfortable to watch.

The Spine of the Entire IP (added 2026-08-10)

Worth stating once because it is now load-bearing across four seasons and a spin-off.

The gods failed at unity and it cost them everything. They sealed the thing holding them together, fell apart over whose law meant what, spread suspicion like a virus, and by the time the real threat came they had to be begged into standing together. It killed them.

The Mandem are that story again at human scale. Three brothers whose bonds were erased, who became strangers, who have to be reassembled before the real threat arrives.

Season 3 is the answer to both. The Mandem reunite, the 3 Little Ninjaz form, and they win through exactly the thing the gods could not hold. The children succeed where the gods failed.

Every character and organisation is connected through a web that nobody fully sees:

Every character and organisation is connected through a web that nobody fully sees:

  • Paul Mitchell funds Bio Genetix, which builds TANCs using Sharon's intel fed through a corrupt officer
  • Paul Mitchell is Hella's father, manipulated Donte's abandonment, employs Tammy
  • Hella is Face's partner. Donte is their son. Neither Face nor Donte knows.
  • Face's "only the strong survive" philosophy will be embodied by the TANCs, forcing him to confront that his vision was wrong
  • Jaden created the Loyalty Elixir, erasing Jon and Face's memories. Kevin is the key to triggering recall.
  • The Hakai Sphere contaminated the water creating all ninjas. Kevin consumed the actual source.
  • Sharon hunts ninjas while unknowingly helping build the weapons that will destroy them
  • Uno is an escaped TANC with a soul, representing what Bio Genetix tried and failed to control
  • Tribal can see Face's fractured memories, guides him toward reunion, and eventually cracks the seal on the Original Ninja God
  • The burn marks connect the Mandem physically even when the Elixir erased them mentally

When these threads converge, every revelation is a season-defining moment. Nobody sees the full picture until the audience does.

END OF SERIES BIBLE

Contents
  1. Appearances in S1E02
  2. Function in the story

Appearances in S1E02

  • The dinner table (Donte 6, Terrence 10). Donte is served last and smallest. Terrence reaches over and takes his bread roll without even looking at him, mid-conversation with someone else. The carer sees it and says nothing. One gesture, and the whole order of the house is established.
  • The freezer (Donte 11, Terrence 15). "Built like a door." Leads the five who ambush Donte in the yard behind the kitchen block. Pats the lid: "We made you a bed, bro. Try it. It's memory foam." After they stack weight on the lid and the banging stops, he is the first whose nerve goes: "Nah he's fine, man, it's got holes... it's got holes innit?"
  • The eruption. A fragment of the bursting freezer catches him across the face and opens his cheek. He goes down with blood running through his fingers, screaming "HE DID IT! HE'S A FREAK! HE DID IT!"

Function in the story

  • He is the load-bearing reason Donte's awakening becomes a conviction rather than a rescue. The adults arrive to find one boy badly cut, four scorched, and Donte unmarked in the wreckage. Terrence's bleeding face reframes an involuntary eruption as a chosen attack, and that is what puts Donte in the basement.
  • He is also the counterweight to the beggar. Two strangers, one takes from Donte for nothing, one gives to Donte for nothing, and the ledger Archer narrates runs between them.
  • Not a mastermind. A big kid in a place with no supervision, doing what the place taught him. The horror in the freezer scene is that nobody above him intervenes: the foster carer watches the ambush assemble from the kitchen window, takes a sip, and draws the blind.

The scar

  • The cut is canon and permanent. If he ever returns, he returns marked, and the mark is the same night Donte's fire first spoke.
  • Unresolved by design: he is the only living witness who saw it happen up close and named it out loud. Whatever he believes he saw, he has been carrying it since he was fifteen.

Open questions (for Bupe)

  • One-episode device, or does Donte meet him again?
  • If he returns: does the scar become a recurring visual marker the way Face's wrist tell is?
  • What did Terrence tell people afterwards, and did anyone with power ever believe him? A boy who has spent years saying "there was a kid who could burn" is either a joke or a lead, depending on who finally listens.
  • Where do the other four go? Currently unnamed and unwritten.

Backstory

Donte Jakes was born 13 years ago to 17-year-old Devon Jakes and 15-year-old Hella Mitchell. He has never known either parent. Paul Mitchell (his grandfather, though he doesn't know that either) manipulated Hella into giving him up at birth and told her the child went to a good family. The "good family" was abusive foster carers in East Danim.

His name is his mother's one act of defiance (locked 2026-08-05): Hella registered him and wrote the birth certificate herself, Donte Jakes, Devon's surname, refusing the Mitchell name she hates. She hid the certificate in the baby seat; the foster carer found it and read only the first name aloud. It is still at the foster home: the single document that can one day prove where he was really sent. Donte has no idea it exists.

Donte grew up in foster care. The carers abused him. The other kids bullied him. He didn't have love. He didn't have support. He had survival.

His powers awakened at eleven. LOCKED 2026-08-05 (S1E02 "Good Family"): five older kids sealed him inside a dead chest freezer in the yard and sat on the lid laughing while he suffocated in the dark, and the foster carer, who had watched the ambush assemble from the kitchen window, drew the blind. The fire came on the truth of it, that no one was coming: an eruption of ordinary orange flame that concentrated into a BLACK-fire core (the black fire is hotter than normal fire) and burst the freezer apart, part-melting it. The fire took his clothes and left his skin unmarked; then the flames went back into him and left an eleven-year-old naked, shivering and squeak-screaming in the wreckage, crying. He never attacked anyone: the only injury was a flying fragment of the freezer that cut Terrence's face open, and that bleeding face got the whole thing blamed on Donte, as if it had been his attack. That night the carers bolted him into the basement "dungeon"; he burned through the locks and let himself out of the front door the same way, because it was his door now.

He escaped the foster system that night, aged eleven. After surviving rough (S1E02: the squatter arch, then months alone), he found an abandoned warehouse in East Danim. He has been living there since.

Pre-Episode 1, Donte bonded with Uno (Chapter 9 silent bonding, in the workspace Archive). Uno had washed up in East Danim with fragmented memories after Bio Genetix's military EMP. The two of them found each other. They share the warehouse. Neither speaks much. The bond is built on presence rather than words.

In Episode 1, Kevin watches Donte from his bedroom window. Four kids surround Donte, mock him. Donte puts four of them on the ground. The fifth walks away. Donte stands in the aftermath, eyes moving over the bodies, checking nobody is getting back up. Calm. Hands at his sides. Not in a rush. Then he walks. Kevin runs outside; Donte is gone.

The LIT hoodie. Black, "LIT" printed across the front in white letters. The hoodie is his signature. Source LOCKED (2026-08-05, S1E02): the night of his escape, aged eleven, a squatter at a railway-arch camp who had shoplifted it to sell covered a shivering kid with it instead, bit the tag off and told him it suited him. The camp, and the man, moved on by morning, as squatters do. Whether the man ever returns is deliberately open.

Personality

Anti-hero. Does bad things for understandable reasons.

Lone wolf. Not interested in alliances. Not interested in being saved. Not interested in being known.

Calm during violence. Doesn't react emotionally to the fight. Doesn't celebrate. Doesn't taunt. Checks bodies after. Walks away when the work is done.

Smaller than the people he fights but doesn't back up. Stands like he is alone in a field even when he is surrounded.

Hands at sides when not fighting. No swagger. The economy is the threat.

The fire is in his core. The exterior is cold.

Cares about Uno. The bond shown in Chapter 9 is the only soft thing about him. He doesn't have the language for love yet, but he has the action of staying with someone.

Silent. Words are rare. When he does speak (Chapter 9 with Uno, future episodes), it should matter.

The contrast with Kevin is intentional. Both are 13, both are discovering their powers. Kevin has love (mum, grandad, the orbit of Jon). Donte has a warehouse, a cyborg, and a hoodie.

Motivation

Five-phase arc.

Phase 1 (early Season 1). Survive. Stay invisible. Stay alive. Protect Uno.

Phase 2 (mid Season 1 to Season 2). Lone wolf with fire powers. Causes problems for everyone. Anti-hero. The world's threat to him generates his threat to the world.

Phase 3 (Season 2). Reluctant engagement. Path crosses with Kevin and others. The 3 Little Ninjaz begin to form, even though Donte resists the framing.

Phase 4 (Season 2 to Season 3). Discovers truth about parents. Face is his father. Hella is his mother. The reveal forces him to choose between continuing the rage path (the path of his father, the dark mirror) or forging something new.

Phase 5 (Season 3 finale). Forges his own path. Becomes a hero in his own right, separate from both parents. The redemption is on his terms.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 2-3 (Awakened to Channelled). Raw, emotion-driven, ceiling unknown.

Aura colour: black and white (Bupe's canon call, 2026-07-15). The earlier reading was dark red / crimson, framed as inherited from both parents (Face's black plus Hella's flickering fire) but corrupted by rage. That reading is retired; the inheritance rationale may want a light story tweak so black and white reads as earned (flag for Bupe).

Fire read (locked 2026-08-05). His flame is standard orange fire that CONCENTRATES into a black-fire core and breathes back out; the black fire is hotter than normal fire. (The black-and-white AURA palette above is the separate, maturing energy signature; the fire itself reads orange-with-black-core from the first awakening.)

Pyrokinesis. Fire manipulation. Spirit-pillar primary, per Bible §3 ("Spirit. Mastering inner energy allows control over elemental forces or pure energy projection... Donte's fire manipulation come from Spirit"). Emotion-tied: anger fuels output. Risk: loss of control when emotion overflows.

Combat. Bible says "raw, untrained." Episode 1 shows smooth, efficient technique (four kids down in seconds with proper martial-arts footwork). The reconciliation: Donte has no formal ninja training but has survived years of abuse and foster-system violence with instinctual combat skill. He is untrained in Aura discipline; he is not unskilled in street violence. CANON: untrained in formal ninja arts, instinctually formidable in street combat.

Consequences of overuse. Per Bible §3, Spirit-pillar overreliance leads to "loss of control, unintended destruction." Donte's rage-fuelled pyrokinesis is a textbook case for this risk. Expect Season 2 or 3 near-catastrophes.

For the power system, see World/Power System (Aura).md (to be created).

Key Relationships

  • Face / Devon (30, his father). Doesn't know Face is his father. Doesn't know he is the LIT hoodie boy by Face's recognition either. The reveal is one of the load-bearing dramatic ironies of the show. Father and son share an aura family (both rooted in black) without knowing why.
  • Hella Mitchell (28, his mother). Doesn't know Hella is his mother. Doesn't know about her loss. The bus stop encounter in Episode 1 brings Hella in close proximity to Kevin (the dark mirror) without Hella ever knowing the boy she carried for nine months is two blocks away.
  • Paul Mitchell (grandfather, unknown to Donte). The man who placed him in abusive foster care. The deepest cut once Donte learns the truth.
  • Uno (companion). Silent bond from Chapter 9. The only person Donte trusts. They share the warehouse, share the silence, share the implicit understanding. Uno's combat capability and Donte's emotion-driven fire create a pair the world should be afraid of, even if they aren't yet acting on it.
  • Kevin Young (13, the "dark mirror"). Has not met face to face in Episode 1. Kevin watched from a window; Donte didn't see him. The mirror framing: both 13, both awakening, both at the start of long arcs, but with opposite emotional ecosystems. Kevin has love. Donte has Uno.
  • The four bullies in Episode 1. Now on the pavement. One walked. They don't matter as characters; they matter as a demonstration of what Donte is.
  • The foster carers. The abusers. Status unknown post-Donte's awakening. Are they alive? Did Donte's fire burn the foster home down on his way out? Flagged.
  • The 3 Little Ninjaz (future). Kevin, Donte, Uno. Donte mirrors Face in the original Mandem trio (rage, abandonment, fire, the dark path). The mirror is the structural payoff of the next-generation framing.

Arc

Season 1. Lone wolf anti-hero. The LIT hoodie boy seen by Kevin in Episode 1. Bonded with Uno (Chapter 9 pre-canon). Causes friction with both good and bad ninjas across the season.

Season 2. Path crosses Kevin's. The 3 Little Ninjaz begin forming. Hella discovers Donte's truth from her side. Donte does not yet know his parents.

Season 3. Donte discovers parents. The reveal forces the choice. Forges his own path. Becomes a hero on his terms by the finale.

Voice and Dialogue

Silent. Words are rare. When he speaks, it matters.

Episode 1. Donte has no spoken dialogue. He fights silently. The fifth-kid intimidation is wordless. He walks away in silence.

Chapter 9 reference (not directly read in this session, see Open Questions). The bonding with Uno is canonically silent. Per MEMORY.md: "Uno bonded with Donte silently (Chapter 9)." The pattern is established.

Pattern. Donte's silence is the character. The contrast with Sleeze's noise, Hella's volume, Sleezed Kevin's stuttering, even Face's calm-spoken authority, is the point. Donte is the one who doesn't say anything because nobody has ever listened.

First spoken line (future, undecided). Should land hard. Probably in a Donte-Uno or Donte-Kevin scene rather than a Donte-villain scene. Worth saving for the right beat.

Pyrokinesis is also dialogue. When Donte's fire flares, it speaks for him. Visual register of his emotional state. The audience reads his emotion through the fire because they can't read it from his face or words.

CANON: untrained in formal ninja arts, instinctually formidable in street combat (forged through years of abuse and foster-system fights). The "untrained" framing refers to Aura discipline, not physical fighting capability.

Father and parent reveal. Old PDF: "Donte is the son of Face and Hella Mitchell, but he was raised in a rough foster home, unaware of his parents." Bible same. CANON: locked.

Donte's escape from foster care. Old PDF mentions: "He eventually escapes the foster system and finds his way to Denim City." Bible doesn't detail the escape. CANON: escape happened, lives in East Danim warehouse. Specifics (did the foster home burn down, are the carers alive) are undecided.

Backstory

Devon Jakes was born in Danim City 30 years ago. African mum. A scar on his face from childhood that caused relentless bullying. Jaden Young was the only person who ever accepted him; the two became as close as brothers.

The name Face has a seed (locked 2026-08-05, S1E02): at seventeen, the first stranger who ever crossed his scar without flinching, a Belvedire schoolgirl on his own high road, left him with "I like your face." The armour got its name years before the warlord did.

At 14, Devon met two younger boys in detention: Jon Clark (13) and Jaden Young (12). Together they found the Book in the school library and became the Mandem. (Note 2026-08-05: at the S1E02 meet-cute, Devon 17, the Mandem already existed; Devon simply was not with Jon and Jaden that day, and neither of them has ever known about the girl or the baby.) All three were unknowing carriers of the Hakai Sphere's diluted potential from the school's water contamination years earlier. They awakened together, trained together, rose to legendary status together. Over the next several years they ran missions for the greater good, then for government and secret service.

Jaden faked his death seven years ago. Devon (23 at the time) was told his brother was gone. The Loyalty Elixir, which Jaden had quietly engineered as a contingency, activated after three months of no contact. Devon's memories of the Mandem bond began to fade. Without the gold (Jaden), the blue (Jon) withdrew. The black (Devon) consumed.

Devon spiralled. The Elixir-erased void left him filling himself with power and ideology. He believed his rise to power was entirely his own doing. He became Face. He built his crew. He started planning to reshape Danim City around a survival-based meritocracy.

What Face doesn't know:

  • Jaden is alive. Operates as the cloaked figure, Daps.
  • He has a son. Donte, 13, born when Devon was 17 and Hella was 15. Paul Mitchell manipulated Hella into giving Donte up at birth and told her the boy went to a good family. Devon was never told he was a father. He knows the night happened (S1E02 was their first meeting); he has never known it produced a son.
  • The far-future thread that undoes the not-knowing runs through Mele (Bupe 2026-08-05): Face sleeps with Mele one day; her pillow talk about a lost best friend's pregnancy at fifteen connects his dots; he confronts Hella, and in one conversation he learns there was a child and she learns he slept with her lost best friend. Nobody tells him. He assembles it.
  • His relationship with Jon was real and deep. The Elixir erased the context but the burn mark on his wrist (matching Jon's, matching Jaden's) is still there. His hand drifts to it when triggers land.

Personality

Calm. Quiet. The kind of quiet that is louder than shouting.

Doesn't rush. Doesn't announce himself. Moves through rooms like gravity adjusts around him. Ninjas part without being told. Sits in his worn leather armchair at the head of the room, the only piece of furniture that looks chosen rather than found.

Observant. His eyes move slowly around a room, scanning every face, reading every posture, missing nothing.

Morally grey. The audience should never fully hate or love him. Cruel when the work calls for it. Funny when his crew earns it. Capable of small mercies. Devastating when crossed.

Controlled. Doesn't snap. The few times the calm cracks are the moments that matter (the burn mark trigger in Episode 1, his hand drifting to his own wrist before he notices).

Charismatic in a quiet way. Doesn't perform. People orient to him without him asking for it.

Three layers underneath the calm (Bible §6 framing).

The Void. The Loyalty Elixir erased his bonds. He feels an emptiness he can't name. Fills it with power. Nothing satisfies him because what he is actually missing is brotherhood. He doesn't know this.

The Ideology. Genuinely believes the system is corrupt. Wants to tear it down and build a survival-based meritocracy. Sees himself as a liberator, not a villain.

The Trauma. The scar, the bullying, losing Jaden. His "only the strong survive" philosophy was forged in being made to feel weak as a child.

Motivation

Four-phase arc from the Series Bible.

Phase 1 (Season 1). Charismatic, terrifying leader executing plans. Face is in full control of his crew and his city blueprint. The Spike incident in Episode 1 introduces the first crack: someone matching the description of someone he should remember.

Phase 2 (Season 2). Cracks show, memories return, crew fractures. The Elixir's erasure starts to fray as Kevin moves in and out of Jon's barbershop, as Tribal feeds Face cryptic hints, as the burn mark recurs. Face's confidence in the project breaks.

Phase 3 (Season 2 into Season 3). Confronts that his vision was wrong. The Apex TANCs embody his "only the strong survive" philosophy in soulless machine form. Looking at them, Face sees what his ideology looks like with the humanity stripped out.

Phase 4 (Season 3 finale). The choice. Die alone as king of nothing, or reunite with the brothers he forgot. The Mandem can reunite only if Face chooses to remember.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 4 (Radiant). Aura fully visible. When Face channels, black smoke oozes from him: wavy, thick cloud with a fizzing sound. The aura behaves like it's alive.

Combat. Fighting style is a blend of Jin Kazama (Tekken 3 archetype), muay thai, and kickboxing. Devastating in close range. Reads opponents like a chess board. Combat tactician.

Blade telekinesis. Mind-pillar ability. Can throw blades and steer them mid-air with telekinesis. His signature unique-Aura technique (manifests at Tier 3 Channelled, fully realised at Tier 4 Radiant). The blades follow his attention.

THE CUFFS DO NOT CLOSE ON HIM (2026-08-27, decision B2). It is the aura, not intangibility, and the distinction is the whole ruling. Bupe kept the police station scene and told Vision to tweak the ability to suit the powers he already has rather than add a new one. No new power was needed. His aura is already living black smoke, so:

  • His wrists are inside the smoke before the metal arrives. The cuffs close on aura and drop through. Same for a grab, a shoulder, a closing door. Nothing about him has stopped being solid.
  • The dispersal is thickening, not vanishing. The smoke boils out until there is nothing to see, and he is still standing there talking.
  • The pair of eyes in the ceiling corner is misdirection, aura gathered where he is not, while the man himself walks out. That is a con, which is Face's actual character, and it is better than a superpower.

The limit, and it is what keeps every future fight worth watching: commit real force and you reach the man. A punch lands. A blade cuts. The aura buys him restraint, custody and courtesy, never combat. The state cannot hold him and a ninja can, which is a sentence about the world rather than about his stats.

Blade telekinesis at distance is simply confirmed, not new. Moving them with two fingers without looking, and recalling both with his back turned, is his existing signature technique operating at Radiant. No ruling required.

Combined ultimate. Part of the Mandem's combined Tier 5 (Transcendent) technique, achievable only with all three (Jaden, Jon, Devon) reunited and bonded. Visual and mechanical detail not yet locked.

For the power system, see World/Power System (Aura).md (to be created).

Key Relationships

  • Jaden Young / Daps (28, presumed dead but alive). The brother who accepted him when no one else did. The gold in the Mandem trio. Devon's memories of Jaden have been erased by the Loyalty Elixir, but the bond's echo remains. Devon called Jaden "Dappy" in private, a nickname from childhood. Face does not know Jaden is alive. The cloaked figure who fought Spike has a burn mark Spike noticed; Face's hand goes to his own wrist when he hears.
  • Jon Clark / Blade (29). The other brother. Has not interacted with Jon in years. The Elixir has erased the deep bond. Both men feel a loss they can't name. They live a couple of districts apart in the same city and the world feels like it has a hole in it. Neither has the language for why.
  • Hella Mitchell (28). His partner: an unofficial couple (amended 2026-08-05): they have sex and act like a couple, and neither has ever said it out loud; she privately considers him her boyfriend and lover, he never names it. The dynamic is brat-and-mountain: tiny Hella needling a huge quiet Devon, cute-wife-bothering-massive-husband energy; he tolerates precisely all of it. They first met at 17 and 15 (S1E02). Devon keeps her close, uses her chaotic energy when it serves him. There is loyalty and a tough-love bond between them. Does not know they have a son.
  • Donte Jakes / Blaze (13, his son). Does not know about Donte. The reveal will fracture everything. Donte mirrors Face in the next-generation trio (rage, abandonment, fire, the dark path). When father and son finally meet, neither will recognise it for what it is at first.
  • Paul Mitchell (Hella's father). The puppet master who manipulated Hella into giving up Donte. Funds Bio Genetix. Paul despises Face. Face is largely indifferent to Paul until Paul's role in Donte's abandonment surfaces.
  • Manic (late 20s, 2IC). Illusionist with memory-altering abilities. Supreme strategist. Loyal to Face but often the voice of reason. The one crew member who can push back without consequences.
  • Sleeze (late 20s). Comic relief in civilian mode, brawler when the work starts. Two-mode duality (see Characters/Sleeze/Sleeze.md, to be created). Face tolerates the noise because Sleeze is loyal and effective when it matters.
  • Spike. The black-and-gold ninja, wasp motif, his move and weapon the sting (name locked 2026-08-13; "Sting" and "Vesor" are both superseded). The Spike incident in Episode 1 is the first crack in Face's project: Spike got jumped by the cloaked figure in Central Danim in broad daylight, caused destruction that made the news, and reported a burn mark.
  • Eve (late 20s). Snake ninja, poison specialist. Cold, manipulative, seductive. Rivals with Hella over Face's attention. Loyal to Face but plays her own games.
  • Tribal (30s). Cryptic advisor. Tribal can see the fractures in Face's Elixir-erased memories and feeds him hints. Tribal's motives are unclear. Face accepts the hints without trusting the source.
  • His mum. African heritage. Devon respects her deeply. She is the only person who can still check him. She doesn't know what he does.
  • The Mandem (historical). Jaden, Jon, Devon. Gold, blue, black. The legend the Hood remembers. Officially dissolved when Jaden "died." In practice still in Face's bones, just locked behind a chemical wall.

Arc

Season 1. Charismatic, terrifying leader executing plans (bank robbery, Dexit preparations). Spike's report of a cloaked figure with a burn mark triggers the first crack in Episode 1. His hand drifts to his own wrist. The final shot of the safe-house scene is the room holding its breath. The audience does not know why yet.

Season 2. Cracks deepen. Memories return in flashes. Manic notices Face is not quite himself. The crew fractures along old loyalties. Hella discovers the truth about Donte. The Mandem reunion begins.

Season 3. Apex TANCs break free and embody Face's "only the strong survive" philosophy. Face is forced to confront that his vision, executed by machines, is the actual horror. The Mandem fully reunite when Face chooses to remember. The combined ultimate technique is unleashed against the TANCs.

Voice and Dialogue

Calm. Quiet. Economical. The kind of voice that makes people lean in because he won't raise it.

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

"What happened?" Calm. Quiet. The kind of quiet that's louder than shouting.

"Jumped by who?" One question. No fluff.

"Well, ain't he lucky. Why is that then?" Sarcastic when the answer is poor. Doesn't help Spike save face.

"That doesn't seem much of a disguise. All this commotion and you couldn't give any sort of description?" Cuts. The crew watches Spike fail and there is no rescue coming.

"Great. That narrows it down." Dry. Bored. He's seen amateurs before.

"What did you just say?" When the burn mark is described, the tone shifts. Harder. Still calm but with something underneath. The crew clocks the change before Face does.

The wrist tell. Face's hand drifts to his own wrist when triggers come up. He doesn't notice. The audience does. This is the visible echo of the bond the Elixir erased.

Silence is his loudest tool. Closes his eyes before asking. Lets the room stretch. Waits. The crew fills the gaps.

Affection register. When alone with Hella or his mum, the calm softens. Not warm exactly, but human. Different from the warlord voice. The audience needs to see this register to keep him morally grey.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Face at 27. Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Face at 30. CANON: 30. The master timeline only balances at 30 (Donte 13, Devon 17 at Donte's birth, Devon now 30). The older age is retired.

Face origin: scar vs pale white face. Old Archive/Characters.pdf: "His street name comes from his pale white face, which he hides behind a mask due to his insecurities." Series Bible: "Devon has a scar on his face from childhood that caused relentless bullying." CANON: scar from childhood. The pale-face-and-mask origin is retired. The scar origin gives Face a real trauma anchor that ties into the Trauma layer of the three-layer motivation. The pale-face version reads as superficial in comparison.

Mask. Old PDF has Face hiding behind a mask. Series Bible does not establish that Face wears a mask. Episode 1 does not show Face in a mask (his expression is read explicitly, his eyes find Spike, the audience watches his hand drift to his wrist). CANON: Face does not wear a mask. His face, scar and all, is visible. The mask is retired with the pale-face origin.

Temperament. Old PDF describes Face as "temperamental." Series Bible and Episode 1 paint him as controlled, calm, the quiet that's louder than shouting. CANON: controlled and calm, not temperamental. Temperamental is retired. The "highly intelligent on the battlefield" and "power-driven" elements from the old PDF remain, but the temperament framing is gone.

City spelling. Old Archive/Characters.pdf Face entry: "his plan to take over Denim City." CANON: Danim City. This is one of the explicit "Denim" spellings in the old PDF that needed correcting. The original PDF stays unchanged as historical record; the extracted Face content uses Danim throughout.

Three-layer motivation, Loyalty Elixir, son Donte, African mum, blade telekinesis, aura colour and behaviour. Not in old Archive/Characters.pdf. Added in Series Bible. CANON: Series Bible additions are locked. These are the additions that make Face work as a morally grey three-season antagonist rather than a flat warlord.

Crew composition. Old PDF lists a generic crew of bad ninjas (Oxyde, Dee-Day, Eve, Sleeze Ball, Manic, Tribal, Koko the Clown, Syren). Series Bible specifies "Manic (2nd in command), Sleeze, Eve, Spike, Grynd, and others." CANON: Series Bible roster as the locked named crew, plus Sleeze (canonised as the same character as Sleeze Ball per Bupe 2026-05-11). Other old-PDF bad ninjas (Oxyde, Dee-Day, Koko the Clown, Syren) are pending or retired (see Characters/_Pending_or_Retired/ files).

  • Face's first reaction to learning about Donte. A major beat. DIRECTION LOCKED 2026-08-05: nobody tells him; he assembles it from Mele's pillow talk and confronts Hella (see What Face Doesn't Know). Season/episode placement, and how he responds, still open.
  • The Dappy nickname. Bible says Face called Jaden "Dappy" in private. When does Face first say it again in Season 2 or 3? The audio of him saying it for the first time after the memories return could be a load-bearing moment.
  • The combined Mandem ultimate. Bible says it lives at Tier 5 (Transcendent), only achievable with all three reunited. What is it visually and mechanically? Sky-darkening, ground-cracking type technique per Bible Tier 5 description, but the specific form is undecided.

Backstory

Hella Mitchell was born 28 years ago to billionaire Paul Mitchell. Grew up in Belvedire, the wealthy outskirts of Danim City, in the lap of luxury and the shadow of her father's cold control.

Always drawn to danger and rebellion. Her sister Tammy admired her from afar; her father tried to control her at every turn. As a teenager she crossed paths with Devon Jakes: fifteen-year-old Hella cutting through South Danim in school uniform, seventeen-year-old Devon crossing the road for her (the meeting is S1E02). Years later, after Donte, they reconnected as Devon rose to become Face. Their relationship today is an unofficial couple (amended 2026-08-05, supersedes the earlier sibling-like framing): they have sex and act like a couple, but neither has ever said it out loud. Hella privately considers Devon her boyfriend and lover; Devon never names it. The day-to-day texture is the brat-and-mountain dynamic (Bupe 2026-08-05): tiny Hella bothering a huge, quiet Devon the way a cute wife needles a wall of a husband; the old "sibling-like" note was reaching for exactly this. Absolutely binding either way.

At 15, Hella got pregnant by Devon (who was 17; ages amended 2026-08-05 to match S1E02 and her birth year). She gave birth at 15. Paul Mitchell manipulated her into giving up the child at birth, told her the boy went to a good family, and sold the lie with a fabricated brochure (Stonebridge House, typeset by his own people; S1E02). Hella's one act of defiance (locked 2026-08-05): she registered the baby and wrote the birth certificate herself, Donte Jakes, Devon's surname, a deliberate refusal of the Mitchell name and the father it belongs to. Paul never knew. She hid the certificate in the baby seat; the foster carer found it and read only the first name; it remains at the foster home to this day, the one document that can prove where Donte was really sent. The boy was placed in abusive foster care in East Danim. Hella does not know about the abuse, or that the brochure was fiction. The wound of Donte is the deepest one she carries, buried under the chaos.

Hella awakened her ninja powers somewhere along this journey. The Bible doesn't specify the exact path or trigger (see Open Questions); the result is twin-dagger combat and a flickering fire-like aura that has no fixed colour.

She has a phoenix tattoo on her arm, symbolising rebirth from the chaos she creates (per old Archive/Characters.pdf expanded entry). Bold, flashy appearance: dyed hair, bold makeup, leather, crop tops. The look is a deliberate rejection of her father's high-society expectations.

The Loyalty Elixir is not directly tied to Hella, but she lives in the wake of Face's spiral after Jaden's "death." She has watched Face fill the Elixir-erased void with power. She is loyal to that path without fully understanding why he needs to fill himself the way he does.

Personality

Chaotic. Wild. Unpredictable. The embodiment of fire and danger.

Loud. Bold. Flashy. Doesn't dress for invisibility.

Fun-loving on the surface, deep emotional wound underneath. The chaos is real; so is the suppression of Donte underneath it.

Loyal to Devon without reservation. Idolizes him. Sees him as the only person who truly sees her. The relationship is an unofficial couple, never labelled aloud (amended 2026-08-05): she plays the brat to him, the cute kind, tiny against his bulk, pestering and orbiting; mutual respect plus tough love, not abusive but charged.

Manipulator when needed. The high-society upbringing taught her to read people; she uses the skill freely now.

Resourceful, street-smart. Crossed from Belvedire to the underworld without losing her ability to survive in either.

Instigator. Stirs the pot. Watches the fallout with amusement, sometimes detachment.

Flirtatious but emotionally unavailable. Offers a 13-year-old condoms at a bus stop. The "Styles" leggings, the casual handing-off, the XXL packaging. The flirtation is reflexive; the emotional connection is closed.

Emotionally complex underneath. Father's rejection cuts. Donte's absence cuts. Devon's emotional unavailability cuts. The complexity is hidden beneath the fire, but flickers through in unguarded moments.

Motivation

Four-phase arc.

Phase 1 (Season 1). Chaotic wild card. Follows Face. Suppresses the Donte wound under chaos. The bus stop scene with Kevin is the audience's introduction to her duality: explosive aggression followed by disarming charm, all hiding a wound she won't admit she has.

Phase 2 (Season 2). Discovery. Learns the truth about Donte's abuse and her father's role in the abandonment. A mother's fury directed at Paul Mitchell.

Phase 3 (Season 2 to Season 3). Independence. Steps out from Face's shadow. Fights for her own purpose. Pursues Donte.

Phase 4 (Season 3 finale). Reclamation. Reaches her son. Or fails to. The resolution is the emotional spine of her arc.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 3 (Channelled), reaches Tier 4 (Radiant) when emotionally pushed. The push is her tell: when she's in control she stays Tier 3; when the wound surfaces (Donte references, her father, threats to those she's loyal to) she breaks into Tier 4.

Aura. No fixed colour. Shifts and flickers like fire. Visible from Tier 3 onward as heat distortion, then full flickering flames in Radiant moments. The unfixed colour mirrors her instability and reads as deliberately uncategorisable: she belongs to neither side cleanly.

RED EYES: the bloodline tell (Bupe's ruling, 2026-08-27, decision B3). When she breaks to Radiant her pupils turn red, she gets faster, she hits harder, and steam comes off her. In the Eve fight she breaks an elbow and then ribs in about two seconds in this state.

It runs in her blood. It is not a technique and it cannot be taught. The proof is in how it is received rather than in what it does: Face's reaction is to look at her eyes, not at what she just did to a man, which tells the audience this is a known and feared thing without a word of explanation.

Live ammunition, do not spend it carelessly: this loads Eve's taunt "apples don't fall far from the tree" (decision C6, open) and it makes Hella's parentage a question the audience starts asking on their own. The red is never explained by anyone in Season 1.

Twin daggers. Her signature weapons. Wild combat style, unpredictable, berserker-leaning when pushed.

Master of street fighting. Combat reads as instinct over technique. Doesn't fight clean; fights to win. Her unpredictability is the weapon.

Master manipulator. Reads people fast, plays them faster. The high-society skill repurposed for the underworld.

Street-smart and resourceful. Connections in unlikely places. Knows where the doors are.

For the power system, see World/Power System (Aura).md (to be created).

Key Relationships

  • Paul Mitchell (father, billionaire, Belvedire). Cold, controlling. Manipulated her into giving up Donte. Cut off financial support when she chose Devon. The relationship is functionally dead but contractually still binding via the family name. Hated and unresolved.
  • Tammy Mitchell (younger sister). Tammy admired Hella from afar growing up. Hella was the rebellion Tammy couldn't risk. By Season 2, when Tammy's innocence is shattered (the bank robbery scene), the sister dynamic shifts. Hella has to face that her role-modelling was, in part, what made Tammy's worldview rigid.
  • Donte Jakes / Blaze (13, her son she gave up). The wound that never heals. Doesn't know he's the LIT hoodie boy in East Danim. Doesn't know about the abuse. The discovery in Season 2 is the inflection point of her arc.
  • Devon / Face (30, partner). Unofficial couple (amended 2026-08-05): they have sex and act like a couple, but neither has ever said it out loud; she privately considers him her boyfriend and lover. In the room it reads brat-and-mountain: she is tiny next to him and bothers him constantly, the way a cute wife needles a huge silent husband; he tolerates precisely all of it. Loyal completely. Sees Devon as her protector, the only person who truly understands her. Devon's emotional unavailability hurts but doesn't break the loyalty. He doesn't know they have a son.
  • Kevin Young (13). Met briefly at a bus stop in Episode 1. Doesn't know his significance. Doesn't know he is, in some sense, the mirror of the son she gave up. The audience reads the parallel; Hella does not yet.
  • Mele (best friend then; lost since). The only person who ever knew about the pregnancy, and she never knew who the father was: Hella never said, and Mele never asked (to Mele sex is just sex, birth control exists, and the father was irrelevant to supporting a friend). They drifted apart after school, nothing bad, just distance. Hella has never had a best friend since. Load-bearing future thread: see the discovery chain in Open Questions.
  • Audrey (the household maid of her teens). Kind, powerless, unknowingly one of Paul's instruments (she believed the brochure with her whole heart). After Hella left the house, Audrey took care of Tammy in the gap Hella left: what she taught Tammy, and the stories she told her about Hella, are future backstory (Bupe 2026-08-05). She has since left the household.
  • Eve (late 20s). Rival within Face's crew. Cold tension over Face's attention. Hella's chaos vs Eve's calculation. They circle each other.
  • The Mandem (historical). Hella is too young to have been part of the Mandem proper, but lived adjacent to Devon's rise after Jaden's "death." She watched Devon spiral into Face without understanding why.

Arc

Season 1. Wild card chaotic flame. Episode 1 bus stop introduces her duality. Suppressing the Donte wound. Loyal to Face. The bus stop encounter with Kevin is the audience's planted seed for what's coming.

Season 2. Discovers Donte's truth. Mother's fury at her father. Confronts Paul Mitchell. The Tier 4 surges become more frequent. Tries to reach Donte.

Season 3. Independence. Steps out of Face's shadow. The reunion with Donte (or the failure of the reunion) is the climactic emotional beat.

Voice and Dialogue

Loud, crude, fast. Cycles between explosive aggression and disarming charm. Comfortable swearing. Direct sexual references casually deployed.

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

"Ahh, you men are all the same! Only stick around to get what you want!" On the phone. The explosive entrance.

"As soon as you bust your nut, you..." Cut off when she notices Kevin. The crude register interrupted by accidental self-awareness.

"...Shit." Sighed. The self-correction.

"Fuck it." The shrug.

"Come sit. What are you afraid of?" Disarming, slightly daring. The pivot to charm.

"Suit yourself."

"You look like you're gonna meet your crush for the very first time." The teasing pivot.

"What I mean is. You look like you want to crack the Da Vinci code."

"Does she even know your name?"

"Your crush."

"Oh?"

"Well, why would you be heading to town at this time?" The condoms moment. Casual. The XXL packaging is the comic punch.

"Why?" When Kevin says he wants someone to teach him something. The first genuine register of the encounter.

"Finally!" When the bus arrives.

"Do you know how long I've been waiting? The app said three minutes. THREE MINUTES. That was fifteen minutes ago. What were you doing back there? Playing with your fucking balls?" The bus driver rant.

(Fading) "No, don't give me that fucking look. I pay for this service! I PAY! You think I'm standing out there in the cold so you can finish your wank break?!"

Pattern. Volume swings. Goes from full shout to flat resignation in a single beat. Profanity is reflexive, not performative. Crude sexual references casual and frequent. Charm and chaos sit side by side.

The maternal undercurrent. The condoms offered to Kevin read as comic on the surface, but the visual subtext is a woman who lost her own 13-year-old son offering protection she didn't get to give. Hella doesn't connect the dots. The audience does, eventually.

Tier 4 surge dialogue register. When she breaks into Tier 4 from emotional push, the voice flattens. The chaos turns into something colder. The flatness is the signal that she's in dangerous territory.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Hella at 26. Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Hella at 28. CANON: 28. Master timeline (Hella 15 when Donte was born 13 years ago, Hella 28 now) is consistent.

Tier and aura. Old PDF silent. Bible adds Tier 3 with Tier 4 surge, flickering no-fixed-colour aura, twin daggers. CANON: Bible additions locked.

Power awakening. Old PDF and Bible both silent on the specific path. Old PDF describes her as "Master of street fighting, Berserker-style combat." Bible adds Tier and aura but not the awakening trigger. CANON: powers and combat style locked per Bible and old PDF; awakening trigger remains an Open Question.

Phoenix tattoo. Old PDF expanded entry mentions a phoenix tattoo on her arm. Bible silent. CANON: retained from old PDF. Symbolises her constant rebirth from the chaos she creates. Visual continuity element for scenes that show her arms.

Appearance. Old PDF expanded: dyed hair (vibrant unnatural colours like fiery red or electric blue), bold makeup, leather jackets, crop tops, "Styles" tights. Episode 1 confirms the "Styles" tights and the bold register. CANON: old PDF appearance locked unless visual director adjusts. The flashy register is part of who she is.

Donte abandonment. Old PDF expanded and Bible both: Paul Mitchell manipulated Hella into giving up Donte at birth, told her the boy went to a good family. CANON: locked.

Relationship with Devon. Old PDF and Bible both said sibling-like. AMENDED 2026-08-05 (Bupe): unofficial couple. Sex and couple behaviour, never said out loud; she privately considers him boyfriend and lover. The sibling-like texture survives INSIDE the couple frame as the brat dynamic (tiny Hella, huge Devon, cute-wife-bothering-massive-husband energy); what is retired is only the idea that it is not romantic or sexual. The not-Harley-and-Joker guard stays load-bearing: loyalty and charge, never a stock unhinged girlfriend. Physical note now canon: Hella is small in height next to Devon's bulk, and uses it.

Hella's mother. No source mentions her. CANON: undecided. Worth a small lock or a deliberate absence. Flag.

Sex and nudity. Bible §1 establishes "Relationships involve sex and it's shown honestly." Hella is one of the most sexualised characters by appearance and dialogue. The line of how much is shown on screen is not explicit in any source. Worth flagging for production-stage decisions.

City spelling. Old PDF Hella expanded entry uses "Danim City" consistently. Good. The only Denim instances in old PDF live in the Face entry and the merged list at the back.

Open Questions

  • Hella's mother. Season 2/3 candidate, deliberately absent for now (deferred 2026-05-12). Who she is, where she is, whether she died or left or was driven out by Paul Mitchell, will be locked when the story needs her. For Season 1 she is not on screen and not referenced.
  • Hella's power awakening. When and how did she become a ninja? Self-trained through trauma? Trained by Devon? Some other path?
  • When Hella discovers Donte's truth. DIRECTION LOCKED 2026-08-05 (Bupe): nobody tells her; it detonates. Far future: Face sleeps with Mele; Mele's pillow talk about a lost best friend (the pregnancy at fifteen, the timing) connects Face's dots; Face confronts Hella, and in one conversation he learns there was a child and she learns he slept with her lost best friend. The unravelling that follows runs through the foster home, the hidden birth certificate in her own handwriting, and the discovery that Stonebridge House never existed. Exact season/episode placement still open (the Bible currently pegs her discovery in Season 2).
  • The phoenix tattoo on screen. Should be visible in Episode 1 if she's wearing the leather jacket arrangement that exposes her arm. Visual continuity flag.
  • The Hella vs Eve rivalry. Bible mentions the rivalry exists but doesn't lock specific beats. Worth mapping for Season 1 / 2 crew tension.
  • Hella's first interaction with Kevin after Episode 1. Bus stop is the planted seed. When does she next encounter him, and does she recognise the significance once the dots connect (a 13-year-old boy in her path, the age her son would be)?

Jaden Young was born in Danim City 28 years ago.
