Backstory

Jaden Young was born in Danim City 28 years ago. Middle of the three Young siblings (Sharon four years older, Kevin fifteen years younger). His father was absent in the same way Kevin's is, though Jaden may know more about that absence than Kevin does (see Open Questions).

At 12, Jaden met Devon Jakes (14) and Jon Clark (13) in detention. The three of them found the Book in the school library, all unknowingly carrying the diluted potential from the Hakai Sphere water contamination years earlier. Jaden's awakening was the deepest of the three; his Aura turned gold and his cognition turned adaptive. He could read fights like chess problems and find moves no one else could see. "Daps" emerged as his ninja name, from the way he adapted to whatever the fight gave him, almost as if he knew it before it happened.

The Mandem rose to legendary status over the next several years. Spy missions, assassin missions for what they believed was the greater good. Government and secret service eventually took notice. Off-the-record missions began.

Jaden started investigating the people giving them missions. He discovered Bio Genetix was the funder behind everything. The Mandem had been weaponised without knowing it.

At 18, Jaden left home to protect his family. Kevin was 3. The departure was framed as rebellion to Devon and Jon; the real reason was that Jaden had to disappear in stages.

At 20, Jaden created the Loyalty Elixir from the Book. A contingency. He obtained Jon's blood through a feigned healing technique and Devon's through a staged sparring match. Neither knew.

At 21, Jaden faked his death. The Elixir activated. Three months of no contact later, Jon's and Devon's memories of the Mandem bond began to fade. Jaden's family was told he had been murdered.

Jaden has spent the seven years since operating in the shadows: investigating Bio Genetix, watching his family from rooftops, intervening only when invisibility could be preserved. He rigged Jon's double-sided coin so Jon would stay (an act of preservation amid the larger erasure). He has not made contact with anyone he loves.

Episode 1 is Jaden's surface coming into contact with the surface world. He fights Spike in Central Danim, calmly, with full Tier 4 capability suppressed enough to look like a struggle. He protects bystanders. His burn mark is exposed when his hand rests on the window frame and Spike notices. Jaden does not panic; the seed is now planted for Face to recognise him eventually. At the end of the episode he watches Kevin's bedroom window from a rooftop.

Personality

Calm. Always. Completely unbothered, even mid-fight.

Strategic. Ten steps ahead. Reads the city like the chess problem it has become.

Adaptive. Sees options others don't. The "Daps" name comes from this.

Family-first. Everything he does protects his family, even though they don't know he exists. The moral weight of the choice he made (faking death, erasing his brothers' bonds) is the central wound he carries silently.

Doesn't perform mercy. The "Please... just leave" to Spike in Episode 1 is offered genuinely. Jaden would rather Spike walked away than escalate. He escalates only when the alternative is worse.

Doesn't taunt. Doesn't gloat. Doesn't narrate his own competence. Speaks rarely. When he speaks, it lands.

Carries the moral weight of being the architect. The Elixir was his choice. The faked death was his choice. He chose to remove himself and to remove his brothers' memories of him in service of a longer game. He doesn't apologise for it but he carries it.

A genius pretending to be a ghost.

Motivation

Three-phase arc.

Phase 1 (pre-series and Season 1). Protect family from the shadows. Investigate Bio Genetix. Stay invisible. Intervene only when no one else can. Watch Kevin grow without being seen.

Phase 2 (end of Season 1 into Season 2). Reveal himself alive. The brother returns. The family is fractured by the truth. The Mandem reunion begins as the Elixir wall starts breaking.

Phase 3 (Season 2 to Season 3 finale). Lead the Mandem reunion. Restore the gold. Combine the trio. The combined ultimate against the Apex TANCs is the technique Jaden has been preparing for the entire seven years.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 4 (Radiant), possibly the most complete ninja of the Mandem. Gold aura. Warm, adaptive, fully visible when channelled.

Adaptive fighting style. The "Daps" signature. Reads opponents with what looks like precognition. Combat decisions made one or two beats ahead of where opponents are. Time appears to slow for him during fights.

Multi-pillar mastery. Bible §3 doesn't explicitly pin Jaden to a single pillar. His adaptive cognition reads as Mind-pillar dominant, but his physical economy (the displacement that doesn't make a sound, the catching of his own thrown knife in the same hand without looking up) reads as Body-pillar advanced too. Recommended canon: Jaden's mastery spans pillars; his "complete ninja" framing in the Bible supports this.

Tools and gadgets. Throwing knives. Sticky bomb devices. Glove with a deactivation button for the bombs (used in the Spike fight). Wrist cable / zipline implied by his rooftop movement.

Combined ultimate. The gold in the Mandem's combined Tier 5 (Transcendent) technique, achievable only with all three reunited. Form not yet locked.

For the power system, see World/Power System (Aura).md (to be created).

Key Relationships

  • Kevin Young (13, little brother). The reason for everything. Watches him from rooftops in Episode 1. The reveal that Jaden is alive lands on Kevin at the end of Season 1 and reshapes Kevin's Phase 3 motivation. Jaden's memories of Kevin go back to when Kevin was 3 ("playing in the backyard, though his brother's face has grown hazy with time").
  • Sharon Young (32, older sister). The childhood corner, his hand on her chest while he watched whatever was coming ("Don't move"), is in Jaden's bones too. She spiralled after his "death" and became a detective. He has watched this from the shadows and has not contacted her. The reveal will hit her with the full weight of what she lost and what she did with the grief.
  • Ivy (mum). Does not know he is alive. The hardest reveal. Jaden has watched her age without him.
  • Grandad. Does not know he is alive.
  • Devon / Face (30, brother). Tricked into the Elixir. Jaden bears the moral weight of erasing his brother's bond. The "Dappy" nickname is the private bond Devon called him by; Devon hasn't said it in seven years and will, eventually, again. Jaden has watched Face become a warlord and has not intervened.
  • Jon / Blade (29, brother). Same. Tricked, same erasure, same moral weight. Jaden rigged the coin so Jon would stay. A small act of preservation amidst the larger removal.
  • Trace (guardian of the Book). Connected to Endsworth School where the Book remains. Likely knows Jaden is alive. Possibly the only person who does. (See Open Questions.)
  • Bio Genetix. The investigation target. Jaden knows their structure, their funding sources, their TANC program. He is the only ninja with this intel.
  • The Japanese man. The Sphere's last carrier in Episode 1. Killed by an unknown shadow figure with a kunai in the alley. The killer's identity is a locked canonical mystery (per 2026-05-12 lock). Jaden's connection to the death, if any, is undetermined.

Arc

Season 1. Operates as cloaked figure throughout. Fights Spike in Episode 1's cold open. Protects bystanders. Watches Kevin from rooftops. Investigates Bio Genetix from shadows. (The alley kunai killing of the Japanese man is a locked canonical mystery; Jaden's involvement is undetermined.) The end of Season 1 is the reveal: Jaden alive. The audience and the family find out at the same time, or staggered (see Open Questions).

Season 2. Reveal himself to Kevin. Begin the Mandem reunion. The gold returns to the city. The Elixir wall begins breaking.

Season 3. Lead the Mandem ultimate against the Apex TANCs. The trio combines for the first time in over a decade.

Voice and Dialogue

Calm. Few words. Inner thoughts are detached observations. Spoken dialogue is direct, concise, often a mercy or a report. Doesn't taunt. Doesn't perform.

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

(V.O., mid-fight) "This isn't a fight." Pause. "It's a temper tantrum."

(V.O.) "This is what happens when you give power to those who haven't earned it."

"Don't move." To the woman and child. Calm. Not a trace of urgency. The line the woman remembers as making her feel safe, and the same two words he said to his sister as a boy. This is the episode's key clue and no other character may use the phrase (Spike's line to the cashier was changed to "Stay still" on 2026-08-13 to protect it).

(V.O., mid-flight toward the building) "Life seemed easier back then. Things like this were left to the military... maybe."

(V.O.) "What does it matter...? All the same."

"Please... just leave." To Spike after dismantling him. Genuinely offered. Mercy first.

"What a waste." On the rooftop after the fight, to himself. Survey of the destruction.

From the Spike flashback (the shop dismantling).

"I have triggered the alarm." Calm. Reporting.

"...And your face is exposed." Same register.

"Now you've completely caused attention to yourself." Quietly to himself after the bomb explodes Spike's cloak.

Pattern. Two-word fragments. Single sentences. Either a report or a mercy. Inner monologue is reflective ("Life seemed easier back then... All the same"), bordering on poetic, but always quiet. The poetry never tips into performance.

The mercy register. Jaden offers exits before he closes them. He gave Spike a chance to walk. He chose to act only when the kunai was the only remaining option for the Japanese man. The pattern recurs.

The Dappy nickname. Jaden is "Daps" to other ninjas (respect), "Jaden" to Blade (sees the person, not the ninja), and "Dappy" only to Face in private memory. He never calls himself Dappy. The name lives with Face.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Status: alive or dead. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Jaden as deceased ("Age: 24 (deceased)"). Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf has Kevin describing Jaden as murdered. Series Bible has Jaden alive, faked his death seven years ago. CANON: alive. The "Kevin believes he is dead" framing is the in-show position; the audience learns Jaden is alive in Episode 1 (the Watcher beat) and the reveal to Kevin lands at the end of Season 1.

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Jaden at 24 (deceased). Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Jaden at 28. CANON: 28. Master timeline (Jaden 12 when Mandem met, met 16 years ago, Jaden now 28) is consistent.

Cause of leaving home. Old Archive/Characters.pdf "rebellious and left home at 18 to protect his family from his journey." Series Bible: left home at 18 after discovering Bio Genetix was the funder behind the Mandem's missions. CANON: Bible. The "rebellious" framing is Kevin's family's understanding (a protective cover); the real reason is the Bio Genetix discovery.

Cause of death. Old PDF "reported dead at 24" with Sharon driven to find the killer. CANON: Jaden faked his death. No killer existed. Sharon's belief in a killer drives her arc but the truth is the Elixir contingency.

Ninja name. Both sources agree on "Daps." CANON: Daps. The "Dappy" private nickname is Face's only; the "Jaden" register is Blade's only.

Loyalty Elixir creation, Bio Genetix investigation, Jon's coin rigging. Not in old Archive/Characters.pdf. Added in Series Bible. CANON: Bible additions are locked. These are load-bearing for Jaden's arc.

Aura colour. Old PDF silent. Bible specifies gold (warm, adaptive, the light between Jon's blue and Face's black). CANON: Bible.

Adaptive fighting style. Bible adds the "almost precognition-like" framing as the source of the "Daps" name. CANON: Bible.

Who killed the Japanese man in the alley. Episode 1 leaves this as "an unknown shadow figure." Series Bible doesn't explicitly assign. CANON (locked 2026-05-12): the mystery is preserved. The shadow figure that throws the kunai is deliberately unidentified. Could be Jaden. Could be someone else. Could be a force not yet introduced. The audience does not know. The characters do not know. This is an open canonical mystery the show will resolve when the story is ready.

Multi-pillar mastery. Bible §3 doesn't explicitly pin Jaden to a single pillar. RECOMMENDED CANON: Jaden's mastery spans pillars (Mind-pillar dominant, Body-pillar advanced, Spirit-pillar functional). Supports the Bible's "possibly the most complete ninja of the Mandem" framing.

Live threads planted in E1

  • The RIP wall (planted 2026-08-13, payoff DEFERRED to a later episode on Bupe's instruction). A faded memorial piece on the end wall of Kevin's block, with dead flowers cable-tied to the drainpipe. In E1 it is deliberately unreadable and passed in half a second; Kevin has never once looked at it. A later episode reads it properly. Do not spend it before then. The obvious strongest use is a shot that puts Jaden himself in frame with his own memorial, since he is the one man in Danim who can stand in front of that wall and know it is a lie.
  • The shelf. Photo, memorial card (IN LOVING MEMORY / JADEN YOUNG), and a candle blackened from use, in the family kitchen. Ivy straightens the card without looking at it. This is where the audience first reads his name.

Open Questions

  • When Jaden reveals himself to Kevin vs Sharon vs mum vs Jon. The reveal at end of Season 1 is locked, but the order of who learns Jaden is alive (Kevin first? Sharon and Kevin simultaneously? Jon ahead of the family because his memories return through Kevin? Mum last?) is unlocked. Worth mapping for Season 1 finale structure.
  • Trace's awareness. Does Trace know Jaden is alive? Are they coordinated through the Book / Endsworth School connection, or independent operators? If coordinated, Trace becomes a key Jaden ally pre-reveal.
  • The double-sided coin's origin scene. When Jaden rigged the coin so Jon would stay. Bible mentions this happened in their youth. Worth writing as a flashback scene at some point.
  • Sharon and Jaden's reunion. The corner flashback is the emotional core. The adult reunion needs an equivalent moment. When and how?
  • Kevin's father vs Jaden's father. Kevin's father canon (resolved 2026-05-11): never came home, mum told Kevin he died before Kevin was born. Jaden is 15 years older than Kevin. Does Jaden remember his father? Same father? Different fathers? Knows more than Kevin about the absence? Worth deciding.

Backstory

Jonathan Clark was born in Danim City 29 years ago. As a child he was exposed to the Hakai Sphere's diluted potential through the school water contamination, like Devon and Jaden, though none of them knew it.

At 13, in detention, he met Devon Jakes (14) and Jaden Young (12). Together they found the Book in the school library. Together they trained. Together they became the Mandem: the gold (Jaden), the blue (Jon), the black (Devon).

Jon mastered blades. Swords, knives, shurikens. Body-pillar primary, with the discipline of someone who trained because the work demanded it, not because he liked attention.

Jaden faked his death seven years ago. The Loyalty Elixir activated after three months of no contact with the Mandem. Jon's deep memories of Devon began to fade. He was left with guilt he couldn't explain and a feeling of loss he couldn't name. He withdrew from the ninja world. He opened Uncle Jon's Barbershop on the Central/South Danim border. He kept Jaden's double-sided coin and never told anyone what it meant.

He has been running the barbershop ever since. The back room has a small deadbolt that no other barbershop has, and certain people walk straight through without sitting down. The ninja world hasn't entirely let him go, even if he's let it.

Personality

Calm. Disciplined. Reserved.

Doesn't perform. The kind of man who works quietly and lets others fill the silence around him. Sleeze comes in loud; Jon stays still. The clippers move steadily.

Sharp wit when prompted. Doesn't engage in Sleeze's antics but lands single dry lines that close conversations: "More than I'd cut on yours if you're not paying." The customer in the chair stiffens; Jon doesn't react.

Notices everything but says nothing about it. Watches the back-room visitors in the mirror. Knows what they're there for. Doesn't speak it aloud.

Reluctant mentor. Kevin has been coming to the barbershop since childhood. Jon has watched him grow without naming the watching. When Kevin starts asking questions, Jon's first instinct is to deflect ("People talk too much"). The reluctance is real; the underlying willingness is also real.

Holds back his Aura. Tier 4 Radiant capability suppressed to Tier 2-3. He doesn't channel openly. The barber is the cover, not the truth.

Carries something he can't name. The Elixir erased the context, but Jon feels the absence of Devon as an unplaceable ache. He doesn't know why he kept Jaden's coin. He knows it matters.

Motivation

Four-phase arc.

Phase 1 (early Season 1). Avoid the past. Run the barbershop. Keep the back room running quietly. Don't engage with what was lost.

Phase 2 (mid to late Season 1). Reluctant mentor. Kevin's presence triggers flickers of memory. Jon resists. Then yields. The barbershop becomes the place where Kevin starts to learn.

Phase 3 (Season 2). Accept the past. Memories slowly return through Kevin's presence. Jon's body remembers fighting alongside Devon before his mind does. The Elixir's wall begins to fail.

Phase 4 (Season 3). Step back into the fight fully. The Mandem reunites. Jon picks up blades again. The combined ultimate is unleashed.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 4 (Radiant), suppressed. Operating at Tier 2-3 because he's holding back. Blue aura: calm, disciplined, controlled.

Master of blades. Swords, knives, shurikens. The Bible §3 places Jon's mastery in the Body pillar (physical training, precision, discipline). His blade work is the body trained beyond normal human capability.

Discipline. Combat philosophy is precision and economy. Doesn't waste motion. Doesn't escalate unless required.

Combined ultimate. Part of the Mandem's combined Tier 5 (Transcendent) technique, achievable only with all three reunited. Form not yet locked.

For the power system, see World/Power System (Aura).md (to be created).

Key Relationships

  • Devon / Face (30). The brother whose context the Elixir erased. Jon feels the absence as an unplaceable ache. They live in the same city and don't see each other. By Season 2 the memories return. By Season 3 the brother is reclaimed.
  • Jaden / Daps (28, presumed dead but alive). The brother who left. Jon carries Jaden's double-sided coin and doesn't fully know why. Jaden rigged the coin so Jon would stay (a quiet act of preservation amidst the larger erasure Jaden orchestrated). The reveal that Jaden is alive lands on Jon at the end of Season 1.
  • Kevin Young (13). Family barber relationship since Kevin was small. Calls Jon "Uncle Jon" without thinking about it. Jon notices something familiar in Kevin's posture and movement (Jaden's gait, traces of the Young family pattern) but can't place it. By Season 2 the recognition crystallises.
  • Sleeze (late 20s). Regular at the shop. Friction is performance for both of them; the underlying relationship is solid. Jon's deadpan is the perfect foil for Sleeze's noise. (See Characters/Sleeze/Sleeze.md, to be created.)
  • The back-room visitors. People who walk straight through without sitting down. Nodded at, never named in Episode 1. The barbershop is a junction node for an ongoing ninja-world network Jon hosts without active engagement.
  • The Mandem (historical). The defining trio of his youth. Officially dissolved when Jaden "died." Functionally erased from his explicit memory by the Elixir. Functionally still present in his body and his blue aura.

Arc

Season 1. Reluctant mentor. Kevin starts asking. Jon's clipper pauses when triggers come up. The back room operates quietly. End of Season 1, the reveal that Jaden is alive hits Jon as hard as it hits Kevin, and the second crack in the Elixir wall begins.

Season 2. Memories return. Jon picks up blades for the first time in years in a moment that forces his hand (specific moment not locked). The reunion with Devon is the load-bearing emotional beat of Jon's arc.

Season 3. The Mandem fully restored. Jon channels Tier 4 Radiant openly. The combined ultimate against the Apex TANCs.

Voice and Dialogue

Economical. Two- or three-word lines. Dry. Doesn't perform. Smirks barely (just the corner of his mouth) when his customers earn it.

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

"Kev." Greeting Kevin. One syllable.

"Sleeze." Greeting Sleeze flatly. Same energy.

"What does it look like?" When Sleeze asks if he's busy. Doesn't dress the answer.

"More than I'd cut on yours if you're not paying." Without looking up. The customer in the chair stiffens.

"What have you done for this shop?" When Sleeze invokes loyalty.

"I can put a price on a haircut though. Fifteen pounds."

"How's your mum?" / "And your grandad?" The check-in. Same two questions every visit.

"Smart man." To Kevin's grandad story about waking before the sun.

"Come." Inviting Kevin into the chair.

"People talk too much." / "And I'm just saying people talk too much." Cuts off Sleeze's Central Danim incident chatter. The second repetition is the real warning.

"Good?" After the cut.

"Straight home." Last thing to Kevin. Doesn't enforce, doesn't elaborate.

The clipper pause. Jon's body language tell. When Sleeze mentions the Central Danim incident, Jon's clippers pause for a fraction of a second. So brief that Sleeze and his boys don't catch it. Kevin does. The pause is Jon's wrist-tell equivalent (parallel beat to Face's wrist drift) and is a recurring visual cue across the show.

The double-sided coin. Physical anchor. Jon still carries it. The coin doesn't appear on screen in Episode 1 but is referenced by the Bible. A future episode will surface it.

What Jon doesn't say. The barbershop scenes are built on what Jon doesn't address. Sleeze gets the comedy; Jon gets the unspoken weight.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Jon at 27. Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Jon at 29. CANON: 29. Master timeline (Jon 13 when Mandem met, Mandem met 16 years ago, Jon now 29) is consistent.

Ninja name. Both sources agree: Blade. CANON: Blade. Locked.

Reputation. Old Archive/Characters.pdf frames Jon as "highly respected in the local community, both for his ninja skills and for his moral leadership" and openly known. Series Bible frames Jon as having "withdrawn from the ninja world" with his past largely private. CANON: Series Bible. Jon is known as the barber. The ninja past is private knowledge among the underground. The back-room network suggests certain people know, but the general public sees a barbershop, not a former Mandem ninja.

Skills. Old PDF "Master of blades, intelligence and strategy." Bible adds Tier 4 Radiant suppression, Body-pillar mastery, blue aura. CANON: Bible additions locked. The old PDF base remains intact (master of blades is preserved).

Personality. Old PDF "Avoids trouble, cares deeply for community, takes teachings seriously." Bible adds the Elixir-erased context and the reluctant-mentor framing. CANON: layered. Old PDF traits remain. Bible adds the underlying ache.

Aura colour. Old PDF silent. Bible specifies blue (calm, disciplined, controlled). CANON: Bible.

Jaden's double-sided coin. Old PDF silent. Bible adds. CANON: Bible. Locked as a physical anchor for a future scene.

City spelling. Old PDF Jon entry uses "Denim City" once when describing his community role. CANON: Danim City. Original PDF unchanged as historical record.

Open Questions

  • The back room. Bible doesn't specify what's in there. Safehouse? Training space? Drop point for active ninjas? The deadbolt and the silent visitors point at something, but the specifics are undefined. Worth locking when we map Season 1 Episode 2 or 3.
  • The double-sided coin. Bible mentions Jon carries it and Jaden rigged it so Jon would stay. When does the coin first appear on screen? When does Kevin or Jon discover its significance? A future flashback to the original rigging moment in the Mandem's youth would be a strong scene.
  • Jon's first time reaching for a blade in the present timeline. When does Jon stop being a barber and start being Blade again? Season 2 likely, but the trigger moment isn't locked.
  • Jon and Sleeze's friendship history. The Episode 1 friction reads as long-standing. Was Sleeze ever part of the Mandem orbit? Or just a regular who happens to know Jon for decades?
  • When the audience learns Jon is Blade. The reveal could be in Season 1 (showing his blade skills to Kevin) or held back to Season 2 (the Mandem reunion arc). Bible suggests Season 2 leaning. Worth locking.

Backstory

Kevin is the youngest of the three Young siblings, brought up by his mother Ivy and his Jamaican grandfather in North Danim (Wood Green, Edmonton, Tottenham energy). His father is absent (see Discrepancies section). His older brother Jaden left home when Kevin was three and was reported dead when Kevin was six. Kevin does not know that Jaden faked his death and is alive, operating as the cloaked figure Daps. His sister Sharon, nineteen years older, spiralled after Jaden's "death" and eventually became a detective.

HIS FATHER (Bupe, 2026-08-27). Kevin never knew his father, and neither did Sharon. Stated once, briefly, flat, as an acceptance the family lives with rather than a wound anybody is working through. Deliberately under-explained: there may be a story behind it later, so nothing elaborates on it yet.

Kevin's earliest memories of Jaden are hazy fragments. Playing in the backyard. His brother's face indistinct now. He has been going to Uncle Jon's Barbershop since childhood, brought there by his mum. Jon is the family barber, the kind of figure who has known Kevin long enough that Kevin calls him "Uncle Jon" without thinking.

What Kevin doesn't know yet. His world is built on hidden things. Jon was once Blade, one of the legendary Mandem ninjas. Sharon is investigating ninja activity she doesn't yet understand. Jaden is alive and watching Kevin from rooftops. And Kevin himself has now swallowed the Hakai Sphere, an ancient prison containing pure destructive consciousness, mistaking it for a sweet.

Personality

Curious. Brave. Awkward. The kind of kid who notices things and stores them. While Jon is cutting his hair, Kevin's eyes track the back-room door with the unusual deadbolt, the man who walks straight through without sitting down, and Jon's micro-pause when Central Danim is mentioned. He does not say anything. He just files it away.

Stands his ground when it counts. Watched a stranger his own age (Donte in the LIT hoodie) put four kids on the ground, and instead of being scared, he ran outside to look for him. Then walked back home with a question lodged behind his teeth.

Fumbles real things. The burning question to ask Jon to teach him how to fight survived the entire bus ride and barbershop visit before being completely buried under Sleeze's noise. Kevin is the kind of kid who needs three or four runs at the brave thing before he gets it out.

Easily scared but not easily broken. The Hakai Scare in his mum's bedroom is a full-body, throat-shredding panic. He does not pretend otherwise. But he keeps moving the next day. He doesn't tell anyone what he saw.

Shrugs at chaos that isn't his to fix. Sees three men chasing one down the street, watches without changing his face. "Danim." Pops a sweet. Watches Hella shout at a bus driver about a wank break, headshakes silently. "Danim." Pops the earphones in. This is now a recurring beat.

Carries the family loss quietly rather than performing it. Added to E1 on 2026-08-13 as a bus voiceover: his dad passed when he was young, his older brother Jaden was murdered, "that's what they told us, anyway", the killer was never found, and Sharon left and joined the police to get justice for him before the case went cold. Kevin states it the way a thirteen-year-old does, flat and without self-pity, and then moves straight on to the barbershop, which is how he copes. He was six when he was told Jaden was dead, so his account is honest but incomplete; he does not know about Sharon's spiral, and the audience should feel the gap.

Favourite superhero: Perfect (locked 2026-08-13, Bupe's call; see the Bible's In-World Popular Culture entry). This is the character Grandad uses to teach him why you protect a stranger, and it is the seed of Kevin's whole moral position. Not yet written into a script; it belongs to the Grandad scene from the 2024 Chapter 8 draft.

Motivation

Five-phase evolution from the Series Bible.

Phase 1 (early Season 1). Curiosity. Something's not right. He wants to understand. The LIT hoodie boy's impossible fight, the back room at Jon's, the news on TV about Central Danim. He just wants to know what's actually happening in his city.

Phase 2 (mid Season 1). Protection. As the world reveals itself, Kevin's motivation shifts from "I want to know" to "I want to keep the people I love safe." Mum. Grandad. Jon.

Phase 3 (end of Season 1 into Season 2). Truth. The reveal that Jaden is alive lands. Kevin wants answers. Why did Jaden fake his death? Why didn't anyone tell him? What does his brother actually do?

Phase 4 (Season 2 and into Season 3). Identity. Hakai delivers the Ultimatum and shows Kevin the vision of his dark future self. Kevin is now fighting two battles: the external one against TANCs and Face's crew, and the internal one against a prediction that says he will become a monster.

Phase 5 (Season 3 finale). Purpose. Kevin comes full circle. He's not fighting just for himself or for his family. He's fighting for everyone. The prediction breaks. Hakai is proven wrong through the people Kevin chose to love.

Powers and Abilities

Tier 1 (Dormant) at series start. Has not yet awakened any Aura. Reaches Tier 2 (Awakened) by the end of Season 1.

The crucial fact, hidden from every character including Kevin: he consumed the actual Hakai Sphere, not the diluted water that gave every other Danim ninja their potential. His ceiling is beyond anything ever seen. This is a slow reveal across the entire series. Nobody knows. Kevin doesn't know.

Aura colour: gold and white (locked 2026-06-03). Intensifies as he grows. See Theme Palette.

Inner entity: Hakai. A consciousness, not a power Kevin controls. Hakai takes Kevin's form but older, sharper, with completely void black eyes and a slight knowing grin. Hakai's personality across the series moves from cold and indifferent ("Pathetic." "Weak.") to antagonistic to dark mentor to mutual understanding. Hakai is bound to Kevin's life force. If Kevin dies, Hakai dies too. This is unprecedented.

For the full power system and Hakai entity behaviour, see World/Power System (Aura).md, World/Hakai Sphere.md, and World/Hakai (the Entity).md (to be created).

KEVIN'S POWER IS THE POWER OF WILL (added 2026-08-10)

Full mechanics in Series Bible section 4. The parts that govern how Kevin is written:

Every other ninja is judged on the same scale (how much Aura, which pillar, which tier). Kevin is the one exception, and the exception is not a bigger number. What he genuinely wants, happens. Not because his will is stronger than anyone's, but because his is the only will in the world wired to an amplifier.

The rule the audience is taught once and tracks forever: Kūga does not answer requests, it answers declarations. "Help me" contains doubt and dies in the air. "I will not let this happen" contains none and detonates. No matter how bad it gets, Kūga will not intervene for pain or pleading. Only for a thing Kevin ultimately, definitely, without a shred of doubt wants otherwise, and believes.

The asymmetry that IS his character arc: harm is cheap, good is expensive. A destructive flicker is already in Kūga's native language and needs almost no signal. Constructive will is foreign to him, so Kevin has to be deafening and any tremor of doubt kills it. Evil is a whisper, good is a scream, and Kevin is thirteen.

The intrusive-thought danger. If Kūga mimes a throat-cut and Kevin so much as pictures it, the throat opens in reality. His will was too weak to refuse the thought. Kevin's recurring nightmare is not the monster, it is his own mind not being his own to control.

His training is subtractive. Most shonen training adds; Kevin's first year is damage control. He must learn to think less before he can learn to think one thing completely. Clearing the mind is survival, not decoration.

He grows without power creep. Kevin never gets stronger and neither does Kūga. The only variable is how much he can hold without being rewritten: a flicker in Season 1, a decision by Season 3.

WHY HE SURVIVED SWALLOWING IT (added 2026-08-10)

Not luck. Chronology. The Springvale contamination ended 20 years before present day and Kevin is 13, so he was born seven years after the last contaminated bottle was drunk. Never write a lucky escape for this. If anyone asks, he wasn't born.

Why that is the protection. Everyone who drank the water carries a trace of Kūga, and Kūga resonates with its own signature, so every water-generation ninja is already partly Kūga. Had Kevin drunk it, the Sphere would have found a door already open in its own handwriting and consumed him in the first second. He has no trace, no signature, no door. He is the first host in history who is not already partly the thing inside him.

He is masked by default. An amplifier at rest emits nothing, so dormant Kūga has no signature to detect. Kevin is not hiding; there is genuinely nothing to find until he uses it. His power is his beacon, which means every time he reaches for it to protect someone he announces his position. The strongest thing on earth stays safe only by staying weak.

WHAT KEVIN SEES WHEN HE LOOKS AT TRACE (added 2026-08-10)

Not the truth, and not the lie. A mismatch.

Kevin is inside the gods' order: a living human, second generation, part of the world. Kūga is not. So Kevin's eyes do what everyone else's do and accept the ordinary lad playing football, while something inside him flatly refuses, and he cannot reconcile the two or locate where the wrongness is coming from.

Correct experience for him, because his whole arc is his own mind not being entirely his own.

Kūga knows exactly what it is and will not tell him. "You should look at that again." Bored, looking elsewhere, never explains twice.

And the reverse: Trace does not notice Kevin either, because an amplifier at rest emits nothing. Not for episodes. Not until the first time Kevin uses the power near it. Mid-game, the ball rolls past, and Trace does not follow the ball. Its rule is the triangle rather than the Sphere, so it does not act. It just notices. Full detail in Characters/Trace/Trace.md.

WRITING KEVIN WITH KŪGA (added 2026-08-10)

Kevin sees him walking about in the world and only Kevin can see him. Kūga can appear to hold someone by the throat and that person feels nothing.

Kūga's test pattern, which Kevin has to learn to survive: "I could just [mischief]", said to the ceiling, bored, never looking at him. Then the corner-of-the-eye check. Then, flat and cold, "Oh. Interesting." Every one of his jokes is a live test, so Kevin can never relax, and neither can the audience.

The comedy is Kevin's, and it costs him. He teaches Kūga slang. Kūga deploys it correctly at horrifying moments. Kūga finds pure hood talk tedious and would rather Kevin killed the person than kept talking like that. Kevin is, without meaning to, influencing a god, and every time it lands it is funny and wrong at once.

Theme Palette (locked 2026-06-03)

Signature colours: gold + white. Gold is bright and sunlit, distinct from Jaden's deeper, tarnished gold. White is the shared "still pure" thread across the next-gen trio. Black is Kevin's anti-colour, reserved for Hakai, kept out of his normal palette on purpose.

Wardrobe rule (the subconscious "that's Kevin"). Cream/off-white base streetwear with gold or mustard accents (drawstrings, chain, beanie or jacket lining, earphones). Reads natural for a North Danim 13-year-old and pops against Danim City's blue-grey.

Corruption tell. When Hakai is subconsciously taking over (mainly Phase 4, the identity battle), Kevin wears black with gold highlights. Same gold, dark ground. The audience reads the shift before it is spoken, the visual sibling of Face's wrist tell.

Aura. Gold and white, intensifying as he grows.

Cast colour map. Jaden gold / Jon blue / Face black (original Mandem); Kevin gold+white / Donte black+white / Uno green+white (Little Ninjaz).

Key Relationships

  • Ivy (Mum). The anchor. Hardworking, packs her bag for work in the morning, sharp with the spatula when Kevin tries to leave without a coat. Soft underneath. Steals food off his plate as a joke. Kevin pretends to be annoyed and hides a smile. The kitchen is hers. The relationship is loving and complete; the comedy and the threat coexist.
  • Grandad. Jamaican, retired, sits at the kitchen table with a cup of tea and the newspaper. Speaks rarely. When he does it sounds like proverbs that don't quite track. "You know in my day we wake up before di sun." Kevin: "Grandad, the sun's already up." Grandad: "Exactly." Doesn't move when Mum is being dramatic. A quiet presence.
  • Sharon (sister, 32). Detective. Lives separately. Kevin has not interacted with her in Episode 1. The audience knows Sharon is investigating ninja activity and has stolen a mini USB drive from a Bio Genetix front. Kevin does not. The two of them are siblings the audience knows are siblings; the world doesn't.
  • Jaden (brother, 28, presumed dead but actually alive). Kevin believes Jaden is dead. Kevin's memories of Jaden are hazy because he was 3 when Jaden left and 6 when the family was told Jaden had died. In Episode 1 Jaden watches Kevin's bedroom window from a rooftop. Kevin does not see him. The reveal that Jaden is alive is the end-of-Season-1 beat that drives Kevin into Phase 3.
  • Jon "Uncle Jon" / Blade. Mentor figure (slowly). Runs Uncle Jon's Barbershop on the Central/South Danim border. Has been cutting Kevin's hair since Kevin was small. Kevin notices Jon's tells: the clipper pause when Central Danim comes up, the people who walk straight through to the back room, the small deadbolt no other barbershop has. Jon does not know Kevin is paying attention.
  • Donte (LIT hoodie boy, 13). Watched him put four kids on the ground from his bedroom window. Has not met face to face. Does not know Donte's name. Kevin's first taste of "the world is bigger than I thought" is watching another kid his age move like that.
  • Hella (28). Met briefly at a bus stop. Doesn't know who she is. The encounter is comic on the surface (broken bus stop glass, condoms, the bus driver argument) but seeded with significance: Hella is Donte's biological mother. Kevin doesn't know any of this.
  • Sleeze. Knows Kevin from the barbershop. Calls him "little man." Kevin presses his lips together to keep from laughing during Sleeze's barbershop bits. For Sleeze's two-mode duality (clown around civilians, brawler when the work starts) see Characters/Sleeze/Sleeze.md (to be created).
  • Hakai (inner entity). Lives inside Kevin from the moment he swallows the Sphere in Episode 1. Appears for the first time during the Hakai Scare. Stage 1 personality: cold and indifferent. Will not engage with Kevin meaningfully until Season 2.
  • The 3 Little Ninjaz (future). Kevin, Donte, Uno. The next generation Mandem. Kevin mirrors Jaden in the original trio (the heart, the glue, family-first). This trio does not yet exist in S1E01.

Arc

Season 1. Discovers the ninja world through Jon and through the events around him. Swallows the Hakai Sphere in Episode 1. Has the first Hakai Scare. Establishes himself in the orbit of ninjas. Reaches Tier 2 (Awakened) by season end. Sharon's investigation crosses his path. Jaden reveals himself alive at the end of Season 1, which is the gut-punch that closes the season.

Season 2. Hakai speaks to him fully for the first time. The Ultimatum is delivered: master Hakai by manhood or be consumed. Hakai shows Kevin his dark future self. Kevin starts training seriously, mostly with Jon as the world starts to align. The 3 Little Ninjaz come together. Kevin starts to live with the prediction Hakai showed him.

Season 3. Kevin proves Hakai wrong through human bonds. Mum, grandad, Jon, his friends. The Mandem (Jaden, Jon, Face restored) and the 3 Little Ninjaz (Kevin, Donte, Uno) converge against the Apex TANCs. Kevin's full ceiling is reached. The prediction breaks. Hakai's first defeat in eternal existence is by a kid from North Danim who refused to become the thing it showed him.

Voice and Dialogue

Kevin talks and thinks like a 13-year-old actually thinks. Not narrated. Not poetic. Casual, internal, slightly dry. The Hood Ninjaz CLAUDE.md writing rule #3 is the standard: "Kevin's inner thoughts are casual. Like a 13-year-old actually thinks, not a narrator performing."

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

"Where are you..." Searching for a sock. Half question, half hope.

"...it'll do." After sniffing the sock. Three dots, full stop, one shrug.

"Safe, Uncle Jon" instead of "thanks."

"Be right back, mum" instead of "I'm popping out."

"Yeah yeah" when his mum says "Straight home." Not defiant. Just minimum compliance.

"Danim." The running beat. Said twice in Episode 1 in response to chaos he's chosen not to engage with. Once as Hella shouts at the bus driver. Once as he watches three men running down the street. Both times: small headshake, sweet pops in mouth, looks back out the window. This is now a recurring beat for Kevin.

"Huh?" Hella starts in on the crush bit. Kevin's default first response to anything weird.

"I want someone to teach me something." The only honest thing he says all episode. Spoken slowly, almost flatly. He doesn't know how to explain why.

The Hakai Scare is the absence of dialogue. Kevin doesn't narrate his panic. Breathing in and out. Heartbeat. Screams. The camera holds on his face and his eyes do the work. He is not a kid who explains himself when it counts.

The burning question. Kevin walked into Jon's barbershop with one question. "Can you teach me how to fight." It survived the bus, the bus stop, even Hella with the condoms. It dissolved into Sleeze's circus. He's the kind of kid who fumbles real things. This pattern recurs.

Source contrast note. In the original Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf prose draft, Kevin's inner voice is more reflective and slightly literary ("Growing up in this part of Danim City wasn't easy..." and "It's funny how much time you can spend in a place without realising how important it becomes to you"). The current screenplay-format Episode 1 deliberately strips that out. Canon voice is the screenplay voice: simple, observational, dry. The novelistic interiority is not how Kevin sounds anymore.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Kevin at 14, soon to turn 15. Current Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Kevin at 13. CANON: 13. The master timeline only balances at 13 (Donte 13 also, both born 13 years ago; Devon 17 at Donte's birth; Devon now 30). The older age is retired.

Jaden's status. Old Archive/Characters.pdf and Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf both have Jaden as dead ("my older brother... murdered. That's what they told us anyway."). Series Bible has Jaden alive, faked his death seven years ago, operating as the cloaked figure Daps. CANON: Jaden is alive, Kevin believes he is dead. Reason: Jaden's reveal at the end of Season 1 is the load-bearing motivational beat that drives Kevin into Phase 3. Removing it removes the engine.

Kevin's father. Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf line: "My father passed away when I was young." Archive/Characters.pdf: "Kevin has never met his father." Series Bible: not addressed. CANON (resolved 2026-05-11): Kevin's father never came home one day when Kevin was very young. He was assumed dead. Kevin's mum told him his dad died before Kevin was born, to protect him from the truth. Kevin therefore believes he never met his father. This is a deliberate seed for a future reveal (Season 2 or 3) where Kevin learns the protective fiction. The Chapter 2 line ("passed away when I was young") is retired in favour of the Characters.pdf framing ("never met his father"), because the latter is what Kevin would say if he believes his mum's story. What actually happened to Kevin's dad is the held open thread (see Open Questions).

Sharon's motivation for joining the police. Old Archive/Characters.pdf and Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf both have Sharon joining specifically to find Jaden's killer. Current Series Bible has her channelling grief into the force more broadly, with the ninja case being her current assignment. CANON: Series Bible version. A personal-vendetta-from-day-one Sharon makes her too narrow; the broader trajectory lets her find the link to Jaden organically.

City name spelling. Archive/Characters.pdf uses both "Denim City" and "Danim City." Archive/Book/ chapters use "Danim City" consistently. Series Bible and Episode 1 use Danim. CANON: Danim City always. Every "Denim" reference in extracted source material is corrected to "Danim" as it lands in workspace files. Original PDFs in Archive/ are not modified (they stay as historical record). Denim instances found in old Kevin sources: none in Chapter 2 (consistent Danim); the Denim spellings live in Archive/Characters.pdf in the entries for Face and Brawla, not in Kevin's own entry.

Kevin's inner voice register. Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf writes Kevin in reflective first-person prose. Current Episode 1 strips this out and replaces with stripped-back screenplay observations. CANON: screenplay register. The novelistic interiority does not match the writing rules in Hood Ninjaz CLAUDE.md rule #3. Old voice is retired.

The fight Kevin watches from his window. Chapter 2 version has the LIT boy doing a sustained chokehold and "toying" with attackers. Episode 1 final version has him efficient and brutal, four kids down (one walking away) in seconds. CANON: Episode 1 version. The efficiency reads as more dangerous and matches Donte's anti-hero positioning.

News location of the Central Danim incident. Chapter 2 has the news anchor saying "an incident in South Danim." Episode 1 has it as Central Danim. CANON: Central Danim. The Bible places the Jaden vs Spike fight in Central Danim deliberately ("ninja fights here are rare and always make the news"). The South Danim version in Chapter 2 contradicts the city's geography logic.

Kevin's school. Series Bible places Kevin's school in North Danim but doesn't develop it. The Bible establishes that the Hakai Sphere water contamination happened in a Danim school 20-25 years ago, where the janitor/keeper hid both the Sphere (in the water supply) and the Book (in the library). Old Archive/Characters.pdf mentions Trace haunts "Endsworth School." CANON (resolved 2026-05-11): Kevin's school is the same school. Endsworth School (name retained from old notes). The water contamination ended decades before Kevin started attending, so the water he drinks now is clean. Kevin's exposure to Hakai is entirely via swallowing the actual Sphere in Episode 1, not via the school's water. The Book remains hidden in the library. Trace haunts this school as the guardian of the Book. This sets up a deliberate continuity thread: Kevin's school is the deepest layer of Hakai mythology in the show, and Trace's presence here becomes plot-relevant in future episodes.

Open Questions

  • Kevin's aura colour. RESOLVED 2026-06-03: gold and white (see Theme Palette and the decisions log). The earlier candidates (pure white, or no fixed colour echoing Hella) were set aside; gold ties him to Jaden and white keeps him in the next-gen "pure" trio.
  • What actually happened to Kevin's dad. Murdered? Ran? Still alive somewhere? Connected to the ninja world? The protective-fiction canon is locked (see Discrepancies and Decisions). The truth behind it is the question this open thread holds for the Season 2 or 3 reveal.
  • When Kevin first asks Jon directly to teach him to fight. The burning question survived Episode 1 unspoken. Does Kevin try again in Episode 2? Does the Hakai Scare derail it? Does it stay buried until something forces Jon to teach him anyway?
  • Whether Kevin tells anyone about the Hakai Scare. He does not in Episode 1. The episode ends with him asleep and the Watcher (Jaden) on the rooftop. Does he tell his mum the next day? Does he doubt his own senses and stay quiet? Does Hakai appear again before he can say anything?

Scrapbook ingest (2026-08-05, from the original "3 Little Ninjaz" doc, now retired to BIN)

Early-draft material worth keeping in view; pre-Bible, so the Bible and this profile win on any clash:

  • Abilities trio (to confirm before any script leans on them): Super Exp (prodigy-rate learning of techniques), Premonition (slight ahead-sight in battle), Instinctual Battle Intelligence (untrained tactical reading). NB Premonition overlaps Jaden's "Daps" adaptive near-precognition: either inherit it deliberately (brothers) or differentiate; do not let it drift in unexamined.
  • First-step beat (usable, strong): Kevin fending off local troublemakers by mimicking a stance he had only ever seen his late brother use, witnessed by Jon, who is shocked by the similarity to Jaden's technique. A prime candidate for the moment Jon decides to train him.
  • Superseded by newer canon: the doc's "Jaden passed away" framing (he faked it), and "Sharon moved out to become a detective driven by the unsolved murder of their brother" (usable as what she BELIEVED; her locked arc is the spiral-then-police redemption path).

WHY SHE WAS NEVER PROMOTED (Bupe, 2026-08-27). This is the centre of her.

Lucas made Marcia the same offer, two decades before he made it to Sharon.

She said no.

She said no to him and she said no to the others, to the sexual coercion, to the compliance, to the blackmail, every time it was put to her across twenty-three years. And it cost her exactly what she was told it would cost her. She made Detective Sergeant and then Detective Inspector fast, on work so undeniable it could not be stopped, and then she stopped, and she has been a DI for fifteen years while men she trained went past her.

She stayed anyway. Not out of hope. The force was the only place she knew how to make a difference, so she stayed inside a machine that had already told her what it thought of her, and did the work.

That is what broke her. Not one incident. Twenty-three years of being right and going nowhere.

SO LUCAS WAS NOT LYING TO SHARON, AND THAT IS WORSE

When Lucas told Sharon "no woman climbs the ranks here, not on merit, not on results, not in twenty years", he was describing his own handiwork accurately.

Marcia Boateng is the proof that he was telling the truth. She is sitting two floors up, frozen at DI, and she is what refusing costs.

Which sets up the cruellest arithmetic in the series:

  • Marcia refused, and was frozen for twenty years.
  • Sharon paid, and was fast-tracked.
  • And Sharon was going to be promoted anyway.

One of them paid for nothing. The other paid everything and got nothing. Neither transaction was ever real. The machine simply took what each woman was prepared to give and gave back whatever it felt like.

WHY SHE WROTE THE RECOMMENDATION, AND WHY IT IS UNBEARABLE

Marcia knew exactly what was going to happen in that office, because it had happened to her.

The accelerated-promotion recommendation is not admiration filed for the record. It is a rescue attempt. She was trying to get Sharon promoted through the proper channel, fast, to put her out of Lucas's reach before he got to her.

She was too late by a matter of weeks.

And she could never say so, because saying so means saying what happened to her, out loud, in a building where she has to keep working. So she watched a woman get charged the price she had refused to pay, and she went back to her desk, and she filed things.

THE ARC OF UNDERSTANDING (Bupe's instruction, and it is the shape of the whole relationship)

The audience must arrive at this slowly and on their own. Bupe: for the longest time Sharon is certain Marcia hated her, then realises Marcia was intentional, and the audience picks up on the admiration underneath.

How it must be paced:

  1. Season 1: Marcia is cold and obstructive and there is no clue otherwise. No warm beat, no hesitation, no music. The audience should believe she dislikes Sharon, because Sharon does.
  2. The file: intentionality. Two documents, one signature. The first thing Sharon understands is not that Marcia cared. It is that Marcia was deliberate. Everything that looked like obstruction was aimed.
  3. The tape: the correction. "I did tell you. I told you in writing, twice, and you were not looking." Still no affection. She is not being kind, she is being accurate.
  4. After the death: Sharon investigates her. Bupe's beat. Sharon goes looking through Marcia's own history, the way Marcia went looking through hers, and finds twenty-three years of a woman refusing, and being punished for it, and not leaving.
  5. Understanding, not forgiveness. Sharon ends up respecting a perspective she spent years resenting, and the respect is retrospective and unreturnable, because the woman is dead and would not have accepted it anyway.

The admiration was always mutual and neither of them ever said it. Marcia admired Sharon enough to try to save her career. Sharon admires Marcia only once it is far too late to be any use to her.

The two documents## The two documents

Both in Sharon's own file. Both signed by Boateng. Sharon finds them at the same time and neither is addressed to her.

1. The recommendation, dated before the office. A plain accelerated-promotion recommendation for PC Sharon Young. No drama, no adjectives, the flat institutional language of a woman who learned early that flat language is the only kind that survives. She had already earned it. It was already moving. Lucas knew.

2. The objection, dated the day Sharon was made lead. Boateng put it on the record that a Detective Constable had no business being appointed to a PIP 3 investigation, and that appointing her exposed her to risk she could not be expected to manage.

"I ask that this be recorded."

That is the whole character in six words. She knew she would be overruled. She wrote it anyway, so that one day it would be findable.

Why Sharon thinks she is an enemy

Boateng blocks her. Queries her expenses. Pulls her up on disclosure and on her decision log. Refuses her requests for resources. Never smiles at her, never has.

Every one of those is protection. She is keeping Sharon off things that will get her hurt or exposed, and she is doing it in the only language she has: procedure. She is not warm, because warmth was a thing she could not afford at 24 and never got back.

Why she never just tells her

She tried once, years ago, with another young officer. She warned her directly, out loud, off the record, because it was the decent thing. That officer is not in the force any more and Boateng does not talk about it.

So now she only ever acts on paper, where it cannot be denied later and cannot be traced to a conversation. It is cowardice and it is also the only thing that has ever worked, and she knows both of those things at once. She has been quietly and ineffectually protecting people for a decade, and she despises herself for how little it achieves.

Integration. LOCKED BY BUPE 2026-08-27.

E1: her name is uttered once and that is all. Planted in Nelson's dressing-down, where he is complaining about her: "Boateng's on my back about your disclosure again, and it ain't her I'm gonna hear it from, is it." The name arrives in the mouth of the man harassing Sharon, as an irritant, so the audience files her exactly the way Sharon does. She does not appear and nobody explains who she is. Live in all three E1 files.

E3: integrated. Not on screen. Her recommendation is the page in the open file on Lucas's desk while Sharon is on her knees. The camera sees it, Sharon does not. The document that eventually ends Sharon exists from this episode onward and nobody has looked at it.

Season 1: pure friction. Blocks, queries, disclosure, never a smile. Played completely straight, no tipping, no music cue. The audience is invited to dislike her.

The turn: Sharon finds the file. Two papers, one signature.

Later: SHE SURVIVES, and Sharon comes to her. Bupe's call. Somewhere down the series Sharon goes looking for her, needing help, and going means saying out loud what she did in that office to the one woman who never had to. Sharon eventually thanks her.

THE END OF HER: an apparent suicide, and it is not one (Bupe, "somewhere later on"). Sharon finds her dead. It reads as suicide. There is a note.

Why this is the cruellest possible ending for this particular character, and why it is right:

  • Her only weapon in twenty-three years was paper, and she is killed with a piece of paper. The last document with her name on it is a forgery.
  • It is Lucas's register exactly. He does not do violence, he does procedure. A staged suicide is a finding, a file, a conclusion, and a closed case.
  • And it is the final test of the one talent that has defined Sharon since Lucas first named it. She reads between the evidence. Now the evidence is her friend's body and a note in handwriting that either is or is not hers. Everyone in that building will accept the note. Sharon will not.
  • Which puts her exactly back where E3 left her: certain, correct, and believed by nobody. The alley, again, with a body in it.

THE COUNTER, and it is set up by everything she has ever done: Boateng writes it down twice. A woman who ends an objection with "I ask that this be recorded" does not go quietly and leave one document behind. If she saw it coming, the real record is somewhere else, and finding it is Sharon's job.

DESIGNED 2026-08-27 to Bupe's spec, full chain in Scrapbook/Threads/boateng-trail-and-bio-genetix.md. Headline: she does not hide anything, she files everything, inside processes legally obliged to keep it. She names Sharon disclosure officer on a dead case weeks before she dies, so a file must reach her by law months later. The file is wrong, and Marcia Boateng did not make filing errors in twenty-three years, so the impossibility is the message. The errors encode a reference; Nelson accidentally hands Sharon the key while eulogising Marcia's pedantry; the reference is a records retention box; the box holds an original carrying nothing but an indentation, read at a raking angle with a pencil, because the machine that does it properly is in the building she cannot ask. And the tape is in lost property, handed in with a receipt, because the safest place for a secret is inside a process.

Craft rules

  • She is never a mentor and never gets a warm scene. If she softens, the character is dead.
  • She never explains herself. The documents do it, years late.
  • Her language is procedural even when it is love. That is the whole point of her.
  • She and Sharon should share as few scenes as possible before the reveal, so that when the audience goes back, there is almost nothing to re-read, and what little there is turns out to have been the truth all along.
  • Discovery Law applies: she is not introduced. She is a rank and a surname on a door, and somebody says it out loud when they are annoyed.

Open

All three of Vision's earlier questions were answered by Bupe on 2026-08-27: she is named in E1 (done), she survives and Sharon comes to her and thanks her, and she dies later in an apparent suicide with a note.

What is still open:

  1. Where the second record is, the one she wrote because she always writes it twice, and how Sharon finds it.
  2. Whether the note is in her handwriting. A forged hand, a coerced hand, or her own words written under duress are three different scenes.
  3. When it happens. Bupe: "somewhere later on." Not Season 1.
  4. Whether Sharon ever proves it. Vision's read: not to the force. Only to herself, and to whoever is left who matters.

Tier B profile, created 2026-08-10. Earned by being the single origin of the only power in the series that does not descend from Kega or Kūga. Source material: Bupe's original "Sera's Life Before Tribal" doc (written some time ago, Drive), plus his 2026-08-10 calls in session. Where the two disagree, the 2026-08-10 calls win.

Backstory

Raised by an abusive father after her mother died young. Violence, hatred and corruption daily, including nights he touched her. She grew up wishing him dead and fantasising about how, and holding onto the last of herself.

At 19 a school friend, seeing the emptiness in her, pushed her toward a church.

Elliot Jones was everything her father was not. Late thirties, handsome, kind, genuinely charismatic. She fixated. For weeks she tried to make him notice her and he stayed kind and completely distant, treating her exactly like everybody else.

He was the real thing, and that matters. He should be shown doing something specifically, unshowily good for somebody else, ideally a child, with Sera watching. It is the moment that proves he was not a hypocrite, and it makes what she does to him worse rather than more deserved.

Researching how to be wanted, she found books on witchcraft and voodoo in Danim. She dismissed them, then did not. What held her was not love spells. It was control.

The photograph. She let herself into his office early one Sunday. On the desk, a holiday photo of the priest kissing another man. The man she had spent months building a future around was never going to want her, and it had nothing to do with anything she could change.

Something in her closed. She spent the next week preparing the ritual.

The cost. The ritual required a sacrifice, and she paid it with the only clean thing she owned: a keepsake of her dead mother. She burned the one good memory she had to buy a man who was never going to want her.

The ritual. The following Sunday, after the service, in his office. She spoke a language he did not recognise. His eyes rolled white and he stood like a puppet.

Then the death. As it ended his eyes cleared, and he understood, and he had time to ask what she had done. Then the second half of the spell took him: the air would not come, and his body drained where he stood. Skin shrivelled, eyes hollowed. Within minutes he was a dried husk on the floor.

She watched, cold, and felt she had got what she wanted.

The Aftermath

Weeks later, pregnant. Conceived in the ritual, not after it.

The police could not explain the death, suspected poison, found nothing conclusive, and arrested her anyway. Inside, the rumours started immediately: that she was a serpent, that she could kill by touch. The baby was taken at birth. She has never seen him.

THE ISLAND, AND WHAT HER POWER ACTUALLY DOES (locked 2026-08-12)

The prison is on a small island, and the island is only the prison. Nothing else on it.

Tribal has never tried to get her out, and it is not sentiment, it is common sense: breaking into an island prison is heat he does not need, for a woman who would have walked out decades ago if she wanted to. He knows that. He has always known that.

So the answer to the long-open question is yes: Tribal knows she could leave. He has known his whole adult life. Every single day she chooses the island over him, and he is aware of it every single day.

Her power inverts the entire Aura system

This is why her arc needs delicate depth: Aura is not a defence against her, it is a meal.

Aura is life energy in a living body. Her power eats life energy. Therefore the stronger a ninja is, the more there is to take, and a blazing Tier 4 aura is the richest target in the room rather than the safest.

That single fact breaks every fight the audience has learned to read, which is exactly why she cannot be on the board casually. The moment she is in play, the power system the audience understands stops working.

And the accidental counter is beautiful: someone with no Aura at all is nearly worthless to her. Dormant, untrained, unawakened. Kevin is the least nutritious person in Danim City.

The release

She is never broken out. She serves her sentence and walks out the front gate with paperwork.

She would have been eligible for parole decades ago and has declined it every time, or quietly sabotaged every hearing, which is consistent with everything else about her: the prison was never holding her, and the paperwork was a formality she kept refusing. When the tariff finally expires there is nothing left to serve. They have to let her go, and she has no reason left to refuse.

This is when Tribal finally learns how powerful she truly is, because until then he has only ever had the story.

Timing: OPEN (Bupe). Recommendation, not locked: not Season 1 or 2, because Tribal's arc needs her absent to work, and it is a bomb you only get to drop once. The strongest placement is Season 4, while everyone is looking at Kega. The whole world is dealing with a god, and the most dangerous human being alive is released on an ordinary Tuesday with a travel warrant, and nobody is watching.

SHE STAYS BY CHOICE (locked 2026-08-10)

She could walk out any day and nothing anybody has could stop her. She does not. This is the hinge of the whole character.

The reason on the surface: the prison is a larder. She drained the priest and she never stopped. That is why she has not aged in forty years and why she looks late twenties at fifty-nine. A prison is a population that cannot leave and that nobody counts carefully. She is not serving a sentence, she is grazing, slowly, for decades. "Enjoying the chaos of her environment" is literal.

The reason underneath: the last time she wanted something, she got exactly what she asked for and it destroyed everything. So she has stopped asking for anything at all. Staying is the one arrangement where she never has to want again.

The Serpent of Danim. The reputation is not atmosphere, it is evidence of her feeding leaving a mark on the building. Guards avoid her corridor. The cold in it does not match the rest of the wing. Light behaves wrongly near her cell. Inmates who spend time near her get thin and tired and cannot say why. Nobody has ever proved anything.

WRITING NOTE. Bupe's framing was that she is not locked in with everyone, everyone is locked in with her. That is very close to Rorschach's line in Watchmen, in the identical setting, so if the idea is delivered aloud it should be in her own register rather than as a punchy one-liner. She has a soft voice. She would say it softly, and it would be worse.

Appearance and Voice (locked 2026-08-10)

Appearance. Attractive, and nothing like her age. Reads as a woman stuck in her late twenties. Deliberately, unarguably seductive, and she knows exactly what it does to a room.

Voice. Sweet, low, seductive as a default. It snaps into frightening, screaming anger without warning and then drops straight back into the sweet register, as if the anger belonged to someone else who has now left. The snap-back is more frightening than the anger.

Damaged, and feared for good reason. Both at once. Never play her as only one.

Why She Matters to the Story

She is Tribal's wound, and she is the reason he does everything he does.

He was taken at birth. She is alive, uncaged in every way that counts, and in forty years she has never once come for him. She could have. She didn't.

That sits directly on top of the Power of Will system (Series Bible section 4): Sera's will is what made him exist, and she has never willed a single thing in his direction since. Everything Tribal reaches for is an attempt to be worth the only inheritance she left him, and the reaching is what eventually wakes a god.

Open Questions (Bupe)

  • When does she get out? Recommendation above (Season 4, while everyone is watching Kega). The arc itself is undesigned.
  • Has anyone else ever visited her? She is a fixed, permanent, unkillable source of information that any character could reach. Sharon investigating ninja activity would eventually find the Serpent of Danim.
  • The island needs a name.
  • Does she know what Tribal became?
  • What is she waiting for? She stopped wanting. Whether that ever changes is a Season 3 or 4 sized question.

Writing Notes

On staging the ritual (REVISED 2026-08-10 by Bupe, supersedes the earlier cut-away recommendation). Play it at full weight. Taking extremity to the edge is a Hood Ninjaz signature, and this scene does real work: it is the conception of a major character and the moment a person becomes a monster. The house calibration applies (Series Bible section 1): toward softcore, never explicit, and violence you feel rather than gore you look at, sitting between Attack on Titan and Mortal Kombat rather than anywhere near Chainsaw Man. The Seven Pillars ban shock value alone; this is not that.

On her magic feeling different. Aura is heat, light and crackle in a living body. Hers is the opposite in every sense: cold instead of hot, void instead of light, heavy silence instead of energy. The rule and the reason are in Series Bible section 3, "The One Power Outside The System: Voodoo".

The priest is ELLIOT JONES (locked 2026-08-12). Tribal's father.
