Backstory

Sharon Young is the eldest of the three Young siblings. Nineteen years older than Kevin, four years older than Jaden. Was a law student, on track for the legal profession.

THE TIMELINE, SET AS CANON 2026-08-27 for E3 and load-bearing. The old "two years ago I started my journey in the police force" is dead: verified against the real UK route, the Detective Constable Entry Programme runs four years end to end and uniform first, two years as a uniformed constable then two developing into a detective, and it requires a degree. So the honest route would have kept her in uniform until she was 31. She did not take the honest route. 19 the boyfriend and the best friend. 19 to 22 the party years, Jenny, the dead-end jobs. 23 road rage into law. 25 graduates, and Jaden "dies" the same week; the law firm; the spiral; the night. 26 "How hard can it be?", she applies. 27 starts, uniform. 28 she is noticed, and fast-tracked (see below). 29 a detective, years before the route allows it. 32, now, about three years a detective, and everybody in that building knows she skipped the queue.

Why this matters everywhere else: in Episode 1 Sharon is roughly ONE YEAR into being a detective. It explains without a line of dialogue why Nelson talks to her that way, why nobody at the station believed the alley, why a chief can hand her the biggest case in the city out of temper, and why she works it alone at home rather than with a team.

THE FAST-TRACK (Bupe, 2026-08-27). This is the spine of her corruption and it is canon.

At 28, still in uniform, SUPERINTENDENT TEDDY LUCAS (named by Bupe 2026-08-27; profile at Characters/Teddy Lucas/Teddy Lucas.md) closes a door on her with her file open. The door and the desk plate both say SUPERINTENDENT LUCAS, which is how the audience gets his name and his power at once. He tells her the truth: her talent is off the charts, she reads between the evidence, she holds detail nobody else holds. It is the first time in her adult life anybody has called her exceptional at anything.

Then he quotes the price. No woman climbs the ranks here, not on merit, not on results, not in twenty years. He is not propositioning her, he is reading out a tariff. She does it. She is fast-tracked. It works.

Why it is worse than the assault: the night was done to her, this she decided. She weighed it and she paid, because the year before had already taught her that saying no is a thing other people get to do. She is not a victim in that room, which is precisely why it never leaves her.

And it retro-loads a line that already shipped. In E1 Nelson circles her and says "What is it the Super sees in you? ...Or what is it he wants to put in you?", and she stares ahead and takes it. That is not a rumour. It is the truth, said by a man who thinks he is only being crude, and she cannot react because reacting is admitting it. The resentment around her in the force is correct that she was fast-tracked and completely wrong about what it cost.

AND SHE DID IT FOR NOTHING (Bupe, 2026-08-27). This is the second of the two things, and it is the knife.

Two things put Sharon where she is. One is her talent, and it is real: on that alone she was going to be promoted anyway. Any normal person with that file gets fast-tracked without anyone asking them for anything. Two is what she did in that office.

She eventually finds out the promotion was already coming. He knew, he said nothing, and he took the price anyway because the situation was there to be taken. It was never a transaction. It was a robbery dressed up as one, and she paid willingly and has carried it ever since as the shameful thing she traded herself for.

Retroactively this reshapes the whole character. Every silence she has swallowed in that building, Nelson included, was protecting a secret that was never even the reason. The one decision she cannot forgive herself for changed no outcome at all. And she is the detective who reads between the evidence, which is the exact talent he complimented: she solves her own case in the end, and the answer takes the ground out from under her.

How she finds out (Vision's proposal, Bupe's call): paperwork, not a confession. Her own file, the one file she never thought to work. A recommendation for accelerated promotion, signed and dated before the day in the office. No malice on the page. Just a date.

The plant is in E3 and she must not see it: the file sits open on his desk throughout, the camera gets a clear look and she never does, because she is looking at him and then at the door.

Where the payoff lands is Bupe's call. Canon has her switching sides in Season 2, and this is a strong candidate for what breaks her loyalty: not the corruption itself, but finding out she degraded herself for a promotion she had already earned.

INDICATED, ONE WORD FROM LOCKED. Canon already has a corrupt senior officer on Paul Mitchell's payroll feeding Sharon's intel to Bio Genetix (Bible s7). Bupe named Lucas as "this corrupt person", which strongly indicates they are the same man, but he has not confirmed it in as many words. If they are the same, which would mean the fast-track was never about sex alone: he bought a detective whose talent he had already measured. She thinks she paid once for a career. In fact she was recruited as an asset, and everything she has handed up the chain since has gone to Bio Genetix.

HER FATHER (Bupe, 2026-08-27). She never knew him, and neither did Kevin. Stated once, briefly, flat, as something the family lives with. Deliberately under-explained: there may be a story behind it later.

THE GRANDMOTHER IS CANON (Bupe, 2026-08-27). Alive through the early years and in the graduation photograph with her mum and grandad. Dies of old age, off screen, between the degree and the present. Bupe's note is that this one is not a trauma, and that is exactly its function: it is the only death in Sharon's life that was allowed to be normal, so she stands at that funeral knowing what a grief is supposed to feel like and knowing she was never given one for Jaden.

THE LAW FIRM IS CANON. She was taken on and lasted months after Jaden. She refused compassionate leave, came in the next morning, then stopped coming in at all. The degree is never used again, and Bupe's reason for keeping it is the point: it proves she knows the law.

THE WOUND NOBODY IN THE SHOW EVER LEARNS. She has a law degree, so on the night at the centre of her origin she knows the exact name of the crime being committed against her, what the evidence would need to be, and what a defence would make of the fact that she opened her own front door. She does not report it. Weeks later she joins the police. Every silence she swallows in the present, Nelson included, is bought there.

REWRITTEN 2026-08-13 (Bupe's call). The memory is now a fragment, not a scene, and it carries no names. Sometime in her childhood, running feet and a shout she could not make out, and a boy younger than her closing a hand round her wrist and pulling her round a corner. Brick against her back. His hand flat on her chest, holding her steady rather than holding her still, while he leaned out and watched whatever was happening beyond the corner. "Don't move." She got half a question out, "What are yo...", and he lifted one finger without looking at her and said "Shhh." Something happened out there. She never saw it. Then he began to turn back toward her, the light behind him, his face just starting to come out of shadow, and the memory thins and drains and she never sees that either.

She has no conscious access to it until the phrase is said again in Episode 1. The old version (a bus stop, older teenagers, Jaden named, several lines of dialogue) is superseded: Bupe cut the name so the audience assembles the family from clues, and cut the dialogue so it plays as a real fragment rather than a staged scene. The name Jaden is never spoken anywhere in Episode 1.

When she was 25, Jaden was reported dead. Sharon was finishing her law degree. She spiralled: substance abuse, party phase, lost purpose. The legal career stalled. Eventually she channelled her grief into joining the police force and rose to detective. By Episode 1 she has been clean for some time (recovering alcoholic) and has been assigned to the special ninja case task force.

What Sharon doesn't know:

  • Jaden faked his death. He is alive. There is no killer for her to find.
  • The senior officer who assigned her to the task force feeds her intel to Bio Genetix via Paul Mitchell. Her investigation is being weaponised to build TANCs.
  • The cloaked figure she briefly sees at the Episode 1 crime scene, the figure who said "don't move" to a witness, is her brother.

Personality

Complex. Emotionally scarred but disciplined.

Stone-faced when the work calls for it. Nelson harasses her openly; Sharon's hands tremble at her sides from suppressed rage but her face stays neutral. The bite comes later, under her breath, in private mutterings.

Sharp deductions. Reads scenes. Pieces evidence quickly. Resourceful enough to slip past three agents into a crime scene she has no authority to enter.

Carries her sexuality without performance. The wet-patch moment during the Boss Lady scene is involuntary, observed flatly, addressed practically ("Whatever"), and moved past. Sharon is comfortable with her body and her appetites; she just doesn't dwell.

Doesn't perform for anyone. The detective sharp inner monologue is just for her. The public face is professional, contained, taking the hits she has to take.

Trauma-shaped. The grief of Jaden's "death" is not surface but it's the geological layer beneath everything she does. The corner flashback in Episode 1 hits her with full body force when triggered.

Resilient. The bin landing, the torn blouse, the bleeding knees, the bare feet on cold metal, the wet concrete. She gets up. She runs. She keeps the drive. She doesn't make a fuss.

Motivation

Four-phase arc.

Phase 1 (early Season 1). Investigator. Following the ninja case. Believes she's serving justice. Building a file. Compiling incidents. Tracking patterns.

Phase 2 (end of Season 1). Betrayal. Discovers the senior officer's connection to Bio Genetix. Witnesses a TANC. Discovers Jaden is alive. Three revelations stacked.

Phase 3 (Season 2). Reluctant ally. Switches sides. Fights to undo the damage her investigation caused. The redemption arc begins.

Phase 4 (Season 3 finale). Witness to the reunion. Sees the Mandem reunite, fully understands the ninja code she had been on the wrong side of, finds her place in a world she now knows she misunderstood.

Powers and Abilities

Deadshot (marksman). Top-tier with firearms. Not on display in Episode 1 (she infiltrates unarmed), but established in the Bible as a defining skill.

Drunken master (martial arts style). A style that fits her recovery arc: trained while drinking, weaponising unpredictability and looseness. Self-taught or trained during her spiral years (source not locked).

Investigation skills. Trained detective. Pattern recognition. Evidence handling. Pursues leads aggressively, photographs notepads, photographs scenes, doesn't wait for warrants.

Resourcefulness. Bypasses security through improvisation rather than training. The ventilation grate, the window drop onto the bin, the bare feet on metal stairs. The drive theft is the throughline: she made the call, she got it.

Possibly water-exposed as a child. Bible §8 timeline: "Sharon (4-7) possibly exposed" to the contaminated water during the contamination window. Never trained. Functionally Tier 0 / Dormant. Recommended canon: she has the latent potential but has never awakened. Worth flagging if a Season 2 or 3 arc takes her there.

Key Relationships

  • Kevin Young (13, youngest brother). Nineteen-year gap. Lives separately. They still never meet in Episode 1, but as of 2026-08-13 she tries. Her first act at the crime scene is to ring him, and he does not pick up, because he is on a bus with his earphones in. That near-miss is the relationship in one image: she is frightened for him and he never knows it happened. The bond is intact but distant.
  • Jaden Young (28, middle brother, presumed dead but alive). The corner. The "don't move." The grief that reshaped her life. The reveal at end of Season 1 lands like a second loss before it lands like a reunion.
  • Ivy (mum). Distant in present day; Sharon lives separately. Partly answered 2026-08-13: Ivy now has her first speaking role in E1, on the phone at the crime scene. The exchange settles the register even though the Bible is still silent on the wider question. Sharon rings her without hesitation the moment she is frightened, calls her "Mum", and gets "Sharon, you're scaring me" back, so this is not estrangement. It is a daughter who does not visit and a mother who would still drop everything. Sharon ends the call on "Thanks, Mum" with her eyes shut. (Frequency of contact and whether there are Sunday dinners: still open.)
  • Grandad. Distant in present day. Same.
  • DS Nelson. Detective Sergeant, one rank above her (set 2026-08-27). Sexually harasses her in Episode 1. London cockney accent, the kind of man who takes up more space than he has earned. His contempt has teeth because he technically outranks her and she can do nothing about it. He envies what Lucas sees in her, and he is closer to the truth than he knows.
  • Superintendent Teddy Lucas (was "The Captain" until the rank pass of 2026-08-27; the American title is retired). Mentioned by Nelson with jealousy. Assigned Sharon to the special task force. The corrupt senior officer feeding her intel to Bio Genetix via Paul Mitchell (canon locked 2026-05-12). Sharon does not know this in Episode 1 and the reveal lands at the end of Season 1.

AND SINCE 2026-08-27 HE IS ALSO THE MAN SHE PAID FOR HER FAST-TRACK, WHICH MAKES THE MAY CANON MUCH WORSE. He did not simply find a useful detective and start milking her. He built her. He spotted the talent, told her the truth about it, quoted her a price she had already paid for in a different currency, installed her in CID, put her on the task force, and has been reading her work ever since. Every single thing about Sharon's career is his, including the one decision she is most ashamed of, and including the promotion she had already earned and never knew about.

  • DI Marcia Boateng. The one person in that building who has ever been on her side, and Sharon does not know it and does not like her. Boateng blocks her requests, queries her expenses, pulls her up on disclosure, and has never once smiled at her. Every block is protection. She wrote the accelerated-promotion recommendation years before the office, and she wrote the objection the day a DC was made lead, and both documents are in Sharon's file with the same signature on them. And she is not the disproof of the sentence Sharon paid for. She is the PROOF (Bupe, 2026-08-27). Lucas made Marcia the same offer two decades earlier and she refused it, and it cost her exactly what he said it would: she has been a DI for fifteen years while men she trained went past her. So when he told Sharon no woman climbs the ranks here, he was describing his own handiwork accurately. Marcia refused and was frozen. Sharon paid and was fast-tracked. And Sharon was going to be promoted anyway. One of them paid for nothing and the other paid everything for nothing. The recommendation was a rescue attempt: Marcia was trying to get her promoted properly and fast, out of Lucas's reach, and she was weeks too late. Sharon has walked past her door every working day and never asked her a single honest question. Her arc with Sharon, locked 2026-08-27: named once in E1 in Nelson's complaint, present in E3 only as the recommendation in the open file, friction through Season 1, then the file, then Sharon eventually goes to her for help and eventually thanks her. She survives all of that, and dies later in what appears to be a suicide, with a note. It is not one. Profile: Characters/Marcia Boateng/Marcia Boateng.md.
  • The Boss Lady. Government / Bio Genetix-adjacent figure at the Episode 1 crime scene. Stole the drive from Sharon. Sharon stole it back. Boss Lady doesn't know Sharon exists.
  • Bio Genetix. Investigation target. Sharon doesn't know yet. The connection becomes clear at the end of Season 1.
  • Paul Mitchell. Hidden adversary. Funds Bio Genetix. The corrupt senior officer is his asset. Sharon's intel passes through him.
  • The witness with the child. Sharon's questioning of the witness in Episode 1 ("don't move") is the trigger that opens the flashback. The witness is the catalyst, not the relationship.

Arc

Season 1. Investigator. Files the patterns. The Episode 1 drive heist. Builds dossier across the season. Discovers the corrupt officer link to Bio Genetix at the end of Season 1, witnesses a TANC, and discovers Jaden is alive (or the audience does, and Sharon learns it shortly after).

Season 2. Reluctant ally. Switches sides. Works against her former colleagues. Reckons with the fact that her investigation built the TANCs. The redemption arc begins.

Season 3. Witness to the Mandem reunion. Sees Jaden, Jon, and Face restored. Comes to understand the ninja code she had been on the wrong side of.

Voice and Dialogue

Sharp detective inner monologue. Cynical, resilient, dry. Doesn't perform for anyone. Public composure plus private bite.

Tonal markers from Episode 1.

"But sir, there is a man over... there." Public, alert, deferential. Snapped out of the moment too late.

"Sir!" Snapping to attention.

(To herself, photographing the building) "What is going on in this city? Am I just seeing things? Impossible things."

"Wait, what did you say? What did he look like? Did you see his face? How tall was he? What was he wearing? Did he say anything else?" The rapid-fire questioning after the flashback.

"Cloaked figure... don't move..." Mumbling, reading the notepad.

"Wait... what do you mean? He made that?" When the witness says the cloaked figure hurled into the building.

"Where are you guys from?" To the suited agents blocking the entrance.

"You're not gonna tell me. Fine. I'll be back."

"Shit." Whispered, when she spots the rear guard.

"Great." Rolling her eyes, leaning back against the wall.

"Judging where the hole is, it should be about the fifth floor." To herself, on the stairs.

(V.O.) "Is that even possible? I'm having a hard time just imagining it." Climbing the stairs with the witness's words on her mind.

"Yeah right, you horny bitch." Barely audible, during the Boss Lady scene.

"...Whatever." Flat, after the wet-patch moment. The most Sharon line in Episode 1.

"Stupid Nelson." Under breath.

"Probably why you never got a promotion." Muttering as she walks away.

"Great. That was new." After the blouse tears.

Pattern. Public deference plus private bite. Inner monologue is sharp and clipped. Sharon doesn't waste words inside her own head. The professional surface is the lie; the muttering is the truth.

The "don't move" trigger. The flashback is the only moment in Episode 1 where Sharon visibly loses composure. Her breathing changes. One hand goes to her chest. The flashback breaks her open for the span of a few seconds. She physically shakes it off and powers through. This pattern, of triggers landing hard then being pushed past, will recur.

The wet-patch resolution. "Whatever." Sharon's relationship with her sexuality is contained, observed, and unsentimental. Not embarrassed. Not performative. The flat one-word resolution is canonical for how she treats her own body.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Age. Old Archive/Characters.pdf has Sharon at 29. Series Bible and MEMORY.md have Sharon at 32. CANON: 32. Master timeline (Sharon 25 when Jaden faked death 7 years ago, Sharon 32 now) is consistent.

Reason for joining the police. Old Archive/Characters.pdf and Archive/Book/Chapter 2.pdf both have Sharon joining specifically to find Jaden's killer. Series Bible: channelled grief into the force more broadly, with the ninja case being her current assignment. CANON: Series Bible. A personal-vendetta-from-day-one Sharon makes her too narrow; the broader trajectory lets her find the link to Jaden organically during Season 1.

Skills. Old PDF "Deadshot, Drunken master." Bible same. CANON: locked.

Recovering alcoholic / emotional state. Old PDF "Recovering alcoholic, emotionally unstable." Bible "recovering alcoholic, emotionally complex." CANON: recovering alcoholic + emotionally complex. The "unstable" framing is retired in favour of "complex," which leaves her dignity intact.

Sexuality. Old PDF includes "Bisexual" in notes. Series Bible does not specify. CANON (resolved 2026-05-12): Sharon is bisexual. The Episode 1 wet-patch scene (where Sharon's involuntary response to witnessing the Boss Lady scene is observed and treated as routine) reads cleanly under a bisexual framing. The lack of explicit Bible mention was silence rather than retirement; now locked.

The corrupt senior officer feeding Bio Genetix. Bible §6: "A senior officer assigns her to a special task force, but he's secretly feeding her intel to Bio Genetix through Paul Mitchell." Bible does not name the officer. CANON (resolved 2026-05-12): the Captain. Nelson resents Sharon for the Captain's preferential treatment of her, but the Captain himself is the asset feeding her career path and her intel to Bio Genetix. The dramatic structure: the man Nelson is jealous of is the man weaponising her. Sharon's discovery of this is the load-bearing betrayal beat at end of Season 1.

Sharon's ex-boyfriend. UN-RETIRED AND NOW CANON (Bupe, 2026-08-27): "her walking in with boyfriend cheating needs to be there." At nineteen she lets herself into the flat she pays half of and finds her best friend in her own bed with him. She says nothing, packs around them while they talk over each other, takes nothing of his, and closes the door on her name being called. The point is that she was already numb, so this is not the thing that broke her. Old PDF "his infidelity hardened Sharon's resolve"; the previous recommendation to retire it is superseded. The Bible's emotional architecture for Sharon's hardening is the Jaden death plus the spiral; the cheating ex feels redundant. Flag for Bupe.

Wet-patch moment in Episode 1. Not in old PDF. New material added in Episode 1 edits. Establishes Sharon's complexity around sex. CANON: per Episode 1. Locked.

The flashback, third version. The kitchen version was replaced by a bus-stop version, and on 2026-08-13 Bupe replaced that in turn with the corner fragment described in Backstory: no names, almost no dialogue, entirely from her eyeline, ending on a face she never gets to see. CANON: per current Episode 1 file. The trigger phrase changed with it, from "stay there" to "don't move".

What he does

At 28 Sharon is still in uniform. The door says SUPERINTENDENT LUCAS, and so does the plate on the desk, which is how the audience gets his name and his power in one shot without anybody introducing him. He closes it behind her with her file open on the desk.

He tells her the truth. She is the best natural investigator to come through that building in years. She reads between the evidence. She holds detail nobody else holds. He is not flattering her and he is not lying, and it is the first time in her adult life anybody has called her exceptional at anything.

Then he reads out the tariff. No woman climbs the ranks here. Not on merit, not on results, not in twenty years. He does not proposition her. He describes a system and lets her work out her own position inside it.

She does it. She is fast-tracked. It works.

What makes him worse than a predator

The promotion was already coming. Her talent alone had earned it, and the recommendation was signed and dated before that day. It is sitting in the open file on his desk while she is on her knees.

He knew. He said nothing. He took the price because the situation was there to be taken.

So it was never a transaction, it was a robbery dressed up as one, and she paid willingly and has carried it for years as the shameful thing she traded herself for. He did not corrupt an honest force to get her. He simply noticed what she would agree to.

Craft notes

  • He is never written as a leering villain. The scene works because he is calm, correct, and largely accurate about the institution. The horror is that his description of the force is basically true.
  • He never threatens her. He does not have to. The threat is the building.
  • The compliment is genuine, which is what makes it obscene, and it should be written so the audience believes it too.
  • He already has a line in the shipped E1 without appearing: Nelson circles Sharon with "What is it the Super sees in you? ...Or what is it he wants to put in you?" That is not a rumour, it is the truth said by a man who does not know it, and Sharon cannot react, because reacting is admitting it.

Found 2026-08-27 in MEMORY: "2026-05-12 - Canon additions locked: The Captain is the corrupt officer feeding Sharon's intel to Bio Genetix via Paul Mitchell (the man Nelson envies is the one weaponising her). Assigned Sharon to the special task force. Sharon does not know this in Episode 1. The reveal lands at end of Season 1." Lucas is that man. Bupe said on 27 Aug that he would unravel who Lucas really is as the story is built; the story had already answered it in May and the two halves fit without a seam.

What the merge does, and it is worse than either half alone. He did not find a useful detective and start milking her. He built her. He saw the talent, told her the truth about it, charged her a price for a promotion she had already earned, installed her in CID, put her on the task force himself, and has read everything she has produced since. Every part of Sharon's career belongs to him, including the decision she is most ashamed of. And the reveal at the end of Season 1 is not "your boss is bent". It is "the worst thing you ever did was not even necessary, and the man who took it from you has been reading your work ever since."

Profile created 2026-08-10 from Bupe's dictation. Supersedes the parked status set earlier the same day. Trace was previously image-only in _Pending_or_Retired; he is now a developed entity with a locked nature, appearance, perception rule, voice mechanic, engagement rule and one canonical fight.

IT IS A REASON (the load-bearing fact)

Trace was not born and was not created. It is a reason, which is why it is not solid and why its appearance is closer to a conceptual outline than a body.

When the gods died in the Second Seal they knew the Book would outlive them, and Trace is the provision they made. Not a guard they appointed. The reason the Book stays shut, given a shape.

Everything below follows from that one sentence.

THE ILLUSION: nobody questions it

Nobody sees Trace as a ghost. Nobody questions its appearance. To them it does not feel abnormal.

Because a reason arrives already accepted. That is what a reason is. You do not interrogate why a reason is present, so humanity inherently files Trace as just another person and moves on. Their minds supply the person; Trace supplies nothing.

So a shadowy human-shaped thing stands in a Danim park and nobody says a word about it, for four thousand years.

AUDIENCE DEVICE, and it is the best hook Trace has. The audience will notice long before any character does, and will spend episodes asking why nobody is freaking out. That question is not a bug to be patched, it is the reveal. Do not have a character voice it early to relieve the tension.

Tribal is the only one who sees it as it is

And it is the same rule as everything else about him. The acceptance is a property of the gods' order, and Tribal sits outside that order entirely (Series Bible section 3, Voodoo). So he gets no auto-fill. He sees the raw thing.

One rule, three consequences, which is what makes the world feel like one system:

  1. Trace has no authority over Tribal (the Second Seal is a covenant among the living).
  2. Kega has no jurisdiction over him (he is not in the ledger).
  3. The illusion does not reach him. He sees what is actually standing there.

He was frightened of it for a very long time, which is correct: he is the only person alive looking at it without the comfort of the lie. That fear only breaks when he works out that Trace is not hostile and is not interested in him.

Then he asks it what it is. That conversation is one of the most anticipated moments in the series by the time it arrives.

IT KNOWS EXACTLY WHAT IT IS (locked 2026-08-12)

Trace knows precisely what it is and why it exists. It is not confused, it is not searching, and it is not waiting to find out. It has known for four thousand years.

Nobody has ever asked it the right questions.

The information has been standing in a park in daylight for four millennia, entirely available, and every single person who could have understood the answer never saw anything worth asking about, while the one person who does see it cannot parse the reply.

That double lock is the tragedy and it should never be resolved cheaply. Everyone else could ask and be answered in a language they would understand, but they see an ordinary lad and have no question. Tribal sees the truth, has every question, and gets the god-language raw.

The information is available to everyone and reachable by nobody.

THE FOOTBALL: the one thing it does not know

It knows everything about itself except this.

It has a strange attraction to football and it does not know why. You will almost always find it in the park or the cage playing. Kids play around it and with it. Nobody thinks it is odd.

And it has a fetish for the scores. It wants results. It will ask, and because everyone accepts it as an ordinary person, they simply tell it. A bloke on a bench gets asked the score by a hole in the world and answers without looking up.

Running gag, permanently unexplained, and football fans will recognise every one of the antics.

WRITING RULE: never explain the football. Ever. Not even Trace can. It works because there is no reason for it, and the fact that a thing with perfect self-knowledge has exactly one gap in it, and the gap is football, is the closest thing it has to a soul.

It is also how the audience should meet Trace, well before anyone says what it is: a shadow playing football in a cage in Danim with local kids, in daylight, and nobody reacting.

VOICE

No mouth. No voice box. You do not hear it with your ears. It puts the words into your thoughts, and because there is no mouth to watch, the character and the audience both experience it as speech.

Sound design rule that makes it wrong without anyone saying so: thought-speech has no room acoustic. No reverb, no space, no falloff with distance. It is exactly as present whether Trace is beside you or across the pitch. Nobody in-world ever comments on it and the audience feels it every time.

The language of the gods, and the two channels

Trace speaks the language of the gods. To a normal person, the thought-speech arrives already comprehensible. To Tribal, who is outside the order, it arrives raw: slurred, reversed, wrong-way-round, unmistakably a real language and completely opaque.

PROPOSED DEVICE, strongly recommended: the audience hears whichever channel Tribal hears. In a scene with both a normal character and Tribal present, we hear the raw god-language while the normal character answers as though it made perfect sense. The audience works out that there are two channels before anybody explains it.

Does Tribal ever understand it?

Recommendation: he never learns the language. He learns what the language IS.

Over years he learns to recognise a handful of specific sounds by what tends to follow them, the way you learn a dog's bark: he can tell a warning from a dismissal without ever knowing a word. Function without meaning, which is a very Tribal thing to have.

The payoff, and it is why this is better than either extreme: Kega speaks the same language, and it is the language the Book is written in. Tribal has been reading that language for twenty years and has never once heard it spoken (Tribal's profile, 2026-08-12). So when Kega opens his mouth in Season 4, Tribal does not recognise a noise. He recognises shapes he has been reading off a page for two decades, coming out of a mouth for the first time.

That is the moment Tribal finally understands what Trace is. He never gets the words. He gets the category.

OPEN (Bupe): whether to take this or leave it fully unresolved.

APPEARANCE

Body type: a university athlete. Clearly not an adult, clearly not a child, past teenage. Lean, capable, unremarkable.

Colour: pure, absolute black. Free of any colour undertone. The reference point is a display state where the pixels are switched off entirely and emit zero light, rather than a dark grey or a blue-black.

The white highlights are the only detail. A subtle tip of white catching an edge, just enough to read as three-dimensional rather than a flat cut-out. Enough that you think you can almost see lips, and cannot.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION, and it is what makes the design hard: Trace is not a silhouette. A silhouette is a person with light behind them, and a viewer's brain resolves it into a person hidden by contrast. Trace is the opposite: a shape with nothing inside it and nothing casting it. There is no source. It is not in shadow, it is the absence, standing in full daylight.

IMAGE SPEC (from the 2026-08-12 generation pass)

Locked and keep: the void figure against a fully lit park; background people not reacting (this is the illusion made visible and every Trace image should carry it); football at the feet; no face; athlete proportions; a thin rim highlight on shoulder and forearm.

Three fixes:

  1. No surface gloss. Broad soft sheens across chest, thighs and upper arms read as a reflective material, latex or vinyl, and a surface that reflects light is the exact opposite of a thing that emits none. Keep the thin edge rim only. The interior stays completely, flatly dead.
  2. Less anatomy. Visible pecs, abdominal contour, knee definition and separate fingers all resolve it into a body. Merge the fingers, drop the interior modelling, let the outline carry the form.
  3. Dress it in the void. This one is canon rather than taste. The illusion requires it to read as an ordinary lad who came down for a kickabout. A naked figure is precisely what people would react to, so it quietly breaks the thing the image is trying to show. T-shirt, shorts, trainers, all rendered in the same absolute black.

ENGAGEMENT RULE: it monitors a sequence, not an object (refined 2026-08-10)

Opening the Book is not a violation. Reading it is not a violation. The violation is the triangular order completing outside the law (Series Bible section 4):

  1. READ
  2. UNDERSTOOD
  3. ACTED UPON

Trace is the monitoring of that triangle. It does not care where the Book physically is or who is holding it. It steps in at the exact point where understanding turns into action outside the law, and it escalates with how badly the secrets are abused.

Which is why Face can run the entire Danim underworld and never once trouble it, and why the Book sat in a school library for twenty years costing nothing. It has no opinion about crime, violence or ninjas. The triangle is the only thing it is for.

It never initiates. It arrives, it stands in the way, and it concludes. See the fight below.

THE ONE FIGHT: Face

The only person known to have fought Trace, and it is the series' entire measure of what Trace is.

How it started. A hot-headed incident. Face told it to stand aside, like a little worm. Trace did not move.

The escalation. Face attacked, not at full power, just to frighten it. Trace dodged. He tried again. Dodged. Faster, then faster, then more ferocious, because the thing was irritating him and making a mockery of him in front of himself. He pushed into a final Aura state. Full speed, full-size attacks, everything he had.

Trace dodged, blocked, and when the smoke cleared was standing at a distance.

The end. Face stood there, shocked, angry and confused. Then Trace closed the whole gap in an instant flash and set what appears to be a one-inch punch against his stomach.

The zoom stops dead for one split second. Face looks down at the hand already resting on him. Shit. His startle plays in slow motion, his head coming down slowly.

Then the punch. A thud inside his stomach, and a burst of force around them both: no colour, just force. He holds his stomach and goes down slowly. His vision blurs, he blinks, he watches Trace walk away, and he passes out.

Jaden and Jon find him and ask what happened. His pride will not let him say it. He has carried it ever since, and he has never told anyone he lost.

Why the one-inch punch is the right technique

Zero wind-up, no travel, pure transfer. For a thing that is a reason, that is exactly correct: no escalation, no build, just consequence arriving. Trace does not fight. It concludes.

And the fix that makes it better

Trace was not there for Face. Its engagement rule is the Book, and Face was not touching the Book. So it was there for something else entirely, and Face walked into it and started a fight over a misunderstanding he will never learn about, because he never told anybody it happened.

He has spent years believing he lost a fight he picked over nothing. He is right. He just does not know what he interrupted.

What it does for Face's character

He now carries two secrets: one that was taken from him and one he chose to keep. The Elixir erased his brothers without his consent. Trace he buried himself. That pairs directly with the wrist tell as a second silent thing running under every scene he is in.

SENSORY SIGNATURE

Three power sources in the series, three distinct registers. Never mix them.

SourceRegister
AuraHot, light, crackle. Fills a room.
VoodooCold, void, heavy silence. Empties a room.
TraceNo temperature, no colour, pure force. Neither fills nor empties. It simply arrives.

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE SEAL BREAKS (locked 2026-08-10)

It does not die. It becomes unnecessary, which is a different and worse thing.

Trace is the reason the triangle stays broken. When Tribal completes it, the reason becomes the reason for nothing. Unnecessary things do not end, they stop having been needed, so Trace fades rather than dies, and there is a window.

And nobody notices, because the acceptance was part of the order too. Everyone who ever looked at it and comfortably saw an ordinary lad loses that lad when the order goes. It is not a death anybody mourns. As far as the world is concerned there simply was never anyone there.

Except Tribal. He was outside the order, so he is the only person who ever saw it truly, and he is the only one who will remember it existed. He is also the man who broke the seal. He kills the only thing that ever let him look at something honestly, and he can never tell a living soul, because nobody else knows there was anything to lose.

The window

For the first time in four thousand years it is not for anything. So it goes to the cage.

The last image of Trace is it playing football, getting less and less there, while nobody in the park notices a player going missing. Tribal on the fence, the only one who can see it.

And the last thing it ever does is not language. Tribal asks it again what it is. He still cannot understand the answer, because he never could. So Trace passes him the ball.

Leave it deliberately unclear whether Trace knows it is ending. Tribal cannot tell. He never could.

WHAT KEVIN SEES (locked 2026-08-10)

Not the truth, and not the lie. A mismatch.

Kevin is inside the order: a living human, second generation, part of the world. Kūga is not. So Kevin's eyes do what everyone else's do and accept the ordinary lad, while something inside him flatly refuses, and he cannot reconcile the two or locate where the wrongness is coming from.

Which is the correct Kevin experience, because his whole arc is his own mind not being entirely his own.

Kūga knows exactly what it is and will not tell him. Free comedy and free dread at once: "You should look at that again." Bored, looking elsewhere, never explains twice.

The reverse question, which is bigger: does Trace see Kevin?

Trace is the last surviving element of the operation that sealed Kūga, and Kevin is carrying Kūga. But Kevin is masked by default, because an amplifier at rest emits nothing.

So Trace does not notice him. Not for episodes. Not until the first time Kevin uses the power anywhere near it.

Mid-game. The ball rolls past. Trace does not follow the ball.

Its engagement rule is the triangle, not the Sphere, so it does not act. It just notices. Which is much worse, and it costs one shot.

Open Questions (Bupe)

  • Does Tribal ever understand the language, or does it stay permanently opaque? Recommendation above.
  • Has Trace ever intervened before, in 4,000 years? If it has, there are incidents in the historical record that nobody could explain.
  • What ARE the right questions? Trace knows everything and has never been asked correctly. Worth Bupe deciding privately what the right question is, even if it is never asked on screen, because it determines what Trace would say if it ever were.
  • Does it know it is ending? Deliberately unresolved on screen.
  • Has it ever intervened before, in four thousand years? If so there are incidents in the record nobody could explain.

THE INTEGRATION (locked 2026-08-10)

Everything below the Quick Reference predates the Kega and Kūga mythology. This section is what makes Tribal fit it, and it is the load-bearing part of the profile.

His power is death-side, and that is why it is outside the Aura system

Look at the full ability list: resurrection, phantoms, spirit manipulation, soul binding, soul capture, life drain. Not one of them touches a living system.

Now look at the gods. Kega legislated the order of life. Kūga amplifies the living. Aura is life energy in living people. The Book is the law of the living. The entire divine system, all 6,000 years of it, only ever covered the living.

CANON: voodoo is the door the gods never legislated, because they never legislated for the dead. This is why his power is separate from Aura. It is not an exception any more, it has a reason.

SENSORY RULE, applies to every depiction of his magic. Aura is heat, light and crackle in a living body. His is the exact inverse: cold instead of hot, void instead of light, heavy silence instead of energy. Where Aura fills a room, his empties it. Never write his power with the vocabulary of Aura.

Where the power came from: nowhere divine. Sera found the remains of something real in books in Danim, while looking for a love spell. Anyone could have found it. It was not destiny, and keeping it mundane is deliberate: the mythology is 6,000 years old and the thing that eventually cracks it is a nineteen-year-old girl who was ignored.

What being outside the order buys him

Trace cannot stop him. Trace is the embodiment of the Second Seal, and the Second Seal is a covenant among the living (Bible section 9). Tribal is not covered by the terms. He does not defeat Trace, he walks past a guard with no authority over him. This is the answer to the long-open "how does Tribal reach the Book" thread.

Kega has no jurisdiction over him, and this is why the Season 4 arrival scene works. A god of judgment stops and calmly asks a human how he got here, instead of purging him, because Tribal is the first being in 6,000 years he has no verdict for. He is not in the ledger. That is why the arm is up and the strike does not land.

He is the only person alive who sees Trace as it actually is (added 2026-08-10). Everyone else accepts Trace as an ordinary person, because a reason arrives already accepted, and that acceptance is a property of the gods' order. Tribal is outside that order, so he gets no auto-fill. He was frightened of it for a very long time, correctly: he is the only one looking at it without the comfort of the lie. Full detail in Characters/Trace/Trace.md.

HE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO HAS EVER READ THE BOOK IN ITS ACTUAL LANGUAGE (added 2026-08-12, and this is the one that ends the world).

The Book translates itself into the reader's own language, but that translation is a courtesy of the order (Series Bible section 4, The Three Depths). Tribal is outside the order.

So the Book never translated for him. Not even the forward side. He had to learn the god-language from scratch just to read the ordinary teaching, which is why he taught himself to read a dead god's handwriting. And once you can read it raw, the backward side was never hidden from him at all. There is no forward and backward for Tribal. There is just a book.

He can read the forbidden layer only because he was never granted the easy one.

And the Book's security assumes a reader inside the order, because when the gods built it there was no other kind. Sera invented that category 5,960 years later, in a library in Danim, looking for a love spell.

So being outside the order does FOUR things, not one. Trace has no authority over him, Kega has no jurisdiction over him, the illusion does not reach him, and the Book does not translate for him, so nothing in it is closed to him. One rule, four consequences, and the fourth one is why Season 4 happens.

He and Kūga are the only two things outside the order: the half that was cast out of the ledger, and the man who was never in it. Very probably why he can see the Elixir scars on the Mandem's souls when nobody else can, and why he could sense Kega at all.

His real motive: Sera never came

Underneath the mystique, he is not chasing "a deeper truth" in the abstract.

He was taken at birth. His mother is alive, could walk out of that prison any day, and in forty years has never once come for him. (See Characters/Sera/Sera.md.)

That sits directly on the Power of Will system: Sera's will is what made him exist, and she has never willed a single thing in his direction since. Power is the only inheritance she left him, so being worth it is the only route he can see to having been wanted.

A god wakes up because a man wanted his mother to have loved him. That is the through-line, and it turns the Season 4 catalyst from a plot device into a tragedy.

HIS ABILITIES, TIERED (locked 2026-08-12)

The old list was everything at once, which made him the answer to every problem. Split into three tiers, and the split itself is characterful.

TIER 1: SIGNATURE, cheap, always available.

  1. Life drain by touch. Inherited straight from Sera, and it is the exact thing that killed Elliot Jones. It is why nobody wants to be within reach of him and why he does not really fight: he touches. Instant, quiet, no build-up.
  2. Spirit sight. Passive and constant. He sees what is left behind: the dead, the residue, the scars on souls (Face's Elixir damage), and Trace as it actually is. This is the whole reason he is a seer rather than a warrior, and it is where nearly all of his information comes from.

TIER 2: SIGNATURE BUT COSTLY.

  1. Phantoms. Raising the dead as tethered clones. This is what made his name as the Voodoo Master, and it must cost. Every phantom is tethered to him, so an army is exhausting and dangerous to hold, and they are not free soldiers. Use it as an event, never as a default.

TIER 3: RITUAL ONLY. Days of preparation, specific ingredients, and a sacrifice.

  • Binding of Souls
  • Soul capture
  • Memory work: plant and distort only, never restore
  • Anything that changes a state permanently

THE COST RULE, and it comes straight from Sera. Every ritual demands a sacrifice, and her first one set the pattern: you give up something you love. Tribal has been giving pieces of himself away for decades. What he has left to give is the Season 4 question, because the ritual that wakes Kega costs him something enormous.

One line he has never crossed. Sera drains to keep. Tribal drains to kill. He has never once turned it on himself to hold back time, and that is a choice rather than an inability. When he eventually learns what she has been doing on that island for forty years, the horror is that they have the same hand and she has been eating people to stay pretty.

THE SECRET SOCIETY: what happened to it (locked 2026-08-12)

They raised him, feared him, and studied him. He killed a trainer by accident as a child and they read it as proof rather than warning, and pushed harder.

The break. In his teens a ritual went wrong and killed several of them at once. Not his intent. But they had told him to do it.

They cast him out anyway, because they needed it to be his fault. If it was his fault they were still in control of something. If it was theirs, they had been playing with a thing they never understood. So he was exiled for obeying, and he grew up believing he was a monster who murdered the only family he had ever had.

Then he found out. In his twenties he learned the truth: the ritual was theirs, the order was theirs, and they knew it was dangerous. They had exiled a teenager to protect their own story.

And he went back. Not to kill them. He went back to make one of them say it out loud. Seventeen years of being told he was a killer, and he wanted one sentence.

They would not give it to him. What he did next is the thing he does not talk about.

PRESENT-DAY STATUS: functionally gone. A handful of very old members, scattered and hiding, who have spent decades certain the Voodoo Master will come back to finish it. He never has. He got his sentence out of one of them, and after that he simply stopped caring.

Why this version rather than a massacre. It makes him tragic instead of villainous, and it leaves survivors who are a live resource for the story: someone Sharon could find, someone who could tell Face or Kevin what Tribal actually is, and someone carrying a version of events that is self-serving and forty years old.

And the thematic rhyme, which is the point. Tribal wanted the people who raised him to admit what they did, and they refused. Sera has never given him a word either. Every adult who was ever supposed to explain him has declined to. Both of his defining wounds are him asking to be seen, and being ignored.

HE CAN READ IT AND HAS NEVER HEARD IT (added 2026-08-12)

He taught himself a dead god's handwriting and has never once heard the language spoken. Reading and hearing are different skills, and he had decades with a text and no teacher: like a man who can read Latin and could not hold a conversation in it.

Which is why he cannot understand Trace, and why the Season 4 recognition is sharper than a sound-match. When Kega opens his mouth, Tribal does not recognise a noise. He recognises shapes he has been reading for twenty years, coming out of a mouth for the first time.

THE WHISPERS: he heard the nouns and lost the verbs (locked 2026-08-12)

His spirit sight is always on, so the dead have been talking to him for decades. But the dead speak in fragments, and across years he got two words out of them.

God. Ultimate power.

They were not tempting him. They were warning him. He received two words out of a sentence closer to a god is in there, and ultimate power is not what you will find.

And it rhymes with everything else about him. Tribal has spent his entire life receiving incomplete messages from people who will not finish the sentence. The society who would not say it out loud. His mother, who has never said anything at all. Now the dead, giving him two words out of ten.

Every single time, he has filled the gap in with the same thing: that something is owed to him.

That is why he does it. Not greed. A man completing other people's sentences in his own favour, because nobody has ever finished one for him.

He thought it was a manual. Reasonably: the forward side had taught him generously for years. He was unaware it was a seal.

He can break, distort and plant. He cannot restore.

Rule added to close a plot hole. If Tribal can manipulate memory, the obvious question is why he does not simply hand Face his memories back instead of feeding him hints for two seasons.

The Elixir did not erase memories, it erased bonds, and the bible says it left scars on their souls. Different layer. Tribal sees the scar perfectly and cannot touch it. Damage is cheap, repair is impossible. Same asymmetry as Kūga's harm-cheap-good-expensive rule, which is what makes the world feel like one system.

Differentiating him from Manic

Manic's memory manipulation comes from the Mind pillar of Aura. Tribal's comes from the dead. Manic works on a living mind; Tribal works through the spirit, which is why his version can reach people who are no longer alive and Manic's cannot.

Ages, and they hold with no reconciliation needed

  • Tribal is 40 (Bupe, 2026-08-10). Face is 30, so Tribal was already an adult operator when the Mandem were kids finding the Book, and he watched them become legends. That is the authority he speaks to Face with.
  • Sera is around 59 and looks late twenties.
  • Tribal was 18 to 20 during the Springvale contamination, outside the 5 to 15 window entirely. So he is the only major character excluded from Aura twice over: wrong age and wrong source.

Backstory

Tribal was born to Sera, a woman raised by an abusive father who became obsessed with a priest. Sera performed a dark voodoo ritual to control the priest. The ritual resulted in the priest's death and Sera's pregnancy. Sera was imprisoned. Tribal was taken from her at birth.

Tribal was raised by a secret society that both revered and feared him. The society treated him as something more than human and something less than safe. He learned the voodoo arts that his mother carried. He inherited her mystical abilities in a form that has grown more sophisticated than hers ever was.

Sera, in prison, became known as "a serpent." Her status is not fully specified (see Open Questions): possibly still imprisoned, possibly dead, possibly something else. Tribal's relationship with her now is unknown.

Crucially, Tribal's powers do not come from the Hakai Sphere or the school water contamination. They come from his mother's ritual and his inherited bloodline. He is the only significant character in Hood Ninjaz whose abilities sit entirely outside the Aura system. This makes him categorically distinct: every other power user in the show is operating on the Aura grid; Tribal is operating on something older and unrelated.

By Episode 1's timeline, Tribal is functioning as a cryptic advisor to Face. He can see the fractures in Face's memories (the Elixir-erased Mandem bond) and feeds Face cryptic hints, slowly guiding him toward remembering. His motives in doing this are unclear. He doesn't appear bound to either side of the ninja conflict.

His pivotal role across the larger arc, per Series Bible §9, is the sequel/Season 4 plot point: Tribal's failed voodoo ritual is the final crack in the already weakening seal that holds the Original Ninja God. He doesn't intend this. The failure is the catalyst.

Personality

Mysterious. Cryptic. Speaks in fragments, in riddles, in lines that don't fully resolve until later.

Dark. Carries the weight of his origin and his powers. Not flamboyantly dark; quietly dark. The kind of presence that empties a room without raising a voice.

Lone operator. Doesn't pledge loyalty. Doesn't take sides cleanly. Useful to whoever needs him, dangerous to whoever miscalculates him.

Sees things. The Elixir-erased fractures in Face's mind are visible to him in a way they aren't to anyone else. He doesn't tell Face what he sees; he feeds the hints in shape and timing rather than content.

Unclear motivation by design. Bible doesn't lock his intent. The audience should not fully read him.

Patient. Plays a long game. The Season 4 ritual is set up in pieces across Seasons 1-3 even though the audience doesn't realise it until later.

Motivation

Three-phase arc.

Phase 1 (Season 1). Cryptic advisor to Face. Feeds Face hints about the past. Watches the Elixir wall start to fracture. Observes the shape of what is coming.

Phase 2 (Season 2). Mystical force against the TANCs. His powers become essential to the ninja defence. TANCs cannot be reasoned with or surveilled; Tribal can drain, manipulate, capture. He becomes a strategic asset even though his alignment remains ambiguous.

Phase 3 (sequel / Season 4). The Original Ninja God awakening. His failed ritual is the final crack in the seal. The series' main villain post-finale is a consequence of Tribal's actions, intended or not.

Powers and Abilities

Voodoo magic and witchcraft. Inherited from Sera. Not Aura-based. Operates on a magical system entirely separate from the Aura grid.

Resurrection / cloning. Per old Archive/Characters.pdf: "Ability to revive and create an army of cloned ninjas." Series Bible doesn't elaborate the mechanics, but the capability is retained.

Life drain. Drains life force from others. Mechanics not specified.

Spirit manipulation. Can influence or interact with spirits, presumed via the voodoo framework.

Memory manipulation. Distinct from Manic's illusion-based memory alteration; Tribal's version is rooted in voodoo rather than Mind-pillar Aura. Can also perceive memory damage in others (Face's Elixir-erased bonds).

Soul capture. Capability listed in old PDF. Mechanics not specified.

Seeing fractured realities. The Elixir damage is visible to Tribal. He sees what Face has lost. This is the basis for his role as cryptic advisor.

Failed-ritual potential. Bible §9: Tribal's failed ritual is the Season 4 catalyst. The ritual is large enough to be the final crack in the Original Ninja God's seal.

Key Relationships

  • Sera (his mother, status uncertain). The source. The serpent. Connection between them in present day is undefined.
  • The secret society that raised him. Revered and feared him. Current status: undefined. They may be allies, may be enemies, may have fragmented after he came into power.
  • Face / Devon (30). Tribal feeds him cryptic hints about his Elixir-erased past. Motives unclear. Face accepts the hints without trusting the source. The relationship is transactional with subtext.
  • The Mandem (Jaden, Jon, Face). Tribal sees the damage in Face. By extension he understands the bond that was severed. He doesn't necessarily know Jaden is alive, but he has more visibility into the Mandem situation than any other character in the show.
  • Bio Genetix. Tribal's voodoo is the only meaningful counter to TANCs in Season 2. The relationship is enemy-of-an-enemy; he is not a ninja ally, but he opposes the TANC project.
  • The Original Ninja God (sequel / Season 4 antagonist). Tribal's failed ritual is the final crack in the seal. He doesn't intend this. The unintended consequence is the engine of the post-main-series arc.
  • Other ninjas. Mostly observes them. Doesn't engage as peer or enemy by default.

Arc

Season 1. Cryptic advisor. Background presence. Feeds Face hints. Observes the wider board.

Season 2. Mystical powers become essential against the TANCs. Strategic asset in the ninja defence. Alignment remains ambiguous.

Season 3. Continues to operate semi-independently. His ritual preparation builds toward the Season 4 catalyst, though the show doesn't surface this yet.

Season 4 (sequel). The failed ritual cracks the seal. The Original Ninja God awakens. Tribal's role in the awakening is the bridge between the main series and the sequel.

Voice and Dialogue

Cryptic. Riddles. Fragments. The line that doesn't resolve until two episodes later.

Speaks rarely. When he speaks, the room listens because the words don't fit any pattern the room expects.

No direct dialogue samples available in the read sources (Tribal is not in Episode 1 and not in Chapters 1-2). The register is inferable from the Bible and old PDF.

Pattern. Each line should function as either a hint or a non-sequitur (which is itself a hint, the audience just doesn't see it yet). Avoid exposition. Avoid clean answers. The audience and the characters should feel that something has been said without being able to reduce it cleanly.

Tonal references. The cryptic-old-mage archetype, but rooted in voodoo rather than Eastern mysticism. Caribbean and African diaspora referents fit Hood Ninjaz's pillar of cultural representation. The accent and speech rhythm would draw from Sera's lineage and the secret society that raised him, neither of which are locked yet.

Possible recurring beat. A single phrase or word Tribal repeats across episodes that means more each time the audience hears it. Worth designing during script work.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Origin: Aura vs separate voodoo source. Old Archive/Characters.pdf describes Tribal's voodoo without contextualising it within Hood Ninjaz's power system: "Tribal is a master of witchcraft and voodoo. He has one eye pupil different from the other, giving him a supernatural edge. He has the ability to revive and create an army of cloned ninjas." Series Bible explicitly establishes that his powers come from Sera's ritual and are separate from the Hakai Sphere. CANON: Tribal's powers are NOT Aura-based. This is load-bearing for the world-building: he is the only major character outside the Aura system, and his magical lineage is the bridge to the Original Ninja God in Season 4. The categorical distinction is preserved.

Age. Old PDF "30s." Bible "30s." CANON (resolved 2026-08-10, Bupe): TRIBAL IS 40. Ten years older than Face, which is the point: he was already an adult operator when the Mandem were kids finding the Book. Supersedes "30s" everywhere.

"Born into a lineage of mystics" is SUPERSEDED (2026-08-10). Bupe's Sera document contains two incompatible origins for Tribal. Its first half is definitive and matches the bible: conceived in the ritual, taken from Sera at birth, raised in isolation by a secret society, never knew his mother, no family. Its second half opens "Born into a lineage of mystics... his family was feared in Danim City... growing up, Tribal witnessed the duality of power," which cannot coexist with an isolated childhood and no family. CANON: the Sera origin. The lineage-of-mystics paragraph is retired. He has no lineage. He has a mother who has never come.

Memory manipulation vs the Elixir. Raised and closed 2026-08-10. He can break, distort and plant, and cannot restore; the Elixir cut bonds rather than memories, so he sees the scar and cannot touch it. Full rule in THE INTEGRATION above.

Overlap with Manic. Both have memory manipulation. Differentiated 2026-08-10: Manic works on a living mind via the Mind pillar, Tribal works through the spirit, so only Tribal's reaches the dead.

Eye difference. Old PDF: "one eye pupil different from the other, giving him a supernatural edge." Bible silent on this physical detail. CANON: retained from old PDF. Visual marker. Locked unless the visual director adjusts.

Sera as origin. Old PDF doesn't mention Sera. Bible introduces her as Tribal's mother and the source of his powers. CANON: Bible. Sera as origin is locked. Worth giving her a small dedicated file (see Tier B order: Sera is included).

Secret society that raised him. Old PDF silent. Bible adds. CANON: Bible. The society is locked as part of his backstory. Specifics (name, current status) are open.

Resurrection / cloning army. Old PDF: "control over life and death gives the bad ninjas an undead army to command." Bible doesn't elaborate but retains. CANON: capability retained. Specifics undefined. Worth flagging if it becomes a Season 2 plot lever.

Face's memory fractures visibility. Bible adds. Old PDF silent. CANON: Bible. This is one of Tribal's defining capabilities.

The Original Ninja God sequel role. Bible §9 establishes Tribal's failed ritual as the final crack. CANON: Bible. Locked.

City spelling. Old PDF Tribal entry uses "Denim City" once (in context: "control over life and death gives the bad ninjas an undead army to command" mentions the city in surrounding text). CANON: Danim City. Original PDF unchanged as historical record. The Tribal-entry-specific Denim instances are in the surrounding narrative rather than direct Tribal description.

Open Questions

  • Sera's current status. In prison, dead, or something else? The "serpent" framing in prison reads as a folk-legend register; whether she is still alive matters for whether the mother-son reunion is possible.
  • Tribal's real name. Just Tribal? A given name underneath? Worth deciding for moments where someone might use it (Sera if alive, someone from the secret society).
  • The secret society. Name, current status, alignment. Are they antagonists, allies, or fragmented? Their existence is locked; their state is not.
  • Tribal's first appearance in Season 1. Bible says cryptic advisor to Face. Episode 1 does not include him. Worth deciding when he first appears on screen.
  • His motivation. Bible says "motives unclear" deliberately. For writing purposes, is there a north star Bupe knows that the audience shouldn't (i.e., a private intent Tribal is working toward), or is the ambiguity all the way down?
  • The cloned ninja army. Capability is retained from old PDF. When does it come into play? Season 2 against the TANCs?
  • The failed ritual. Season 4 catalyst. Specifics of what the ritual is, what he's trying to do, why it fails, are entirely undefined.
  • Tribal and Trace. Both are non-Aura-system mystics with roles in the larger mythology. Do they know about each other? Adversaries? Indifferent? Worth flagging once Trace's file is built (Tier B).
  • Voice samples. No spoken dialogue is on record from any source I read in this session. Tribal's voice register will need to be drafted from scratch when his first scene lands.
