Backstory

Uno was built by Dr Lucius Kane at Bio Genetix. He is the first fully autonomous TANC, the prototype that was supposed to prove the program. Bio Genetix wanted a soldier. Kane wanted something more.

Uno was given a conscience. An unauthorised feature in the design. Kane designed Uno to think, to feel, to grow. Built in the form of a young boy, the body is engineered to read as 13. Bio Genetix didn't notice the depth of the autonomy at first; they noticed it when Uno refused to perform a directive that would have hurt civilians.

MADE, THEN ABANDONED, THEN FOUND (Bupe's ruling, 2026-08-27, decision B1)

Both origins are true and they run in that order. The lab is not replaced by the warehouse, it is followed by it. Kane made him. Then he was abandoned. Then Donte found him.

What the 2024 Chapter 9 restores, and it is now canon: Donte finds a filthy, starving, mute, feral boy living in his warehouse. He feeds him. He gets silently followed for days. The chapter ends on the first apple Donte gave him, uneaten, shrivelled and rotting on a table with the shop sticker still attached, set as the centrepiece of a shrine of wrappers.

Why both is stronger than either. The lab explains what he is. The apple shrine explains who he is. And it gives Donte the only claim on Uno that ever mattered, which is not that he owns him or built him: he fed him. A thing that was made to be a weapon kept the wrapper.

Standing note for anyone writing him: the shrine is never explained by Uno and nobody ever asks him about it.

THE REAL REASON UNO WORKS (added 2026-08-10, late-series reveal)

Kane cheated. Uno is not a successful engineering outcome, he is a contaminated one.

Dr Lucius Kane was a Springvale kid himself. He drank the contaminated school water as a child (see Series Bible section 4), it made him what he is, and he spent his career at Bio Genetix watching the company fail over and over to replicate Aura with technology.

So on the one project that was his own, he used the real thing. His own blood on one side, the last bottle of Springvale on the other, and he infused both. His blood carried the trace; the bottle was the source. It is the only successful infusion ever performed, and Bio Genetix never knew it happened.

Why it can never be repeated. He had one bottle left and he used it. The input does not exist anywhere on earth any more, so Bio Genetix cannot reproduce Uno no matter what they spend. That makes Uno irreplaceable, and eventually makes him hunted: their masterpiece is a contamination they did not design, cannot repeat, and will one day want back badly enough to tear the city apart for.

And it makes Kane his father in the same way Face is Donte's. All three of the 3 Little Ninjaz have a father problem: one who does not know him, one who made him, and one who is really a brother.

How it gets delivered on screen. Uno does not remember (the EMP took it, see below), so he learns it in the room at the same time as everyone else. Give the fact to someone else and the line to Uno. Heavy moment, silence after the reveal, and Uno is the one who breaks it, trying to make it lighter, in the shape of "so I have got a man's blood running through my circuits." It should land as the saddest thing in the episode rather than a joke. Find the exact wording in the scene; do not pre-bake it.

The Escape

The military, working with Bio Genetix, demanded Kane strip Uno's conscience and reset his autonomy. Kane refused. Kane helped Uno escape.

During the escape, the military deployed an EMP. The EMP wiped most of Uno's memory and destroyed his tracker. Bio Genetix believes Uno is dead. Kane's fate is uncertain; whether he survived the escape, whether Bio Genetix retains him, whether he's still trying to reach Uno, is unknown.

Uno washed up in East Danim. Fragmented memories. Childlike innocence on the surface. Combat capability and advanced intelligence underneath. He doesn't fully understand human emotions or social cues; he understands he should not return to Bio Genetix.

He found Donte's warehouse. The two of them bonded silently (Chapter 9, the canonical tonal north star for Hood Ninjaz writing, per workspace CLAUDE.md). They share the warehouse, the silence, and the implicit understanding that the world is hunting both of them in different ways.

By the time Episode 1 opens, the bond is already in place. Uno is not on screen in Episode 1; he is the implied second occupant of the warehouse Donte returns to off screen.

Personality

Childlike innocence on the surface. Asks questions humans wouldn't think to ask. Doesn't understand jokes, sarcasm, or social cues without context.

Advanced combat capability beneath the innocence. The Bible frames the duality explicitly: "childlike innocence with combat abilities."

Identity crisis. The question Uno lives inside: am I a weapon or am I a person? He doesn't have a stable answer. He doesn't act on the question. He observes himself.

Curious about the world. Reads people, environments, objects with a calibration register that is recognisably non-human up close.

Loyal and protective once attached. Bonded with Donte; would defend Donte without hesitation. The protection is not programmed; it's earned. That distinction matters to the character.

Quiet. Like Donte. The Chapter 9 bonding is built on silence rather than words. Uno's silence is different from Donte's: where Donte is silent because nobody listened, Uno is silent because he is still figuring out what to say.

Memory-fragmented. He knows pieces. He doesn't know Dr Kane's name reliably. He doesn't remember the EMP. He has flashes that don't connect.

The dark mirror of Bio Genetix's intent. They built a weapon. They got a child with a conscience.

Motivation

Four-phase arc.

Phase 1 (pre-series and Season 1). Survive. Stay with Donte. Don't be found. Don't be reactivated. Don't return to Bio Genetix.

Phase 2 (Season 1 to Season 2). Establish trust with Donte. Begin to understand the world. Learn what humans do, why they do it, how feelings work. Donte teaches without intending to.

Phase 3 (Season 2 to Season 3). Become part of the 3 Little Ninjaz. Discover identity. Kevin and Donte form around him. Uno mirrors Jon (the outsider who joins, the developing moral compass).

Phase 4 (Season 3 finale). Confront Bio Genetix who built him. Helps defeat the Apex TANCs. Identity reconciled by the end: he is a person, not a weapon. The line is his to draw.

Powers and Abilities

Enhanced physical capability. Cyborg-grade strength, durability, speed, and reflexes. Above human ceiling but not infinite.

Advanced learning and adaptation. Bio Genetix designed him to learn faster than humans. He absorbs combat patterns by observing them. He absorbs language and social cues by watching humans live.

Combat protocols. Retained from his TANC base architecture. Trained fighter underneath the childlike surface. Style not yet locked in any source (see Open Questions).

No Aura. Uno is technology-based, not biological. The Aura system doesn't apply to him. This means Tier/colour entries are N/A and Uno operates by a different power logic than every other ninja.

Memory fragmentation. The EMP damage means Uno's recall is partial. Some technical knowledge is intact (combat protocols, basic identity), some emotional and biographical context is gone (Kane's full identity, the escape sequence, his early activation period). Memory recovery is an arc thread.

The wildcard. Not a ninja, not a fully functional TANC, something else. The category-defiance is the point of his character: where every other antagonist threat is either Aura-based or TANC-based, Uno is both and neither.

Key Relationships

  • Dr Lucius Kane (creator). Built Uno. Gave him a conscience. Refused to strip it. Helped him escape. Fate uncertain. Uno's memories of Kane are fragmented; he doesn't reliably remember the name but carries a residual sense of being chosen.
  • Donte Jakes / Blaze (13). The silent bond. Donte is the first person who didn't try to use or fix Uno. The pre-series Chapter 9 bonding establishes the relationship. Uno would defend Donte without protocol. Donte would not say it but reciprocates.
  • Kevin Young (13). Future relationship. Uno mirrors Jon in the next-gen trio; Kevin mirrors Jaden; Donte mirrors Face. Bible: "Uno mirrors Jon/Blade: the outsider who joins, questions everything, developing moral compass." The structural parallel is explicit.
  • Bio Genetix. Created him. Believes him dead. Will find him eventually. The reckoning is Season 2 or 3.
  • The TANCs (Season 1 Prototype, Season 2 Adaptive, Season 3 Apex). Uno's "siblings" in a way. They share architecture without sharing intent. Uno watching the Season 3 Apex TANCs break free is watching what he could have been if Kane hadn't intervened.
  • Paul Mitchell. Funds Bio Genetix. Indirect adversary. Uno doesn't know him personally.
  • The 3 Little Ninjaz (future). Kevin, Donte, Uno. Uno's place in the trio is the moral compass position. The outsider who questions.

Arc

Season 1. Lives with Donte. Silent companion. The audience meets him at some point in Season 1 (specific episode not locked). The audience learns he is a cyborg gradually.

Season 2. The 3 Little Ninjaz form. Uno starts to express opinions. Memory fragments return. Dr Kane's status surfaces (alive? dead? hostage?).

Season 3. Confronts Bio Genetix. Helps defeat the Apex TANCs. Identity reconciled. Person, not weapon.

Voice and Dialogue

Childlike when he speaks. Literal. Observational. Asks the question humans wouldn't think to ask.

Quiet by default. Silence is his baseline. Words emerge slowly, halting at times, calibrated.

Chapter 9 reference (not directly read in this session, see Open Questions). The bonding with Donte is canonically silent. The pattern is established: Uno doesn't fill space with words.

Pattern. When Uno speaks, the sentence is usually short, and usually a question or an observation. Doesn't use sarcasm. Doesn't use slang at series start (will pick it up slowly over seasons, which is a writeable evolution).

The literal register. "You are hurt." "He is afraid." "The door is open." Statements of what is. Doesn't editorialise.

The question register. "Why?" "What does that mean?" "Should I have done that?" The questions reveal his interior. They also slow scenes down in a way that is sometimes funny, sometimes devastating.

Combat dialogue. Probably none. Uno fights silently. The combat itself is the dialogue when he's in motion.

First major spoken scene (future, undecided). Bible doesn't lock. Worth saving for the right beat, probably a 3 Little Ninjaz scene where Uno has to define himself to the other two.

Discrepancies and Decisions

Creator and origin. Old Archive/Characters.pdf: "the first cyborg ninja, created by the police to combat other ninjas. However, his creator gave him a conscience, which made him uncontrollable. After the police tried to shut him down and killed his creator, Uno became a free agent." Series Bible: built by Dr Lucius Kane at Bio Genetix; military demanded autonomy strip; Kane refused and helped Uno escape; military EMP wiped memory; Bio Genetix believes him dead; Kane's fate uncertain. CANON: Series Bible. The "police creator" version is retired entirely. The substantive difference: Bio Genetix is the institutional villain, not the police; Kane's fate is uncertain rather than confirmed dead; the EMP is the specific damage mechanism.

Age. Old PDF "Unknown (Cyborg)." Bible "Appears: 13." CANON: appears 13. The body presents as 13.

Conscience as design feature. Old PDF: "his creator gave him a conscience, which made him uncontrollable." Bible: same idea, with the additional detail that Kane refused to strip it. CANON: Bible (preserves the moral architecture).

Abilities. Old PDF: "Enhanced strength and durability as a cyborg, advanced learning and adaptation abilities." Bible: same. CANON: locked.

Loyalty / protectiveness. Old PDF: "Loyal and protective." Bible: "childlike innocence with combat abilities." Both consistent. CANON: layered. The loyalty is earned through bonds (Donte), not programmed.

EMP memory damage. Bible adds. Old PDF silent. CANON: Bible. The fragmented memory is a key arc thread.

Chapter 9 bonding with Donte. Bible references; old PDF silent. CANON: Chapter 9 is the canonical tonal north star. Per workspace CLAUDE.md, Chapter 9 is the tone target for Hood Ninjaz writing. The Donte-Uno relationship anchors there.

No Aura. Bible §3 establishes Aura as the universal ninja power system. Uno operates outside that system entirely. CANON: Uno has no Aura. This makes him categorically distinct from every other significant character in the show. Worth holding deliberately.

Open Questions

  • Uno's first on-screen appearance. Bible says he's in the East Danim warehouse with Donte but doesn't specify an Episode 1 cameo. He is not in the current Episode 1 draft. Episode 2 reveal? Or held longer for impact?
  • Uno's combat style. Bible says combat capability retained from TANC base, but doesn't visualise the style. Mechanical? Adapted from observation? Hybrid?
  • Dr Lucius Kane's fate. Alive? Captured by Bio Genetix? In hiding? Looking for Uno? The answer shapes a Season 2 or 3 reveal.
  • Other TANCs from old Archive/Characters.pdf. The old PDF lists Dee-Day, Oxyde, Koko the Clown, Syren, others. Some of these may be early TANC prototypes (rather than human ninjas) in the new framing. Worth flagging during the Tier C pass.
  • Memory recovery. When and how do Uno's memories return? Is it gradual across seasons? Triggered by specific stimuli (seeing Kane's face, seeing another TANC, returning to Bio Genetix)?
  • Chapter 9 specific content. I have not directly read Archive/Book/Chapter 9.pdf in this session. Reading it would unlock Uno's first established voice, the specific texture of the silent bond, and the tonal anchor the rest of Hood Ninjaz writing is calibrated against. Worth surfacing into a dedicated Source Material/ file in Phase 3.
  • Uno's first spoken line on screen. Bible doesn't lock. Probably worth saving for a 3 Little Ninjaz scene where Uno has to define himself to Kevin or Donte.
  • The TANC architecture. Uno is the first fully autonomous TANC. The Bible's TANC evolution arc (Season 1 Prototype, Season 2 Adaptive, Season 3 Apex) describes TANCs that become more like Uno over time. The implication: the Apex TANCs in Season 3 are functionally closer to what Uno is. The horror of that parallel is worth building.

Scrapbook ingest (2026-08-05, from the original "3 Little Ninjaz" doc, now retired to BIN)

Origin texture worth keeping; consistent with the Bible summary, and the Bible wins on any clash:

  • Dr. Lucius Kane's escape play: the fake shutdown sequence, and the whispered final command in Uno's ear: "Run."
  • The EMP caught him at the river's edge; his vitals FLATLINED on the Bio Genetix monitors. That flatline is exactly why nobody ever hunted him: written off as destroyed, project moved on.
  • Kane, watching the flatline from behind his captors, shed a single tear ("No...") before being detained and dragged away. Fate uncertain: standing canon hook.
  • The body drifted for days in a small boat down the river before washing up at Danim City; systems rebooted with fragmented memory and the childlike innocence that defines him.
  • His central question, kept from the draft: is he a weapon or a person, and what makes someone human: body, mind, or soul.
