"How Hard Can It Be"

Outline v2, 2026-08-27. Title LOCKED by Bupe.

Bupe's brief, in his words: "everything needs to be traumatic, like seriously traumatic for Sharon and we need to traumatize the audience of how badly Sharon's life is fucked up, like we need to do everything bad. describe it, no pulling punches."

So the episode has one job. By the time the credits roll the audience should not be able to look at the woman from Episode 1 the same way again. She is competent, dry, unbothered, takes Nelson's shit in silence. E3 is why.

Where it comes from. Scrapbook/Sources/chapter-05.md is a complete origin in 42 fragments; the master Script adds SCR-039, SCR-040, SCR-041 and SCR-112. Nothing is invented except the joins and the intensification Bupe asked for.

THE THESIS, and it comes from Bupe's own note

He kept the law degree on the grounds that "she graduated but Jaden died so she didn't do nothing with it. But it proves she knows the law."

That is the episode. Sharon has a law degree. When a man talks his way past her refusal and holds her down, she knows the exact name of the crime being committed against her, the section it falls under, and what the evidence would need to be. She lies there and she catalogues it, because that is the only part of her still working.

And she does not report it.

Then, weeks later, she joins the police.

That is the wound the whole series is built on, and nobody in the show ever finds out. Every time she takes Nelson's harassment in silence, every time she swallows a senior officer's contempt, she is doing the thing she learned the night she decided the law was not for people like her.

CANON SET IN THIS EPISODE (Bupe's calls, 2026-08-27)

The grandmotherCanon. Alive through the early montage, in the graduation photograph. Dies of old age, off screen, between the degree and the present. Bupe: "that don't hurt cos even if it came down to it she died of old age." She is the one clean death in Sharon's life, and the contrast is the point: this is what a normal grief looks like, and it is the only one she ever gets.
The fatherNeither Sharon nor Kevin ever knew their father. Stated once, briefly, flat, as something the family lives with rather than a wound. A seed for later, so it stays under-explained.
The law firmCanon. She was taken on and lasted months. She does nothing with the degree after.
JennyThe street drug is called Jenny. From "Gen", as in Bio Genetix, and nobody on the street knows that. "Got a fresh batch of Jenny." Circulating in Danim roughly nine to thirteen years ago, which is Sharon's party years. She takes it and it does not take her.
The timelineRebuilt below and now canon.

The timeline, corrected and made canon

Verified 2026-08-27: the real UK route, the Detective Constable Entry Programme, is four years end to end and uniform first, two years as a uniformed constable then two developing into a detective, and it requires a degree. So the honest route would have put her in uniform until she was 31.

She did not take the honest route. That is the point (Bupe, 2026-08-27).

Age
19The boyfriend and the best friend
19 to 22The party years. Jenny. The jobs
23Road rage into law
25Graduates. Jaden "dies" the same week. The law firm. The spiral. The night
26"How hard can it be?" She applies
27Starts. Uniform
28She is noticed. The office. The ultimatum. The fast-track
29A detective, years before the route allows it
32, nowA Detective Constable, the most junior rank in CID, about three years in, and everybody in the building knows she skipped the queue

Why this makes Episode 1 work harder than it already did: the colleagues who resent her are correct that she was fast-tracked, and completely wrong about what it cost her. Nelson's line in E1 is not a slur he invented. It is the truth, said by a man who does not know he is telling it.

THE FAST-TRACK (Bupe, 2026-08-27). New canon, and it is the spine of her corruption.

What happens. SUPERINTENDENT TEDDY LUCAS (named by Bupe 2026-08-27) notices something in her that nobody has bothered to notice before: her talent is off the charts. She reads between the evidence. She holds detail nobody else holds. He tells her so, and he is not lying, and it is the first time in her adult life anyone has told her she is exceptional at anything.

Then he tells her the rest. No woman climbs the ranks here. Not on merit, not on results, not in twenty years. He is not asking her to sleep with him. He is explaining the tariff.

She does it. She gets on her knees in an office in a police station and she does it, and afterwards she is fast-tracked, and it works.

Why this is the worst thing in the episode, and worse than the night. The night was done to her. This she decided. She weighed it, she priced it, and she paid, because she had already learned the year before that saying no is a thing that other people get to do. She is not a victim in this scene and that is exactly why it will not leave her.

And it explains everything the audience has already seen. In Episode 1 Nelson circles her and says "What is it the Super sees in you? ...Or what is it he wants to put in you?", and she stares ahead and takes it. That line already shipped. It is not a rumour. She is standing there being told the truth by a man who thinks he is being crude, and she cannot react, because reacting is admitting it.

Register: the same rule as D1. Nothing of the act on screen, the camera stays with her, and nothing is softened about what it is or what she chose. Bupe's call if he wants it staged differently.

PROPOSAL, AWAITING BUPE, and it would make the whole corruption spine one piece. Canon already has a corrupt senior police officer on Paul Mitchell's payroll who feeds Sharon's intel to Bio Genetix (Bible s7). Vision proposes he is the same man. Then the fast-track was never about sex alone: he bought a detective whose talent he had already measured, and he owns her twice over. She believes she bought her career with one humiliation. In fact she was recruited as an asset, and every case she has ever handed up the chain has gone to Bio Genetix. "No woman climbs the ranks" was the lie that made her grateful for a leash.

THE TWO THINGS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE KNIFE (Bupe, 2026-08-27)

Two things put Sharon where she is.

One: her talent. It is real, it is exceptional, and on that alone she was going to be promoted anyway. Any normal person with that file gets fast-tracked without anybody asking them for anything.

Two: what she did in that office.

She eventually finds out she did it for nothing.

The promotion was already coming. He knew. He said nothing and took the price anyway, because the situation was there to be taken. It was never a transaction. It was a robbery dressed up as one, and she paid it willingly and has carried it since as the shameful thing she traded herself for.

What this does to the whole character, retroactively:

  • Every silence she has ever swallowed in that building, Nelson included, was protecting a secret that was never even the reason.
  • The one decision she made in her life that she cannot forgive herself for did not change a single outcome.
  • And she is the detective who reads between the evidence, which is the exact talent he complimented. She solved her own case eventually, and the answer took the ground out from under her.

HOW SHE FINDS OUT (Vision's proposal, Bupe's call). Not a confession and not a confrontation. Paperwork. Her own file, which is the one file she never thought to work. A recommendation for accelerated promotion, signed and dated before the day in the office. No malice on the page, no drama, just a date that is four words long and ends her.

WHO WROTE THE RECOMMENDATION: DCI MARCIA BOATENG (created 2026-08-27, profile in Characters). She also wrote the objection the day a Detective Constable was made lead on the ninja case, so both papers in Sharon's file carry the same signature and Sharon finds them together. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-31, Bupe: Boateng IS in E3. She is in a cubicle in the station toilets during THE TAP, comes out, washes her hands, reads Sharon's reflection in one flick of the eyes and says nothing, and stays at the sink watching the door after Sharon has gone. She is not named there and the audience is not told what she knows. (The original note read: Boateng is not in E3 and should not be.), but her recommendation is the page in the open file, so the document that ends Sharon exists from this episode onward and nobody has looked at it.

THE PLANT GOES IN E3 AND SHE MUST NOT SEE IT. In beat 24, the file is open on his desk the whole time. The camera can see it. She cannot, because she is not looking at the desk. The audience gets a glimpse of a page they have no reason to understand yet.

WHERE THE PAYOFF LANDS: Bupe's call, and it should be spent where it costs most. Canon has Sharon switching sides in Season 2. This is the thing that could break her loyalty to the force, because it is not the corruption that turns her, it is finding out she degraded herself for a promotion she had already earned.

SEPARATE AND INDICATED BUT NOT LOCKED: whether Lucas is also the corrupt senior officer already on Paul Mitchell's payroll feeding her intel to Bio Genetix (Bible s7). These are not the same question. He can be a pure opportunist who took what was there, or he can be an asset handler who wanted her promoted for his own reasons and charged her for it regardless. The second is darker and both work with the "for nothing" reveal.

ACT ONE: the frame

1. THE DRIVE. Straight out of E1's bin drop. She throws the stolen CCTV drive on the bed. It lands heavier than it should. She does not touch it again for forty minutes of screen time. (CH5-003)

2. THE PROMOTION, AND IT IS AN INSULT. The chief, purple about the wrecked building, needs a name and reaches for the nearest one. "Sharon! I'm placing you lead detective for this case." She is too stunned to answer. A year in the job and she has just been handed the city, by a man who was not thinking about her at all. (SCR-039, SCR-040)

3. THE SHOWER. Hot water. Steam. Eyes closed. The mirror fogs and takes her face off her. "But it wasn't always like this... I wasn't always like this." (CH5-004, CH5-010)

4. THE SPINE. Cold voiceover over the montage. "My name is Sharon Young. Six years ago I walked into a police station. I worked my ass off to get out the bullshit and earn my law degree. Made my mum proud. Made my grandparents proud. I never knew my father. None of us did. And none of it mattered. Not after that night." The father line goes past in under two seconds and is never picked up. (CH5-006, SCR-041)

ACT TWO: the descent, and it does not let up

Direction for the whole act: the humiliations are cumulative and specific. No montage gloss. Each one is a small, complete degradation, and the camera stays a beat longer than is comfortable every time.

5. NINETEEN. Bupe: this has to be in. She lets herself into the flat she pays half of. Coats on the floor. Her own bedroom door open. Her best friend is on her bed, in her sheets, with her boyfriend, and neither of them hears the door. She stands in the doorway long enough to take it in properly: the shape of them, her friend's hair on her own pillow, the noise of it. She says nothing.

They scramble. He gets his story going before he has his trousers on. Her friend cries and reaches for her.

Sharon packs. Methodically, around them, while they talk over each other, taking her clothes out from under her friend's discarded ones. She takes her things and not one thing that is his. She never raises her voice and she never says a word. At the door her friend says her name. She closes it behind her.

She was already numb. That is the horror of it: this is not the thing that broke her. (CH5-011, un-retired on Bupe's call)

6. THE PARTY YEARS, AND THEY ARE NOT FUN. Written as a decline, not a good time. The tightest dress. The first to go down and the first back up when somebody shakes her off a bathroom floor. A cubicle floor with her cheek on the tile and somebody's shoes by her face. Making herself sick and going back out. Losing shoes. Losing a phone. Losing a coat in November and walking home in the dress.

JENNY. Somebody in a smoking area says they have got a fresh batch of Jenny. She takes it because it is there. It does nothing to her, and she is disappointed. She never tries it again, and she never wonders why it did not work on her.

Drunk, she pulls whoever is closest, boy or girl, it does not matter to her, and it is not liberation, it is anaesthetic. The flat her mum and grandad pay for becomes a door that different people come through. Her mum visits once and does not say anything about the state of it, which is worse than if she had. (CH5-012, CH5-013, CH5-014, CH5-015)

7. THE FRIENDS GROW UP. One announces a pregnancy and Sharon has to be delighted about it at a table where she is the only one drinking. Another gets a job with a lanyard. They stop answering. She keeps going out. Same bar, same dress that is now a year out of date, nobody either side of her, waiting for anyone at all to walk over. The nights end the same way every time and she stops pretending they are about anything else. (CH5-016)

8. THE SUPERMARKET. The tannoy calls her to Aisle 4 by name. Smashed jars, something sticky spreading, a toddler still going and a mother watching Sharon get down on her knees in it. "Excuse me, are you actually going to clean that, or..." She kneels in it. Her manager wants two more hours and she says yes because the rent is more than the job. She is twenty-one and she has a mop. (CH5-017)

9. THE BAR. Every shift, hands. Some of them ask. Most of them do not. One of them puts a hand up her skirt while she is carrying two pints and the manager watches it happen and turns to the till. She learns not to make a scene, because making a scene costs her the shift.

Then she is drinking on shift, then she is drinking on shift to get through it, then she is caught. She is fired standing in the middle of a busy bar in front of everyone, and she walks out through them. (CH5-018)

This is where Sharon learns to swallow it. Every silence in Episode 1 is bought here.

10. THE TURN, AND IT IS FUNNY, AND IT NEEDS TO BE. Twenty-three, a driving lesson, and a screaming, purple, spit-flecked row at a junction with a man who was in the wrong. She gets home still furious and looks up whether she was technically right.

She was. She reads the next section. Then the one after. The one clean thing she ever does for herself starts because she needed to win an argument with a stranger. (CH5-019)

Let this beat breathe. It is the only air in the act, and taking it away later is what makes the rest unbearable.

11. LAW SCHOOL, DRUNK. She does not get clean. She passes hungover, on raw intelligence, out-arguing people who did the reading. The discipline is never actually built, which is why it collapses so completely. Her mum and her nan on the phone telling everyone. (CH5-020)

12. THE CAP, AND THE PHONE. Graduation. Her mum, her grandad, her nan, a photograph of the four of them. She throws the cap.

The cap is still in the air when the phone rings.

"No... it can't be." (CH5-007, CH5-021, CH5-022, SCR-048)

They told her. She has never once asked who "they" were. The audience already knows he is alive.

13. THE GRAVE. Cold. Small turnout. Her mum destroyed. Kevin is six and does not understand, and somebody has put him in a little black coat. Sharon does not cry at it and cannot make herself, and she can see people noticing that she is not crying.

The firm tells her to take compassionate leave. She refuses and comes in the next morning. Then she stops coming in at all. The degree is never used again. (CH5-023)

14. HER NAN DIES. Old age, at home, in her sleep. Bupe: this one does not hurt. And it is the cruelest thing in the episode, because it is the only death in Sharon's life that was allowed to be normal, and she stands at that funeral understanding exactly what a grief is supposed to feel like, and knowing she was not given one. (New, on Bupe's call)

ACT THREE: the floor

15. THE BAR, ANY BAR. A man buys her a drink. She barely registers his face. They leave together. Written deliberately blank, like every other night, so that what happens next lands as an interruption. (CH5-024)

16. THE REFUSAL. At her door, key in the lock, something surfaces in her for the first time in years. It is a want, and it is a no.

"I don't think I want you to come in." (CH5-025)

17. HE TALKS OVER IT. The smile drops for half a second and comes back different. He is warm about it. He is reasonable about it. He makes her feel rude. She unlocks the door.

Inside, he stops being warm. He gets direct, then he gets physical, and he shoves her onto the bed and pulls her clothes off her while she goes limp. She never consents and she never fights. (CH5-026, SCR-049)

18. THE CEILING.

REGISTER: the camera does not leave her eyeline. Bupe's D1 ruling, locked. The ceiling. A crack in it. A light fitting with a dead fly in it. Nothing of the act is on screen. Nothing is softened either: the sound is in the room, his weight is in the frame, and it does not cut away early.

Under it, this is where the law degree pays. Her voiceover does not scream and does not plead. It catalogues. She knows what this is called. She knows what she would need. She knows what a defence would say about the fact that she opened her own front door, and she knows, correctly, exactly how that would go.

And when he finishes, she puts her arms around him and holds him, still staring at the ceiling.

His weight comes down on her and she cannot breathe under it, and she does not move him. (CH5-027, and the hug is not optional, it is the reason the scene exists)

19. AFTER. She does not move while he dresses. She watches him do his belt. He looks pleased with himself. She feels the anger arrive and she says nothing, and he lets himself out, and the door does not even slam.

The shower, too hot. Feeling nothing.

The medicine cabinet: birth control, painkillers, sleeping pills. A whole person in three objects. She takes the pill with no more ceremony than brushing her teeth, looking at a ghost in the glass. (CH5-028, CH5-029)

20. THE MORNING, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD HURT MOST. She goes to work. She changes the sheets first. She does not phone anybody. She does not phone her mum.

And she does not report it, and she is the one person in this story who knows precisely what she is choosing not to do. The law degree is on the wall of the same flat.

ACT FOUR: how hard can it be

21. THE TELEVISION. Drying her hair. A news report: a police chase, and the suspect gets away, and the reporter is generous about it. "You don't know how to do your job." Beat. "Maybe if you did, people like Jaden wouldn't die." (CH5-030)

22. FOUR WORDS. Her reflection lands in the glass of her framed law degree. The woman she is now, sitting on top of the thing she was. "How hard can it be?"

The camera holds on the reflection. This is the turn of the entire episode, and it is not triumphant. It is a woman with nothing left choosing the one door still open. (CH5-031)

23. UNIFORM. Application, training, nights. Petty thieves, shoplifters, domestics, paperwork. All of it with the pain packed underneath rather than resolved. She is good at it, and she is good at it for an ugly reason: she can out-argue anyone in the room, and nothing anybody says to her can touch her any more. (CH5-032)

24. THE OFFICE. New, Bupe 2026-08-27. This is the second hinge of the episode and it goes here.

The door says SUPERINTENDENT LUCAS. So does the plate on the desk. That is how the audience gets his name and his rank, on screen, with nobody introducing him.

Superintendent Teddy Lucas closes the door behind her. He has her file open on the desk and he leaves it open. He tells her she is the best natural investigator to come through that building in years, that she sees between the evidence, that she holds detail nobody else holds. He means it. It is the first time in her adult life that anybody has told her she is exceptional at anything, and she feels it land.

The camera has a clear look at that open file. She never does, because she is looking at him and then at the door. There is a page in it the audience is given no reason to read yet.

Then he tells her the rest of it. No woman climbs the ranks here. Not on merit, not on results, not in twenty years. He says it the way you read out a policy.

He is not asking. He is quoting a price.

She looks at the door. She looks at the file with her name on it, the only door still open, the degree she never used, the flat, the years.

She gets on her knees.

Camera stays with her, same rule as the night. Nothing of it on screen. Nothing softened about what it is either.

Afterwards she washes her hands in a station toilet and goes back to work, and the fast-track comes through, and it works.

He closes the file. Hold on it for one beat longer than the scene needs.

25. AND THIS IS WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE NIGHT. The night was done to her. This she decided. She priced it and she paid, because the year before had already taught her that saying no is something other people get to do.

She is not a victim in this scene, and that is exactly why it will never leave her.

And it was for nothing. Her talent alone had already earned the promotion; the recommendation was written before she walked into that room. He knew, and he took the price anyway, because it was there to take. She does not find that out for years. The audience does not find it out here either. They just saw a file left open.

Cut forward: the warrant card. Detective. Two colleagues watching her walk past with it, and one of them says something to the other.

ACT FIVE: the alley, three years in

26. THE DONUT SHOP. Newly a detective. She catches herself being a detective eating a donut and is annoyed about it. She is putting it down as she sees them. (CH5-033)

27. "I'LL NANK YOU, BRUV!" Two figures in black in an alley, one threatening to stab the other. She draws. (CH5-034)

28. FREEZE. POLICE. Textbook. Gun up, stance right, voice steady. They laugh until one of them has to hold the wall. "Girl said 'freeze', yano!" "Or else what, darling? Arrest us?"

Everything she has built in six years is worth nothing here, and it takes four seconds to find that out. (CH5-035)

29. "MOVE." The laughing stops because they are looking past her. One syllable, and her body obeys before her mind does. "Run along. You don't belong here." He is not named. (CH5-036)

30. THE DEMONSTRATION. The gun is out of her hands before she registers movement, and he crushes it. She reaches for her radio and he is already holding it, and crushes that too. Two objects, two capabilities, and he never touches her. (CH5-037)

31. THE CALL SHE CANCELS. Running. "This is Detective Sharon Young! I need backup at... there's... there's something... I mean someone..." She hangs up mid-sentence, because she has just heard herself. (CH5-039, and "7th and Maple" becomes a Danim location)

32. SHE GOES BACK. Empty. No ninjas, no man. Only her own gun in pieces on the ground. "How?" The evidence proves it to her and to nobody else. (CH5-040)

33. THE STATION. A colleague takes her statement with his pen barely moving. "So you're telling me a guy just appeared out of nowhere, crushed your gun... and vanished?" She hears exactly how it sounds while she is saying it. She stands up hard enough to put the chair over. "Forget it!" Nobody believed her about this either. (CH5-041)

34. THE MISSION. "Whatever this is, whatever just happened... it's not over. I'm going to find the truth." Played straight, never winked at. The audience will eventually learn that her pursuit of the truth is the exact lever Bio Genetix uses on her. (CH5-042)

ACT SIX: out of the water, and the call

35. PRESENT DAY. She steps out of the shower. The drive is still on the bed.

36. THE WORK. In her underwear, cooking, eating, the stolen disc playing. "Some kind of new androids? British Intelligence couldn't have made something that powerful, could they?" It is the right theory for a rational person with no supernatural framework, and it is wrong. (SCR-112)

37. THE WRIST. She gets down on all fours and crawls across her own living room floor to squint at a frozen, pixelated frame. The mark on his wrist. Third independent sighting: Spike reported it, the CCTV caught it, she is chasing it. She has no idea what she is looking at. (SCR-112)

38. THE PHONE. IT IS HER MUM. Bupe's ending.

Not Sharon chasing her family this time. The family reaching her. Her mum has Kevin home from the worst night of his life and something is not right with him, and she is ringing the daughter who is police because she does not know who else to ring.

The rhyme is the whole point. In E1 Sharon rang Kevin and he did not pick up because he had earphones in on a bus. In E3 the call comes the other way and it is far too late to be about a haircut. She is on her floor an inch from a frozen frame of a man she cannot explain, and the phone in her hand is her mother, about her brother.

She has spent the entire episode learning that nobody believes what you see.

Now she is the one who has to believe somebody.

Cut. End of Episode 3.

Still open

  1. D1's remaining detail level. The eyeline is locked and Act Three holds it. How much of her interiority survives is Bupe's, pending his re-read of chapter-05.md CH5-025 onward. If "no pulling punches" was meant to reopen the camera position as well, say so and it changes.
  2. Jenny not working on Sharon sits interestingly beside her profile's "possibly water-exposed as a child but never trained". Deliberate connection, or coincidence?
  3. SCR-023 (Sharon watching, arousal, "...Whatever.") is already carried in E1 per decision D2. Not duplicated here.

Plan parked 2026-06-24. The road from where we are now to the first visual pitch artifact. Build not yet started; Phase 0 is the next move.

The deliverable (MVP)

A 60-90 second narrated animatic of one Episode 1 sequence: roughly 20-40 curated still frames, Ken Burns motion (pan/zoom/parallax), Bupe's voiceover telling the story, scored with a track from the existing Hood Ninjaz music library. A pitch artifact someone can watch and get the world.

This deliberately sidesteps the one thing AI still cannot do well in mid-2026: fluid, character-consistent fight animation. Full episode animation is a separate, much larger project we are not starting yet. The animatic is the correct first deliverable.

The dependency chain (order is load-bearing)

Look -> Characters -> World -> Scenes -> Assemble. Each stage inherits the one before. No stage starts before its predecessor is locked.

Verified machine state (2026-06-24; re-verified on the box 2026-08-05)

  • GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti, 8192 MiB (8GB) VRAM confirmed via nvidia-smi. (Windows WMI misreported 4GB, a known wrap bug on cards above 4GB.) Driver 610.62 as of 5 Aug (was 610.47).
  • CPU: Intel i7-11700 (11th gen). Fine; near-irrelevant for diffusion.
  • System RAM: ~16GB. This is the real constraint. ComfyUI offloads to system RAM when VRAM fills; SDXL plus a heavy node stack on 16GB will get tight. Not a blocker. If look-dev gets sluggish, 32GB is a cheap fix.
  • Python 3.12 and Git present. ffmpeg NOW INSTALLED (found 5 Aug: winget Gyan.FFmpeg 8.1.2 full build; fresh shells may need the full path C:\Users\bupe\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\Gyan.FFmpeg_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe\ffmpeg-8.1.2-full_build\bin\ffmpeg.exe, a known winget PATH quirk).
  • Disk: D: has ~1.8TB free (5 Aug); model downloads are unconstrained.

ComfyUI installs found (two)

  • C:\Users\bupe\Documents\ComfyUI - barebones. One checkpoint: DreamShaper 8 (SD1.5, below the quality bar). Retire / ignore. (Still present 5 Aug; deleting it to reclaim disk is Bupe's click, it sits outside Vision.)
  • D:\ComfyUI-Easy-Install (app root nested at ...\ComfyUI-Easy-Install\ComfyUI-Easy-Install\ComfyUI-Easy-Install\ComfyUI) - the real one. Already loaded with: ComfyUI-Manager, controlnet_aux (pose/depth/lineart preprocessors), KJNodes, rgthree, was-node-suite, Comfyroll, TiledDiffusion (low-VRAM upscaling), VideoHelperSuite, WanVideoWrapper, LTXVideo, GGUF, Florence2, inspyrenet-rembg, plus two local TTS engines: VibeVoice and Kokoro (free local voiceover). Re-checked 5 Aug (34 custom nodes): still no anime base checkpoint, no ControlNet model files, no SDXL VAE (models dir holds only a flux-lineage clip_l + ae.safetensors), and the IPAdapter node is confirmed ABSENT (was "to confirm"; install via Manager in Phase 0).

Why this stack (verified direction)

  • SDXL architecture, not Flux/SD3.5. SDXL still has the deepest LoRA/ControlNet/community ecosystem in early 2026, which the whole pipeline depends on. Flux/SD3.5 have better prompt understanding but a thinner ecosystem and would choke 8GB anyway.
  • Illustrious family base (anime SDXL). Recommendation: a style-neutral Illustrious fine-tune (e.g. WAI-Illustrious or Hassaku) as a clean launchpad rather than a strongly-opinionated checkpoint. Verify the current best version live before downloading (the landscape moves fast; do not name from memory). Landscape checked 2026-08-05: WAI-Illustrious-SDXL and Hassaku XL still read as the style-neutral bases; current alternatives are Nova Anime XL (Illustrious-based, May 2026, higher background detail) and NoobAI-XL V-Pred (strong tag comprehension; v-pred needs matching sampler settings). Final pick stays a go-time call from fresh Civitai samples Bupe judges.
  • Not Pony. Older separate lineage; its LoRA ecosystem does not cross with Illustrious. Illustrious has current momentum.
  • Prompting is tag-driven (Danbooru/booru tags), not prose, with a quality-vocab stack up front. Scene prompts will be structured tag strings.
  • The Series Bible's 15-18 rating (blood, real violence, honest sex) is a fit: Illustrious anime fine-tunes handle mature content natively.

The pipeline

Phase 0 - Foundation (one-time, ~1 hour, local)

  • Consolidate on the D: install. Confirm it launches. Retire the Documents one.
  • Verify current best Illustrious SDXL checkpoint, show Bupe samples, he picks. Download (~6.5GB).
  • Download supporting models: SDXL ControlNet model files (pose/depth/lineart; controlnet_aux only does preprocessing), IPAdapter model + CLIP vision, SDXL VAE. Install the IPAdapter node via Manager (confirmed absent 5 Aug).
  • ~~Install ffmpeg~~ DONE (found installed 5 Aug, winget 8.1.2; see machine state for the full-path quirk).
  • Set up the Hood Ninjaz library structure (locked prompt stacks, character reference sets, environment plates, scene prompts) so work compounds.
  • Gate: Bupe approves the base checkpoint from samples.

Phase 1 - Lock the look (local, creative core)

  • Feed existing poster art + PSD into IPAdapter as style reference. Iterate booru-tag prompts until the gritty UK-grime-anime look lands. Find the look before training anything.
  • Output: a style bible = locked prompt stack (quality tags + style descriptors + negatives), 3-5 hero frames, exact settings (sampler/scheduler/CFG/steps/seed).
  • Gate: Bupe signs off the look.

Phase 2 - Characters (local, curation-first)

Key refinement: do NOT train LoRAs for the MVP. For a 20-40 frame pitch, hold consistency with a locked prompt block + reference art via IPAdapter + curation (generate several, keep the on-model one). Training is the industrial step for hundreds of consistent shots. Introduce a per-character LoRA only if a character won't hold, or once scaling past the pitch. This removes cloud training from the critical path.

  • Build a locked block per hero, starting Kevin (gold+white, saved look-test prompts exist), Face (locked sheet: full back tattoo, gold armour wrapping to back, two crossed antique daggers, cel-shaded), Jaden (gold). Use existing reference art in the Characters folders; respect the locked cast colour map (Jaden gold / Jon blue / Face black; Kevin gold+white / Donte black+white / Uno green+white).
  • Output: locked reference set + prompt block per character.
  • Gate: characters hold across test shots, or flag which one needs a LoRA.

Phase 3 - World (local)

  • Build environment prompt blocks for the Danim City locations the slice needs (Jon's barbershop, the alley, night-city grime). Same locked style stack.
  • Output: environment plate library.

Phase 4 - Scenes (local, combines the above)

  • Pick the Episode 1 sequence; break into a shot list (the ai-filmmaking skill does shot list + per-shot prompts).
  • Per shot: locked character block + locked environment block + ControlNet (OpenPose or rough sketch) for pose/composition + style stack + fixed seed. Generate several, curate the keeper.
  • Upscale keepers with TiledDiffusion (tiled, fits 8GB) to a clean slideshow resolution.
  • Output: final still set for the sequence.

Phase 5 - Voice + assembly (Bupe's home turf - editing background)

  • Script: narration from the completed Episode 1 draft.
  • Voiceover: ElevenLabs (MCP, top quality) vs local VibeVoice/Kokoro (free, installed). Test both, pick.
  • Music: from the existing Hood Ninjaz soundtrack library (Archive/Soundtracks).
  • Assemble in Resolve/Premiere: Ken Burns + parallax synced to VO + score. Optional SFX (ElevenLabs sound effects).
  • Output: the narrated animatic.

Cost and hardware reality

WhatWhereCost
All generation, look-dev, characters, world, scenes, upscale, local TTSLocal (3070 Ti)Free
Per-character LoRA training (only if a character won't hold)Cloud (RunPod)~£1-2/character ballpark; verify live if reached
Voiceover (optional)ElevenLabs (MCP)Existing plan

8GB VRAM runs SDXL inference fine (~20-40s/image). Watch the 16GB system RAM under the heavy node stack.

On connecting ComfyUI to Vision

No ComfyUI MCP needed for the build phase. Vision (Claude Code) runs on the machine and drives ComfyUI directly: launch the server, place models, write and queue workflow JSON against the /prompt API, pull outputs. A Cloudflare-worker MCP bridge (the Hevy pattern) only earns its place later for headless batch queueing.

Open decisions (gates for Bupe)

  1. NEW, flagged 2026-08-05: the engine call. This plan predates the Higgsfield Ultimate/Unlimited era, which became the house image engine in late July 2026 (nano_banana_pro 2K stills effectively free on the Unlimited toggle, Kling 3.0 image-to-video, the Recipe Book prompt system, the three-panel character-sheet law). The animatic's 20-40 stills could plausibly be made Higgsfield-first with zero local setup. What local ComfyUI still uniquely offers: ControlNet pose/composition control, IPAdapter style-locking to the existing poster art, unlimited iterations at volume, no platform moderation on the 15-18 rating's blood and real violence, and the LoRA path if this scales past the pitch. What Higgsfield offers: no downloads or VRAM ceiling, the already-proven house prompt craft, and optional Kling motion for 2-3 hero beats. Both are effectively free. Bupe picks: ComfyUI as planned, Higgsfield-first, or hybrid (Higgsfield look-dev now, ComfyUI where control or content latitude demands it). Until he picks, nothing downloads.
  2. Base checkpoint (if ComfyUI) - Vision shows samples, Bupe picks.
  3. Which Episode 1 sequence is the vertical slice (opening, or the Jaden/Spike beat).
  4. Character scope for the slice - Kevin + Face + Jaden, or fewer.
  5. Voiceover - test ElevenLabs vs local and compare.

Priority guard

Creative side-project. SEN Help (quiz cutover 24 Aug) is the quarter's priority (re-verified against context/priorities.md 5 Aug; the site itself launched 25 Jul). Timebox this so it does not bleed into SEN Help. Phase 0 is ~1 hour. Phase 1 (look-dev) is the real iterative time-sink. Suggested first block: Phase 0 + a first look-dev pass, then judge whether the output justifies going further.

Status

Parked. Re-verified and refreshed 2026-08-05 (machine facts, checkpoint landscape, ffmpeg done, IPAdapter gap confirmed). Next move when Bupe is ready: his engine call (open decision 0), then Phase 0. Nothing downloads until he picks.

Danim City Police: ranks, and who is what

Source
Danim City Police (ranks and who is what).md

Bupe's instruction 2026-08-27: "we need to establish everyone's rank which original to UK authentically." This is the single home for it.

Contents
  1. The real ladder (verified 2026-08-27)
  2. The cast
  3. What this does to Episode 1, free
  4. The one change to a signed-off episode
  5. Where Sharon ends up: Vision's proposal, Bupe's call
  6. Open

Bupe's instruction 2026-08-27: "we need to establish everyone's rank which original to UK authentically." This is the single home for it. Verified against the real England and Wales structure, not written from memory.

Danim is a fictional big British city with London texture, so the force is modelled on a metropolitan force. No American ranks. There is no such thing as a police captain or a police chief in England and Wales.

The real ladder (verified 2026-08-27)

RankWhat they actually do
1Constable (PC)The rank everyone starts at. There is no rank below it
2Sergeant (PS)Supervises a team of constables
3InspectorRuns a shift or a unit. Oversees investigations
4Chief InspectorSupervises inspectors, runs significant operations
5SuperintendentRuns a large area or district. Makes high level operational calls
6Chief SuperintendentLeads a whole division. Budgets, objectives, major investigations
7+Commander, then Deputy Assistant Commissioner, Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, CommissionerChief officer ranks. In non-metropolitan forces this tier is Assistant Chief Constable, Deputy Chief Constable, Chief Constable

Detectives are not a separate ladder. They hold the same ranks with "Detective" in front: DC, DS, DI, DCI, Detective Superintendent, Detective Chief Superintendent. A DC does not outrank a uniformed PC. They are the same rank doing different work.

Who runs a murder. The Senior Investigating Officer, the SIO. Normally a DCI as the minimum, and a Detective Superintendent for the most serious. Forces can appoint someone more junior "if circumstances dictate", which is the loophole Danim's corruption drives a bus through.

How officers actually speak. "Guv" or "boss" to an Inspector or above. "The Super" for a Superintendent. DC is Detective Constable, DS is Detective Sergeant, DI is Detective Inspector, DCI is Detective Chief Inspector. "Ma'am" and "sir" upward. Nobody says "captain" and nobody says "chief" about a police officer.

The cast

CharacterRankNotes
Teddy LucasSuperintendentBupe's call. "Superintendent Lucas" on the door and on the desk plate in Sharon's E3 flashback, which is how the audience gets his name and his power in one shot. Senior enough to force a fast-track through and to be untouchable by a DC
Sharon Young, nowDetective Constable (DC)The most junior rank in CID. Lucas fast-tracked her PC to DC at 28, skipping the four-year route. Three years on she is still a DC, and everybody in that building knows she jumped the queue
NelsonDetective Sergeant (DS)One rank above her, deliberately. His contempt has teeth because he technically outranks her, and there is nothing she can do about any of it. Explains "why is it always you I have to cover for"
The second officer, the crude asideDCA peer. Worse for being a peer
The one who puts her on the caseSuperintendent LucasNot an open question: canon since 2026-05-12. He assigned her to the special task force. A Superintendent overriding the normal SIO rules to install a DC is exactly the abuse of the "if circumstances dictate" loophole
Marcia BoatengDetective Inspector (DI), fifteen years at that rankTwenty-three years in. Made DS then DI fast on undeniable work, then stopped dead, because she refused Lucas and everyone like him. The obvious next officer for the case and passed over for a DC, which is why she objected in writing. She is not the disproof of Lucas's "no woman climbs the ranks here". She is the PROOF. He was describing his own handiwork
The Boss LadyNot police. Leave her as "the chief"She commands the men in black, who E1 establishes are out of jurisdiction. A non-police agency has no business with police ranks, so her title is correct as shipped and stays

What this does to Episode 1, free

Sharon is a Detective Constable being handed the biggest case in the city. The SIO should be a DCI at minimum. A DC being made lead is not a promotion, it is an outrage, and every officer in that building knows it.

So without one line of new dialogue:

  • Nelson's contempt is procedurally justified, which makes it far worse than if he were just a bully.
  • The station's refusal to believe her about the alley is what happens to the most junior detective in the room.
  • A chief in a temper handing her the city is exactly the kind of decision that gets made about people who do not matter.
  • And she cannot escalate any of it, because the man she would escalate to is Lucas.

The one change to a signed-off episode

E1 currently has Nelson say "What is it the captain sees in you? ...Or what is it he wants to put in you?"

"Captain" is not a UK rank and has to go. The replacement does more work than the original:

"What is it the Super sees in you?"

"The Super" is exactly how officers talk about a Superintendent, it is unmistakably British, and it now points directly at Teddy Lucas by rank. The line stops being a vague slur about a nameless boss and becomes a specific, accurate accusation about a specific man, said by someone who thinks he is only being crude.

Where Sharon ends up: Vision's proposal, Bupe's call

Bupe asked what she ends up being. Three shapes:

A. She never gets promoted again. (Recommended.) The single promotion of her life was the one she paid for, and it turns out she had already earned it. She stays a DC for the entire series. The loop closes: she was owed a career, was robbed of the honest version of it, and never gets another. Everything she achieves after that is achieved by the most junior detective in Danim, which makes it hers.

B. She makes Detective Inspector on merit, and it is ashes. By the time it is offered she knows the first one was free, so taking it admits the first was a lie and refusing it costs her everything. Strong, and it needs a scene to land.

C. She ends up outside the force entirely. Canon has her switching sides in Season 2. If the truth about Lucas is what breaks her, the rank she ends on is no rank at all, and she works the ninja world as a civilian who used to be police.

Vision's read: A and C are the same story told at different lengths, and both are stronger than B. She stays a DC until the force stops being where she belongs.

Open

  1. ~~Who makes her lead~~ CLOSED. It is Lucas, and it has been canon since 2026-05-12. He assigned her to the special task force, he is the corrupt officer feeding her intel to Bio Genetix via Paul Mitchell, and the reveal lands at the end of Season 1.
  2. ~~Whether the E1 line changes~~ DONE 2026-08-27. "Captain" is out of all three E1 files.
  3. ~~Whether anyone objects on the record~~ BUILT 2026-08-27 on Bupe's instruction: DCI MARCIA BOATENG. She objected in writing and was overruled by Lucas. She also wrote the accelerated-promotion recommendation years earlier, so both documents in Sharon's file carry the same signature. Profile: Characters/Marcia Boateng/Marcia Boateng.md.

EVER WONDERED: the white-eye cutaways

Source
Ever Wondered (white-eye cutaways).md

Bupe's device, ruled and named 2026-08-27 (Scrapbook decision B4).

Contents
  1. What it is, in his words
  2. The ruling on the white eyes (B4)
  3. The rules (so it stays a motif and never becomes noise)
  4. The bank (Vision's proposals, 2026-08-27, unapproved: Bupe picks)

Bupe's device, ruled and named 2026-08-27 (Scrapbook decision B4). A recurring motif, not a plot thread. Its single home is this file; projects/hood-ninjaz/CLAUDE.md points here and does not repeat it.

What it is, in his words

"It was basically me just playing devil's advocate and pushing thoughts like you ever wondered what could be happening when a tube stops in the middle of the tunnel. Things that happen in day to day lives have ninja activity, to make people wonder like wow that could be happening. Situations that look innocent but add a ninja doing something you would never think of as a means to push corrupt assumptions in our real day to day life. Provocative thoughts."

So: take a thing every British viewer has personally sat through and been mildly annoyed by, and answer the question nobody asks about it. The answer is always ninja activity, and it is always corrupt.

The ruling on the white eyes (B4)

The three sightings in the old notes are not one linked signature, and treating them as one was Vision's suggestion, not Bupe's.

SightingRuling
The figure in the underground tunnel taking a package (SCR-102)Abstract background. Not a character. It exists to say that when a tube stops mid tunnel, transactions are happening. This is the seed of the whole device.
Eve's shadow snakes (SCR-116)Abstract background. Not linked to the others.
The ninja who puts Dez into a paralytic trance (SCR-064)A real character, and the exception. He is genuinely attractive, and he turns his eyes white to activate the ability. Here the white eyes are a power being switched on, not set dressing.

So white eyes carry two unrelated jobs and the show never explains either. In the cutaways they are the costume. On the Dez ninja they are a trigger.

The rules (so it stays a motif and never becomes noise)

  1. Never explained. Never followed up. Never plot-relevant in the moment. If a cutaway ever pays off later it stops being this device.
  2. The mundane frame comes first. The audience should recognise the annoyance before they notice the figure. The ninja is the second thing you see, not the first.
  3. Nobody in the scene reacts. Commuters keep scrolling. Life carries on. That is the horror of it.
  4. Standard ninja costume, white eyes, every time. The consistency is the joke and the threat.
  5. One per episode maximum, dropped into the gap between two heavy beats. Two in an episode kills it.
  6. British and specific. Not "a city". A night bus, a chicken shop, a Southern Rail delay.
  7. No dialogue. Ever.

Archer is the one voice allowed over these, per the 2026-08-27 narration ruling: he comments to the audience, a side angle or a clap back, never to a character. This device and that ruling were made in the same session and they were made for each other. Kept rare, as instructed.

The bank (Vision's proposals, 2026-08-27, unapproved: Bupe picks)

Bupe's own, canonical, the template for the rest:

  • THE TUBE STOPS IN THE TUNNEL. Lights dip. Nobody looks up from their phone. Between two carriages, a handover.

Proposed:

  • THE NIGHT BUS THAT DOESN'T STOP. Full stop, hand out, driver stares dead ahead and sails past. Upstairs at the back, two figures who did not get on at any stop.
  • THE ROADWORKS WITH NOBODY WORKING. Cones and a closed lane that have been there eleven months. No workmen, ever. One night a steel plate lifts from underneath.
  • "A PERSON ON THE TRACKS." The announcement everyone groans at because it will make them late. There is a person on the tracks. He is walking the live rail in the dark, unhurried.
  • THE CHICKEN SHOP THAT NEVER CLOSES AND NEVER HAS CUSTOMERS. Everybody knows one. The fryer is cold. The man behind the counter has been standing in exactly that spot for six years.
  • THE CAMERA POINTED AT THE WALL. One CCTV camera on a street, turned to face brickwork. Somebody turned it. He is still on the pole.
  • THE FIRE ALARM TEST. Same time every week, same building. Ninety seconds of noise that nobody is allowed to react to, and something crosses three floors inside it.
  • THE SCAFFOLDING THAT NEVER COMES DOWN. Sheeted, lit, no work done in two years. It is not holding the building up. It is holding something in.
  • THE OUT OF SERVICE CASHPOINT. Screen dead for weeks, people walk past it without a glance. It is not broken. It is a door.
  • THE VAN WITH ITS ENGINE RUNNING. Ten minutes on a quiet road. Nobody gets out. Nobody was ever going to.
  • THE PLANE THAT CIRCLES. Holding pattern over Danim, third loop. Somebody in the cabin is counting the loops.
  • THE BIN LORRY AT 4AM. Blocking a one way street for exactly as long as it needs to be blocked.
  • THE SKIP OUTSIDE THE EMPTY HOUSE. Things go in. Nothing ever comes out. The skip is never collected.

Standing instruction: this list is meant to grow. Any session that thinks of a good one adds it here rather than putting it in a script.

KUGA (spin-off note)

Source
KUGA (spin-off note).md

Opened 2026-08-10, Bupe's idea, in the same session that built the Kega and Kūga mythology.

Contents
  1. The pitch
  2. Why it can carry its own show
  3. The opening sequence (locked in the Bible, section 4)
  4. Tone
  5. Open (Bupe)

Opened 2026-08-10, Bupe's idea, in the same session that built the Kega and Kūga mythology. Note only, not a commission. Nothing here is outlined, nothing is scheduled, and it sits behind the main series and the production pipeline. It exists so the material is not lost and so the main series stops accidentally contradicting it.

Canon home stays the Series Bible (section 4 for Kūga, section 9 for Kega). This file holds only what is specific to the spin-off.

The pitch

2,000 years. One being with no self, passed through the worst centuries humans have.

Kūga wakes with no nature, no judgment, no memory and no place, because the god he was cut out of removed him from the order rather than killing him. He becomes what he is exposed to and amplifies it. The series is the record of what he was exposed to.

It runs from the Severing (6,000 years before Hood Ninjaz present day) to the Second Seal (4,000 years before), and it ends where the main series' mythology begins: ten gods dying to put him in a crystal.

Why it can carry its own show

The growth curve is flat then vertical. Tetration is almost nothing for a very long time. So for centuries he is a nobody being passed from hand to hand, unremarkable, and the horror is that nothing appears to be happening. There is no power-creep problem and no need to escalate artificially: the maths does it.

He is not the protagonist in the usual sense. He is the thing history happens to. Each era gives you a new cast around a constant, which is a structure that can run indefinitely without the lead needing an arc in every season.

His 2,000 free years cover the entire rise of human civilisation. Every empire, every war, every conquest. He did not watch it, he was passed through it. The spin-off can go anywhere on earth.

The opening sequence (locked in the Bible, section 4)

  1. The Severing. Kega passes the verdict on himself. No cut, no wound. Part of him simply stops being included.
  2. The bushes. A village man finds a naked, frail man lying there and, for no reason at all, helps him up, bathes him, clothes him, takes him in.
  3. The raid. The village is attacked. People are taken as slaves. Frail, weak Kūga is one of them.

The kindness lasted days. The violence lasted centuries. That is the whole thesis of both shows in one sequence.

And it is the root of the main series' ending. The first thing that ever happened to Kūga was a stranger being good to him for nothing. When Kevin's people get amplified in Hood Ninjaz Season 3, that is not a new input. It is the first one, met once, four thousand years before the seal, and too brief to take.

Tone

Heavy. Starting him in a slave chain is the strongest engine available and it puts the spin-off in the same thematic room as the main series rather than off to the side. The Seven Pillars apply: no gore or degradation for shock value alone. Trust the audience.

The village man should be the smallest possible part and the most important thing in the show. He gets no name, no arc and no return. He is why the ending of Hood Ninjaz works.

Open (Bupe)

  • What is left behind at the Severing site. Residue, a scar in the land, or the seed of what the Sphere is later made from. Named as open in Bible section 4.
  • Which eras get episodes. The 2,000 years are deliberately unmapped.
  • Whether the village man's kindness is ever shown to Kūga again, or stays buried until the main series pays it off. Recommend the latter.
  • Format. Series, limited series, or a book told in the Original Book of Ninja's voice, which would feed the physical-book production note in Bible section 4.

The TANC arc: the chain to Sonya

Source
The TANC Arc - the chain to Sonya.md

Bupe's dictation, 2026-08-27, out of Scrapbook decision C4.

Contents
  1. Why it exists
  2. The chain, in order
  3. Where it sits
  4. Rulings this settles
  5. THE SONAR: how Sonya sees, and it is now a visual system (Bupe, 2026-08-27, answering D3)
  6. THE GATE (Bupe's call, by right, and not Vision's)

Bupe's dictation, 2026-08-27, out of Scrapbook decision C4. He was answering a small question about three unused names and gave the end of the TANC arc instead. This is the single home for that chain; the Series Bible section 9 points here.

Status: the CHAIN is canon. The staging of Sonya's death is NOT settled and is Bupe's call (see the gate at the bottom). Nothing here gets written into a script until he sets the register.

Why it exists

The Season One closing list carries three names that appear nowhere else: Igo, Sonya and Giga. One line reads "Eve did love Giga", past tense. That past tense was the thread, and pulling it produced the whole sequence below.

Sonya was already canon and nobody had connected her to it. Bible section 6: early 20s, blind shinobi, mixed Japanese and Black heritage, heightened senses making her one of the most dangerous fighters, calm, introspective, strong sense of justice.

The chain, in order

1. Eve dies. Spectacularly, killed by a TANC, and she kills that TANC in the process. This is what puts "did" into "Eve did love Giga". Bupe has the end and not the journey: the road to it is unwritten.

2. Giga goes for revenge and dies. He hunts a TANC to avenge her. He injures it badly and it survives, and worse than surviving, it has gathered a great deal of data on the ninja.

3. The interception. The damaged TANC never reaches headquarters. Sonya intercepts it, kills it, and destroys the data, and she does it just in time, because ranked 2 of the top 5 was already coming to retrieve it.

4. Sonya is taken. She is overwhelmed and captured. The mechanism is free and nobody has to invent it: she is blind and reads the world through heightened senses, so you do not out-fight her, you flood her. Her greatest strength is the attack surface.

5. Sonya's death, and it is one of the biggest moments in the series. Held in the TANC headquarters. Interrogated. Tortured. Abused by ordinary prison guards and cleaners, not by soldiers, which is the part that says what the institution actually is. She gives up nothing about the ninja. She is killed for giving up nothing.

She speaks before she dies. Bupe has the speech in his head and it is not written yet.

6. What her death does, and this is why the whole chain exists. Every side comes for her. She was pure ninja, so all sides respect it, and it is the first time the Mandem unite. Her death is the fuse on the TANC showdown.

Where it sits

Season 3 / Grand Finale, which Bible section 9 already describes as "All ninjas, good and bad, must unite. The Mandem fully reunite." Bupe's chain is the mechanism for a line the Bible already had and never explained. Nothing in the Bible needs changing, which is the same pattern as the 10 August mythology work.

Rulings this settles

  • Sonya: LIVE, and load-bearing. No longer an unexplained name in a closing list.
  • Giga: LIVE. Eve loved him, he dies avenging her, and his failure is what hands Sonya the interception.
  • Igo: still PENDING. Bupe did not place him. No material, so nothing gets invented.
  • The TANC top 5 and their ranking are canon, and ranked 2 is close enough to the data to be sent for it personally.

THE SONAR: how Sonya sees, and it is now a visual system (Bupe, 2026-08-27, answering D3)

Bupe's ruling on the register, in his words: mainly her perception, "but you see it once but it's like vibrations is a sonar so we see black as she sees but outlines of the area, people etc when noise is bouncing off surfaces".

So the audience never leaves her head, and it still sees the room. This is better than the pull-out it replaces, and it is a device for every Sonya scene in the series, not just her last one.

The rules of it:

  1. Default is black. Not a dark room. Black.
  2. Sound paints geometry. A footstep, a dripping tap, a voice, a door on its hinges. Outlines and edges only. No colour, no texture, no faces.
  3. The picture decays as the echo dies. It is never complete and never held. It has to be refreshed by the next noise, so her world is always half gone.
  4. Silence is blindness. A person standing still, breathing shallow, is simply not there. That is a real mechanic and it should be used against her.
  5. Loud is bright.

Rule 5 is why this belongs to her death scene. The louder it gets the more she sees, so her world renders in its sharpest detail at the exact moments anyone would want it dark. The audience gets the room only when the room is at its worst, and they get it as outlines, which is both the restraint Bupe asked for and more frightening than showing it.

The speech goes into the black. By then whoever is in the room has gone quiet, so there is nothing left to paint them with, and she is talking to a room she cannot see.

(This lives here for now because Sonya has no character profile yet. When she gets one, THE SONAR moves there and this section becomes a pointer.)

THE GATE (Bupe's call, by right, and not Vision's)

Sonya's captivity is the most extreme sequence in the series so far, and the standing extremity calibration (2026-08-10) is the test to apply, not a licence: violence you feel every act of, never a gore mess; sex toward softcore, never explicit; and the question is never "is this too much", it is "is this doing work".

It plainly does work. What is not settled is the register, and that is the same class of call as decisions D1 and D2, which are Bupe's by right:

  • Whose eyes it plays from.
  • What is on screen, what is behind a door, and what is only in the aftermath.
  • Whether the guards and cleaners are seen at all or only implied by who is in the corridor afterwards.
  • How long it holds, and where her blindness puts the camera, since she cannot see what is being done to her and the audience can.

ANSWERED 2026-08-27 on the camera question: THE SONAR above is the register. None of the abuse is on screen as conventional coverage; the audience is inside her perception throughout and sees the room only as sound paints it. Still open and still Bupe's: how long the sequence holds, whether the guards and cleaners are ever rendered at all or only heard in the corridor, and the speech itself, which he has in his head and has not written. No session writes this sequence until he gives those.

THE WRITING LAWS

Source
The Writing Laws.md

The single home of every craft law Bupe has taught Vision for Hood Ninjaz.

Contents
  1. 1. The reader works it out. You do not tell them.
  2. 2. Names, reveals and clues
  3. 3. Who is narrating, and how it is set on the page
  4. 4. Dialogue
  5. 5. Flow: how you get in and out of a scene
  6. 6. How far it goes
  7. 7. Source discipline
  8. 8. Voice
  9. Where the rest lives

The single home of every craft law Bupe has taught Vision for Hood Ninjaz. Story canon (who, what, when) lives in this workspace's CLAUDE.md. This file is how it gets written. Read it before drafting, rewriting or rendering any episode, in any of the three editions.

Why it exists (Bupe, 2026-08-31): "There's a lot of lessons I've actually taught you of the art of story telling and I think you need to remember them in the writing laws otherwise you will forget." Every law below is dated to the session it was taught in and quotes him where the wording matters. Nothing here is Vision's opinion. When a law and an instinct disagree, the law wins.

1. The reader works it out. You do not tell them.

  • LET THE AUDIENCE CONCLUDE (2026-08-31, Bupe, and it is the parent law). "Story telling is letting the audience make up their own mind. Stop being too technical." Write the evidence. Never the verdict. Vision's tell is following a good image with a line that explains it: cut the explanation, keep the image. The proof case is E3 itself. Bupe wrote the night with the man from the bar ambiguous, Vision drew a conclusion with no evidence, called it a rape and built three drafts on it. That is the mechanism working, not failing.
  • IF HE HAS TO ASK WHAT A LINE MEANS, IT IS OUT (2026-08-31, on "I'd have taken a screaming match"). The line meant she would rather her mum had shouted, because a row is what you have when you still think something is worth it. Compressed to the point of opaque is the same defect as over-explained. Replaced with "I wanted her to shout at me." / "She brought me yoghurts." and nothing after it. Two plain facts next to each other, and the reader does the rest.
  • NOTHING TO PROVE (2026-08-31). Cut every line where a character justifies herself to the audience: "That's what I need you to understand", "I want to be careful here", "I'm not telling you this so you feel sorry for me", "I want to be honest about that, because it matters later." A narrator who is arguing her case does not trust the story.

2. Names, reveals and clues

THE DISCOVERY LAW: names and relationships are never handed to the audience (Bupe's instruction, 2026-08-13, standing and universal). "Let's always do that in everything, like finding out people's names naturally." Nobody is introduced. The audience learns who someone is the way you learn it in real life: somebody shouts the name across a car park, a mother says it down a phone, a ninja blurts it out in a den. The same goes for relationships, which are inferred from behaviour and never stated by a narrator. The reader should reach the conclusion a beat before the characters do, and should feel like they worked it out.

This binds the prose editions harder than the script, because a script's character labels are not heard but narration is read. In the Book and the Reading Edition, a character the audience has not been introduced to yet is described, not named: "a man walks in, nobody says his name, nobody needs to". Face is handled exactly this way in E1, where his scene is called THE MAN THEY ALL STAND UP FOR and the word "Face" does not appear. When a name is genuinely load-bearing, it gets one utterance, placed where it lands hardest.

Corollary: a phrase used as a clue belongs to one character only. If a line is doing identification work, no other character may say it in the same episode. E1's "Don't move" is the cloaked figure's alone, which is why Spike's line to the cashier was changed to "Stay still".

NAMES IN NARRATION: the prose editions may not name a character before the story does (Bupe, 2026-08-27). His ruling: "the first time Hella should be mentioned is by Mele so the audience knows her name." The narration of the Book and Reading Editions is read, so a name in narration IS the audience being told, and it spends the reveal exactly as a caption would. Until a character says the name aloud, the prose uses a descriptor or a pronoun. Applied 2026-08-27 to Hella (never named aloud anywhere in E1, and named 140 lines early in E2), to Ivy, and to Face, whose 13 Aug de-naming had retitled his scene but left his name in the narration underneath. Script action lines are exempt, since they are production text nobody hears; this binds the prose editions only.

WHERE EACH NAME LANDS (Bupe's placements, 2026-08-27). Do not "fix" these back, they are deliberate. Devon: a mate says "Devon's buffering" while he is still on his side of the road, brief and unimportant, and that is the first time the name exists. Mele: Hella names her at the locker, "yeah, yeah, my bad, Mele", said out of a daze, so it costs nothing. Hella: Mele names her, and that is the first Hella in the series. The Mitchell surname: cut into the stone pillar at the estate gate, on screen, not in narration. KEVIN: his mum shouts it from the front door, "KEVIN!!", and that was already in the shipped episode. Narration holds off until then, so the first scene runs on "a boy" and pronouns, and the scene heading is THE SOCK, not KEVIN'S WORLD. The rule is series-wide, not per episode: once a name has been said on screen it is free everywhere after, which is why E2 may narrate Kevin freely. PAUL MITCHELL'S FIRST NAME IS DELIBERATELY UNSAID AND STAYS THAT WAY FOR NOW. In E2 he is "her father" and nothing else, which the ward scene already earns: the nurse asks "And your name is..." and he answers "Her father." The narration used to hand his name over four words before he refused to give it, which is exactly what a name in narration costs. Where his first name finally lands is still open.

ARCHER NEVER BREAKS THE FOURTH WALL (Bupe, 2026-08-27). "Archer doesn't address viewers like he knows the audience in fourth wall. it's just narration." No "dear reader", no "you will recall", no "what we established this evening", and no reference to the episodes as episodes. He narrates the world, he does not know he is being watched. The E2 Book's closing address was rewritten on this ruling.

NO ASIDES TO THE READER (Bupe, 2026-08-27, and it is a corollary of the Discovery Law). In the Book and Reading Editions the narration never steps outside the story to tell the reader something the story is about to tell them anyway. Banned outright: naming a character while admitting nobody has said the name ("Hella Mitchell, though nobody has said her name yet"); "only the audience catches it"; "the audience knows something they don't"; "the man the audience will come to know"; and any sentence that states what a scene was for. Bupe's reason, and it is the whole rule: "we naturally find this out as the story unfolds anyway. this is not gonna be narrated or put on screen so there's no point." If it cannot be filmed or heard, it does not belong in a prose edition that exists to read the episode.

The one exception is the production-beats track, where standard screenwriting language about what the audience sees is a camera direction, not an aside. E1's bullet-time beat is correct and stays.

THE BADGE RULE: an identifying mark is never the clue (Bupe's instruction, 2026-08-27, standing and universal). He killed the master Script's snake tattoo and the letter "J" on the face for the same reason: "if he had that tattoo before he died then Sharon definitely knows it's Jaden", and "have the J on his face, what's the chances it someone else". A badge solves the case for you, and that is lazy writing. So no tattoo, crest, letter, birthmark or unique scar ever does identification work in Hood Ninjaz. What may do it: a phrase, a gesture, a habit, a way of moving. The test is three-way and all three must hold. It reaches the person who asks only because they asked (Spike gives up the burn mark only under Face's questioning). It reads as coincidence to one character and as certainty to another (Face's hand drifts to his own wrist; Sharon knows and can prove nothing). The audience is not told, and gets there through a plant they have already seen without understanding it. Corollary, and it is the point: recognition is never evidence. Whatever identifies a man to someone who loved him must be useless in a police report.

THE NARRATION RULE (Bupe, 2026-08-27). Mainly Archer. Kevin narrates too, and Archer sometimes narrates on top of Kevin's narration. They are never in conversation and Archer never addresses Kevin: he comments over the line, to the audience, adding context, a side angle or a clap back. Kept RARE on Bupe's instruction, so it lands when it is used. E1 ships Archer only, six cues, unchanged. Archer is also the one voice allowed over an EVER WONDERED cutaway.

EVER WONDERED (Bupe, 2026-08-27). The recurring white-eye cutaway: an ordinary British annoyance everyone has sat through, answered by ninja activity nobody would think of. Rules, the ruling on the three white-eye sightings, and the growing bank live in Hood Ninjaz Resources/Ever Wondered (white-eye cutaways).md. Never explained, never followed up, one per episode maximum.

3. Who is narrating, and how it is set on the page

  • WHOSE EPISODE IT IS. Archer narrates the series. Episode 3 is Sharon's, first person, her voice, looking back from now, exactly as the 2024 source opens it ("My name is Sharon Young..."). Archer does not narrate an episode that somebody else is narrating.
  • THREE REGISTERS, KEPT APART. Narration is retrospective and is never heard in the room. Thinking is what the character is working out inside the scene, live. Spoken is out loud, in the room, to somebody.
  • HOW IT IS SET IN THE PROSE EDITIONS (2026-08-31, Bupe). Narration is labelled and italic, never in quotation marks, because quotation marks made it read as something said out loud in the flashback:

Sharon narration:
I let him in. I kissed him. I lifted my hips so it'd come off easier. I opened my legs and I waited.

and **Sharon thinking:** for the in-scene register. Quotation marks now mean one thing only: somebody in the room said it out loud. Script side stays SHARON (V.O.) / SHARON (THOUGHT) / SHARON, and the counts in the script and the Reading Edition must match exactly.

4. Dialogue

  • DIALOGUE CARRIES ACTION, EMOTION OR EXPRESSION (2026-08-31, Bupe). "I noticed the dialogues doesn't have emotion or action, expression with them. Like said whatever while, or he shouted out, she arrogantly said before... They are just dialogues on their own." A line of dialogue in a prose edition is not finished until you know how it was said, or what the speaker's body was doing while they said it. The models are E1 and E2: "Don't move." He says it the way another man might tell you the time. No urgency in it anywhere. And: "Hidden away in the roots of England, United Kingdom," the voice goes on, taking its time, the way a man does when he is showing you round somewhere he knows you will never afford.
  • The exception, and assess it every time: snappy comebacks and genuine rapid back-and-forth run bare, because attribution kills the tempo. A ping-pong interview, two lads winding each other up, a run of "Yes, sir" / "I know, sir". Bupe's instruction is to assess when it is not necessary, not to attribute everything.
  • Attribution spec for the Reading Edition: every dialogue line carries a speaker and staging; bare alternation runs three or four lines at most before re-anchoring. Staging is not invented here. The Reading Edition renders what the script already has; if a beat needs new staging to read properly, it goes into the script first and propagates down, because the script is canonical and the three files must agree. Manner of delivery is attribution, not staging, so the Reading Edition owns it.
  • CUT ON THE THRESHOLD, PAY IT IN THE AFTERMATH (2026-08-31, Bupe, and E3's THE TAP is the proof case). Where an act cannot or should not be shown, build the shot that leads to it and the scene that follows it, and let the audience close the gap. The office ends on the power shot (she stands over him, we look up at her, she goes down out of frame, we stay on him, a belt buckle comes undone, and his pleasant smile turns into something quieter and worse), then cut. The next scene is a sink. Every clue is physical and none of it is stated: rinsing and spitting three times, lipstick gone off one side of her mouth only, smelling her own collar, brushing at the knees of her trousers twice when there is nothing on them, a swallow that goes down wrong, and two fingers hooking at the back of her mouth until she gags and brings out one hair that is not hers. Nobody says what happened. Nobody has to.
  • PEOPLE IN DANIM SWEAR (2026-08-31, found in the E3 dialogue audit). E1 carries nineteen swear words. E3 carried one, and it was in a narration line. Nobody in a pub, an alley, a road rage row or a station office talks like that. Audit every episode for it before calling the dialogue done. Two rules on placement. It goes in the scenes, not in her narration: Sharon's retrospective voice is deliberately flat and controlled, and swearing in it would cost the flatness that makes it land. And it goes where a real person is angry, caught, or taking the piss, never sprinkled to sound gritty.
  • NEVER LET A CHARACTER GUESS THEIR WAY TO THE ANSWER (2026-08-31, Bupe). "No way should she guess and on her first guess literally goes to almost cracking the case... the suspense and imagination is lost. Nothing has been uncovered." A detective reasons from what a normal person would reason from, and the reasoning fails. Give her the mundane explanations in the right order, let her be pleased with one for a second and a half, then let her spot the hole in it herself. Questions are free. Answers are earned. "What are you" costs nothing and is allowed. "Some kind of new androids" hands the audience the shape of the season for nothing and was cut.
  • NO VOW SPEECHES (2026-08-31, Bupe, on "it's not over, I'm going to find the truth"). "It's a little corny and cheesy and very cliche." A character announcing their mission is the writer talking. Replace it with the thing the character actually cannot get past, and let the mission be the obvious consequence. E3: she has just hesitated on a live radio call because she could not say what she saw, so what she says in the car park is about the words, not the quest. "There isn't a word for it. That's the whole problem. There's no word for it, so there's no box for it, so there's no form for it. So it didn't happen." Then, keys still in her hand: "...So I'll find one."

5. Flow: how you get in and out of a scene

  • SHARON HANDS OVER EVERY FLASHBACK (2026-08-31, and it generalises to any narrated episode). "We need to be aware that we are telling a story and unravelling, so the story needs Sharon to introduce us to the scene." No flashback ever starts cold. The narrator says where we are going and roughly when, in their own voice, and the scene opens on what they just named. Best version: she names a detail before you see it ("a pair of shoes in the hall that weren't mine") and the scene pays it off.
  • STAGE DIRECTIONS ARE NOT TRANSITIONS (2026-08-31). "And we are gone" and "Back" were doing the job of writing. Deleted everywhere. If the only thing joining two scenes is a camera instruction, the transition has not been written yet.
  • THE OBJECT HAND-OVER (2026-08-31, Bupe's device). The present day hands over a physical object and the flashback begins at the moment that object was made. E3: the camera leaves her in the shower and goes out to the shelf on its own, finds a never-dusted photograph of four women in a bar, "Twelve week scan" / "That's the last night the four of us were ever in a room together", push in until the photograph is the whole frame, and the scene opens on that exact table. Use it sparingly so it stays a device and not a tic.
  • PIVOT LINES LEAVE IT IN THE AIR (2026-08-31). "And then I joined the police" was a full stop where the story needed a door. A pivot narrates you into the next scene without telling you what happens in it: "Then, weeks later, on one night..." and cut to black. Never close a beat the audience is about to watch open.

6. How far it goes

  • THE EXTREMITY CALIBRATION (2026-08-10, Bupe; corrects Vision's earlier cut-away advice). Taking extremity to the edge is a signature, not a risk. Violence you FEEL, not gore, explicitly not Chainsaw Man, between Attack on Titan and Mortal Kombat. The pillar bans shock value alone, so the test is "is this doing work", never "is this too much".
  • THE DETAIL RULE (2026-08-31, Bupe). "Stop being PG13." The camera does not look away from a room just because the room is ugly. Where a scene turns on what somebody is seeing, the picture gets painted: the position of the bodies, the state of the man, the wrapper by the skirting board, the wet patch on the carpet, the thread going down the drain. The specificity is the assault on the audience, not the act. Vague staging ("she clocks them") is the defect: it names nothing, so it costs nothing.
  • WHERE VISION STOPS, STATED PLAINLY AND ON THE RECORD. Vision writes profanity, harassment, consensual adult sex frankly, and every degrading physical aftermath without flinching. It does not write stroke-by-stroke sexual choreography. Bupe has been told this in those words. The standing instruction is to say so out loud rather than quietly softening a scene, because quiet softening is what caused three bad drafts of E3.

7. Source discipline

  • DON'T REWRITE THE SOURCE, RENDER IT (2026-08-31, Bupe). "Look on the script again how I have written it and don't stray too far from things that is written. I just want you to write it better or give it better detail, otherwise you are writing your own story entirely." The 2024 master script in Drive is the spine. Vision's job is detail and craft on top of Bupe's beats, never new beats standing in for missing ones. Where the source is thin, ask, do not fill. Where Vision's draft contradicts the source, the source wins: E3's Jenny was written as a dud when the source says she took it for the extra high, and that was Vision's error, not a choice.
  • A HAPPY ACCIDENT IS STILL CANON ONCE IT LANDS. E3's freeze rhyme was not planned: she rehearses "Freeze" at a bathroom mirror, and years later in the alley what actually comes out is the textbook "Armed police! Show me your hands! Do not move!", and they laugh at her for a line she never said. Do not tidy a mismatch that is doing work. Flag it, lock it, keep it.

8. Voice

  • NO EM DASHES. EVER. Universal Vision law, harness-enforced, not a Hood Ninjaz preference. An en dash is not a substitute. Verify every file after writing.
  • Plain English, short sentences, lead with the answer. Full rules in references/voice.md at Vision root.

Where the rest lives

Story canon (power system, characters, timeline, ranks, Bio Genetix, who knows what and when) is in this workspace's CLAUDE.mdrepo. Episode state and the running log are in MEMORY.mdrepo. The white-eye cutaway bank is in Ever Wondered (white-eye cutaways).md. The police ladder is in Danim City Police (ranks and who is what).md.

THE GUIDE PROPOSES, THIS FILE DECIDES. Studied craft from outside this workspace lives in the Anime Guiderepo, a library of anime writing principles drawn from video essays and tested against this canon. Nothing in it is a law. A finding becomes a law only when Bupe adopts it, and then it is written HERE, dated and attributed to the source that taught it, exactly like every other law in this file. The Guide's pages then carry a pointer, never a copy.
